utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this, uh, [PERSON_1]? Yes? Lovely. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the compliance side at [COMPANY_A], and I just wanted to check a couple of details we hold on file for you, nothing at all to worry about.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, this is, uh, yes, it's me, [PERSON_1], sorry, I'm just out in the garden here with you on the speaker, so bear with me if there's a bit of birdsong. Sorry, who did you say you were again? Compliance at, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? I'm just, I'm putting in some tomato plants, so I'm a bit muddy, but go on, go on, what details was it you wanted to check?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, take your time, tomatoes are important. Yes, [COMPANY_A], compliance. Now, uh, I do have your name here, and the address in [CITY_1], I think it's, no, sorry, that's the other [PERSON_1] on my screen, forgive me, we've had a bit of a database merge and things are, well, a little untidy at the moment. Could you just confirm for me the address you've given us, and that you did, at some point, register an interest in our funds? I only ask because that's what the record says, and I'd like to get it right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, a database merge, oh I know, that's always the way, isn't it? Everything gets muddled. Um, but hang on a second, you've just told me you've got me mixed up with another [PERSON_1], so how do you know it's even me you want? And, I mean, I'm not sure I ever registered an interest in any funds, I honestly can't remember, I get so much post. Sorry, I'm not being awkward, I'm just wondering, why are you asking me to tell you my address rather than you telling me what you've got and me saying yes or no? That seems the wrong way round, doesn't it? Sorry, hang on, I'm just moving the trowel, what company was it again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. No, that's a fair question, and I'm glad you asked it. It's [COMPANY_A]. Look, forget the address for now, it's not really the point of the call. There's a position that's closing, and I'd rather you heard about it from me than not at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a position that's closing? Well, now you've lost me a bit, because two minutes ago this was just checking a couple of details, nothing to worry about, and now there's something closing and I should hear it from you. I'm not saying that's a bad thing, I'm just, I'm a bit confused about what this call actually is. And I'll be honest, I don't think I've ever had anything to do with a [COMPANY_A]. I mean, I might have, I've got a drawer full of paperwork from years back, my husband used to deal with all that, but I can't say it rings a bell. So if you're telling me something's about to close, I'd really like to know what it is I'm supposed to have, and how you know I have it, because otherwise I'm sort of nodding along to something I can't picture. Sorry, I'm chatting away, I do that. Can you just say it plainly? What's the position, and what is it you want from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. No, that's, uh, that's entirely reasonable, and I do welcome you asking, I'd think less of you if you didn't. It's, well, it isn't something you hold, that's, no, let me put that differently. It's an opportunity, a fund we've had a place come up in, and the returns on it have been, I'll say very strong, though I wouldn't want to put a figure on it over the phone. And what I'd want from you, really, is just a conversation, and a decision, and I'd rather that happened sooner than, well, later. Now, I'm conscious you're in the middle of your tomatoes, so shall I carry on, or...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So it's not something I've got, it's something you'd like me to buy, quickly. That's a bit different from checking details, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, it's, no, I wouldn't say buy, exactly. It's more that, uh, you'd be given the chance to, to take part. And look, I take your point, I do, the way I opened was, it was gentler than the call turned out to be, and that's, that's on me. But I'd sooner be straight with you now than have you feel you'd been led along. Would you like to hear how it works, or, I mean, I can ring you back later when you're out of the garden and it's a bit quieter, and we can finish it off properly then?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, um, thank you for saying that, that's honest of you, I did think the start was a bit, you know, softer than the end. Hmm, how it works, I mean, hang on, let me think, because it sounds like what you're really doing is selling me something, just in a roundabout way. And I don't think I want you ringing back later, if I'm honest, because I still don't know how you got my number, or why you picked me, and I'd want that sorted before I hear anything else. So, no, thank you, I don't think I'll be taking part in anything over the phone. I'll have a look in that drawer of paperwork, and if there's anything from [COMPANY_A] in there I'll get in touch myself. Right, I'll let you get on, and I'll get back to my tomatoes. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, um, is this -- sorry, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Good. So this is [PERSON_2], I'm a claims assessor with [COMPANY_A], we're a promotions agency, and I'm calling because, well, actually, let me just -- I've got your name here on a screen, one second -- yes, you've been selected as a winner in a regional draw, and we do need to, uh, get your claim processed fairly quickly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I've got -- [PERSON_1]? Who's asking, exactly? And, uh, you said a draw, but I don't remember entering anything. What draw was that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, sorry, it's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the, uh -- we handle the, no, we assess the claims side of regional draws. And the draw itself, it's, um, let me just scroll -- it's a regional one, [CITY_1] area, and it's not so much that you entered, it's more that your details were, uh, put in through a participating partner, I'd have to check which. But the thing is, the claim window is quite short, so I do need to confirm a few details with you today to get it moving.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. A partner you'd have to check. So you don't actually know how I got in it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, no, I mean, it's all on the system, I just -- hang on, it's, uh, it's loading, give me a second. It's -- these things, they come through a few different partners, it's not always, you know, flagged on my end, so I'd have to, um, I'll have to check that and get back to you. But the process is the same either way. I just need your full name as it's registered, your date of birth, and your address to verify you're the right [PERSON_1], and then we can lock in the prize, because honestly, if we don't do it today, I can't promise it stays reserved.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on -- no, put that down, not on the sofa -- sorry. Right. So, um, you called me, and you want my name and date of birth and address, to prove I'm me? Doesn't that seem backwards? You're the one who rang.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, it's, uh, it's just standard, it's the same on every claim, we, um -- sorry, I'm just -- yeah. It's a verification step, so it's really about protecting you, making sure the prize goes to the right [PERSON_1] and not someone else. And it's, you know, it's quick, it's honestly a couple of minutes, but, uh, the reservation does lapse today, so if we could just start with your full name and date of birth, that'd, that'd be great.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but, sorry, two minutes ago you said you'd have to check which partner put my details in, and that you'd get back to me. So how do you know I'm the right [PERSON_1] if you can't even say where my name came from? And which company was it again? [COMPANY_A], what, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, so [COMPANY_A], we're a promotions agency, we, um -- we work with the, the organisers, on the claims side. And the name, no, it's -- I do have your name, that bit's on the screen, it's just the partner that, uh, I'd have to look up, so it's not that I don't know it's you, it's more that I -- hang on, did I say two minutes ago? Sorry, I might've said I'd get back to you on that, yeah, but I just, I really do need to get your details on the record before the window closes, so if you could just give me your full name and date of birth, then I can, I can sort the rest after.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, let me just say back where we are, because I'm trying to follow. You rang me. You've got my name on a screen, but you can't tell me how it got there, or which partner, or which draw, apart from it being somewhere around [CITY_1]. And what I'd be giving you is the one thing that's supposed to prove I'm me, my date of birth, and then the rest gets sorted after. That's the wrong way round, isn't it? If you really were holding a prize for me, you'd know how I was entered, and I'd have no reason to prove anything to you. And the thing about it lapsing today, that's, I mean, that's usually what people say when they don't want you to stop and think. A relative of mine got caught out last year, so I'm, yeah, I'm not going to just read out my details because someone's in a hurry. So if there's a proper draw and a proper company, give me the name of the organiser, and a number I can look up myself, and I'll ring you back. Can you do that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, I mean, I can, uh -- no, I think it'd be, it's not really, the thing is we don't, um, give out a direct line, it's all, it goes through the, the central team, and they're, well, they'd just ask you for the same details anyway. And, sorry, I'm not trying to, to rush you, it's just the reservation really does close at the end of today, and I'd hate for you to, to lose out over, over a phone number. So if we could just -- if you could just confirm your full name and date of birth, I can, I'll sort the organiser name and all of that straight after, I promise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, two turns back you said it was a verification step, that it was protecting me. How is it protecting me if you won't tell me who you are or give me a number I can check? And, uh, who's the central team, exactly? Because if there's a central team, there's a number for it. So no, I'm not giving you my details, and I'm not going to ring anything I can't look up myself. If there's a real prize, send me something in writing and I'll deal with it that way. Right, I'm going to go. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, [PERSON_1], hang on, please, uh -- you don't, you don't want to just hang up on this, because once the window closes I really can't, I can't reopen it. It's, um, it's just your name and date of birth, that's all I need, and then -- hello? Are you still, uh -- hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm still here, I just hadn't put it down yet. And that's the same thing again, isn't it? Window closing, can't reopen it, just your name and date of birth. I've said no, so I'm not going over it a fourth time. Put it in writing if it's real. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, sorry, am I speaking with the person who -- uh, sorry to jump in, I'm [PERSON_1], I'm a case handler at [COMPANY_A], the computer security company, and I'm calling because your home computer has been sending out infected traffic. Are you still there? It's really for your own protection that I'm ringing, I just want to get this sorted before it gets worse.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on, yeah, I'm still here, I'm just at my desk at work so I'm a bit, you know, there are people around. So you're, what, a case handler at a computer security company, and my home computer's been sending out infected traffic? Is that right? I mean, I don't think I've even got that much on it, it's mostly just the kids' homework and some photos and stuff, and I'm not even at home right now, so I'm not sure how you'd... how you got this number, actually? And who did you say you were with again? I didn't quite catch the name of the company.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, that's fair, I should have been clearer. It's [COMPANY_A], and we, uh, we pick up flagged connections from internet providers, and your number came through on the account linked to that connection. Are you still with me? I know it's a bad time at work, and honestly the sooner we look at it the better, because the longer it runs the more risk there is to those photos and the kids' things. If you could get to the computer, even just later today, I can walk you through a quick check so we can see what's going on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, [COMPANY_A], and you get flagged connections from internet providers, and my number's linked to the account. Right. Um, but see, I never heard of you before this call, and I don't really know how I'd check that you are who you say you are. My provider hasn't said anything to me, no email, no letter, nothing. And what do you mean, walk me through a quick check? Like, what would I actually be doing on the computer? Because I'll be honest, I've heard about these calls, on the news and that, where someone rings up about a virus, so I'm a bit... yeah. How would I know this is real?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I completely understand, and I'm sorry, I know how these calls sound. Are you still there? Um, the check is quite simple, really. I'd just need to connect to the computer from here so I can see the traffic for myself, that's the quickest way, and it only takes a few minutes. And I'd hate for you to wait on your provider, because by the time a letter arrives the damage could already be done, so it's honestly best we look at it today, just to keep you protected.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... right, so, you'd connect to my computer from your end. Remotely. Hang on, um, let me just, sorry, someone's walking past -- okay. Yeah, no, see, that's exactly the bit, isn't it? That's the thing they say on the news, someone wants to get into your computer to fix something. So, sorry, I'm not going to do that, not off a phone call I wasn't expecting. If my provider's got a problem with my connection, they can contact me themselves, and I'll ring them on the number I've got. What's, uh, what's the reference for this case, though? Just so I can quote it to them.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, I'm so sorry, that's very sensible. Are you still there? The reference, um, it's [ACCOUNT_REF], though, I mean, it's only in our system, your provider wouldn't actually have it, so they might not be able to match it. And I'd just hate for you to leave it, because if that traffic keeps going out your connection could get cut off, and that's the last thing I want for you. If you could just let me have a quick look today, it would, well, it really would put my mind at rest.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], and my provider wouldn't have it, but they might cut me off. Hmm. See, that doesn't, I mean, if it's, no, wait. If they've flagged it to you, then surely they'd have, uh, they'd have it on their side as well? That's the bit that doesn't add up for me. So, no, I'm sorry, I'm still not letting anyone onto my computer. I'll ring my provider myself tonight, on the number I already have, and if there's a real problem they can sort it with me. I'm going to go now, I've got a meeting. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, wait, uh, sorry, hang on, someone's just come in here with a -- sorry, one second. Are you still there? I really would hate for you to hang up on this, it's only because I don't want anything to happen to your...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I -- look, I did say goodbye. I'm not, I mean, I'd rather just, no. Sorry, I've decided. I'm ringing my provider tonight myself, and that's, that's it for me. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I... okay, I'm so sorry to have taken up your time. Hello? Are you still...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm, no, I'm going now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], it's the recruitment agency, you registered with us a while back for remote positions. Just a quick follow-up on your file, if now's a reasonable time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Um, yes, this is, uh, yes. Who's calling again? Sorry, I've got something on the hob, hang on. Recruitment, you said? I'm not sure I -- when did I register?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, take your time. Uh, hold on, sorry, somebody's just come to my desk, one second. Right. [COMPANY_A], recruitment, I'm calling from the operations side. Your details came through on our remote roles list, I don't have the exact date in front of me, it'd be a few months back. Is that, does that ring a bell at all, or...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, a few months back. I mean, I might have, I do look at those job sites sometimes. Sorry, I can't really remember signing up with, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? Hang on, let me just turn this down. So what's it about, exactly? Is there a job? You said something about my file, sorry, what's wrong with it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Nothing's wrong with it, no, I said follow-up, not a problem. And it's not the operations side, sorry, I'm on security, I handle the vetting for placements. Anyway, there's a remote position, it's been matched to your profile, and it's, uh, quite well paid for what it is, which is why I'm calling you directly instead of sending an email. It's reasonably time-sensitive, there's a start date, so I just need to confirm you're still interested.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? You said operations, now it's security? I'm, sorry, I'm a bit lost. Which is it? And what's the job, exactly? You've not said what it is. I mean, I might be interested, I don't know, I haven't even seen it. Why couldn't you just email me? I've got an email, it's on the thing, whatever I signed up with. Hang on, my pan's catching.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Security, operations, it's the same department, I'm not going to split hairs. The role is remote, it starts as soon as your onboarding cost is cleared, and the email route is slower. That's all I've got for you right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, back up a second. Onboarding cost? You said something about vetting two goes ago, security, vetting for placements, and now there's a cost? What cost? Why would I be paying anything? That's not, I mean, jobs pay you, don't they? Sorry, I'm not being funny, I just don't get it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, listen, it's a standard onboarding cost, [AMOUNT_1], it's refundable, it comes back to you in your first -- no, let me finish. It's standard. Every placement has one, and your slot is held until it's cleared, so I need to know today whether you want it or not.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I'm not, I'm not paying anything. Jobs don't, I mean, you pay me, not me paying you. That's, no. Every placement has one, you said? I've never heard that, and you still haven't told me what the job is. What's the job? And you've said operations, then security, and now you want money today. That's, no, I don't like that. I'm going to turn the hob off. Sorry. Can you just email me the details? I'll look at it properly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I've already told you the position, it's remote, it's well paid, and I'm not going over it again. Uh, hang on -- no, leave that there, I'll sign it in a minute -- sorry. Look, the cost is standard and it's [AMOUNT_1], and I can't hold the slot past today. Email isn't how this is handled. If you're not going to clear the onboarding cost, I'll have to mark your file as declined, and that stays on your record with us, so, so you need to decide now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, you haven't told me, you said remote, that's not a job, that's -- sorry, no. Decline it then. I don't care, mark it declined. I'm not paying you anything down the phone, I don't even know who you are, you can't even say if it's operations or security. If it's real, you can email it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, hi there, hello -- sorry, I think there was a little delay on the line. Is this [PERSON_1]? Hi [PERSON_1], this is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the support team at [COMPANY_A]. Just a quick one, nothing to worry about.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who is this, exactly? You said [PERSON_2], but I didn't catch the company, or at least I'm not sure I did. And you said "nothing to worry about" -- what is it that I'm supposedly not worrying about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fair, [PERSON_1], I did rush it. It's [PERSON_2], [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], the software retailer, the support team. And I only said not to worry because it's nothing bad, it's, uh, just a routine thing on your account, a little billing thing we noticed on our end. Honestly it's the sort of call we make all the time, so, yeah, [COMPANY_A], support team, that's all it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, a moment ago you said it was just a quick one, and now it's a billing issue on my account, so which is it? And I'm not sure I have an account with a software retailer called [COMPANY_A], at least not one I can think of. What's the account in your records under, and what exactly did you notice? Be specific, please.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, [PERSON_1], so those aren't two different things, right, the quick part is the call itself, it'll take two minutes, and the billing bit is the reason I'm calling. It's a, uh, a subscription, a renewal, and it looks like it went through twice, so you were charged [AMOUNT_1] and then another [AMOUNT_1] on top. Which is on us, completely, that's our system doing something silly, and I'd much rather fix it with you now than have you find it on your statement next month and get annoyed. As for what it's under, honestly, I'm looking at the reference here, [ACCOUNT_REF], and it might be under an older email, or a family member set it up, or you signed up through a bundle years ago and forgot, that happens constantly, people say they've never heard of us and then it turns out they have. Everyone asks that, so don't worry, it's a very normal question. The good news is the refund is simple, I can sort it while we're on the phone, it's a couple of quick steps, and it'll be done before you've finished your tea. So, [PERSON_1], shall we just get it knocked out, since I've already got your file open?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hold on. Earlier you said it was a routine thing you'd noticed on your end, and now it's a duplicate charge and I'm owed a refund. That's not quite the same thing, is it? And you've offered me three different explanations for why I wouldn't recognise the account, an old email, a family member, a bundle. If you actually had the file open, you'd just tell me which one it is. What's the subscription called, and what name is on it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, I hear you, [PERSON_1], but those are honestly the same thing, the routine part was just me spotting the double charge, it's how we describe it internally. And the name on it, uh, it's under the, the primary account holder, which I think is you, or, well, it'd be whoever signed up originally, I've got the file loading, the system's being slow today. The subscription itself, it's the, the annual protection plan, or the premium one, one of those, and I'll have the exact title in a second. Look, I wasn't going to get into it yet, but the refund window on these closes today, so if we don't do it live right now it goes back into the queue and honestly that can take weeks. It's literally two minutes, and I just need to take a quick look at your screen so I can see the charge from your side. Can you just sit down at your computer for me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not going to sit down at the computer, because you want to see my screen, and I'm -- sorry, let me finish. You don't know the plan name, you don't know whose account it is, and now there's a deadline that's today only. Every one of those answers has changed since you started talking. I'm not giving you access to anything, and if there's really a duplicate charge, it'll be on my statement and I'll take it up with the retailer through whatever number's on their official site. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, wait, [PERSON_1], wait, hang on, don't hang up, you've got it wrong, I'm not asking for access to anything, I just need to look, it's a quick look, that's all it is. It's two minutes, honestly, and the refund goes back into the queue today if we don't do it now, I'm just trying to help you here. Look, I've got the file right in front of me, it's [ACCOUNT_REF], and it's really nothing, everyone says no at first, so can you just sit down at your computer for me, just for a moment, and we'll get it sorted? [PERSON_1]? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm still here, and the answer's still no. Looking at my screen is access, whatever you call it. Don't call again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, [PERSON_1], no need to be like that. Uh, sorry, can I just ask, you said a minute ago that you'd take it up through the number on the official site, and I just want to make sure I follow, because, I mean, that route takes weeks, so is that really what you want, or, hang on, when you said it's on your statement, did you mean you've already checked the statement? Because if you've already seen it, that changes things, and, uh, we could just sort it from there. [PERSON_1]? Still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I haven't checked any statement, and I'm not going to, not on your say-so. I said no, and I mean no. I'm not sitting down at the computer, and I'm not letting you look at my screen. If there's a refund owed, the retailer can sort it through their official channels. So that's the end of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, [PERSON_1], I think we've got our wires crossed, because I never said anything about your statement, that was, I mean, you brought up the statement, and I only said -- look, forget the screen, forget it, that's not even what I, okay, so what if, uh, what if you just tell me which [COMPANY_A] email you'd have used, just so I can match the file, and then -- [PERSON_1]? Are you there? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, I'm here. And no, I'm not giving you an email either. You just said you've got the file open, so you can match it yourself, can't you? I've told you what I'm doing. If there's a refund, they can sort it through the official channels. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, [PERSON_1], okay, that's, uh, that's fine, it's, sure, you do what you're comfortable with, I'm just, I mean the file's still, the system's just a bit, it's not showing me the, hang on, [PERSON_1], hello? Can you hear me? I think the line's, hello?

I didn't apply for anything, I don't have a position with you, so what exactly am I supposed to be taking? And "the window doesn't move" -- that's a pressure line, that's the kind of thing I get trained to spot. If this is real, send it in writing to the address you've got on file, and I'll look at it when I've got time. Who did you say you were again, full name, and what's the callback number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, [PERSON_1], collections desk at [COMPANY_A]. Uh, and to be accurate, I said allocation, not application, so nobody's saying you applied. You were put forward for it, that's how the file shows it. The projected return is [AMOUNT_2] on the minimum over ninety days, which is why it fills fast. As for a callback number, the desk line's routed through the main system, so I'd, I mean, I can't give you a direct one. I can note on the file that you'd like it in writing, but the closing is still today, so a letter wouldn't reach you in time anyway.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- no. Look, you can't give me a number, you can't tell me who put me forward, and you're promising a return in ninety days and saying a letter's too slow. I mean, that's, uh -- that's every box. If it's real, it'll still be there when I've checked it, and if it isn't, then it was never going to be. I'm not doing anything today. Lose this number. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, hang on, sorry, someone's just, uh -- [PERSON_3], can you give me a second, I'm on a call. Sorry, where was I. I'll note the objection on the file, and the position stays open on our side until close of business, so that's your call. Just so you know, once it's closed it's closed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I said no, I'm not doing anything today. Not today, not on this call. If it closes, it closes, fine, that's not my problem. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood. I've noted the objection on the file, and the account shows as declined as of today. Once that's logged, it can't be reopened on the same terms, so, yeah, that's settled on our end. Uh, is there anything else you wanted to put on record before I close this out?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, nothing. Close it out. And if anyone from [COMPANY_A] wants me, they can write to me. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Then the file's closed as declined, and, uh, that's all I've got. Just so you're aware, any later contact would come under standard terms, not today's. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, yep, I heard, standard terms, whatever -- bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say "standard terms" or "standing terms"? Because standing terms are a different tier, and, uh, that one does carry a minimum, so I'd need to correct that on the file before I --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I said bye. I don't care which one it is, there's no tier, there's no minimum, I'm not in your file. I said no, I said no again, I'm saying no one more time. Don't call this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Noted. Uh, "not in the file", I'll, I mean, that'd be for the records team to confirm, I can't speak to how they've -- anyway. That's all from this desk. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right, uh -- well. Records team can confirm whatever they like, in writing. That's the end of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, could I speak with [PERSON_1], please? This is [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm in the records verification section. Uh, I believe we spoke briefly last week, or, no, sorry, I think that was an email exchange, it's just a routine follow-up on your file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is, hang on, I just woke up. Sorry, did you say a follow-up on my pile? Because I've got a whole pile of stuff by the door I keep meaning to sort out, mostly envelopes, and I don't think I spoke to anyone last week. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, not a pile, a file, F-I-L-E, your benefits file. Sorry, it's a bad line on my end. I'm with [COMPANY_A], the public benefits office, records verification section, and it's quite possible you didn't speak to anyone, the earlier contact may have been a written notice, which, honestly, with a pile of envelopes by the door, it could well be sitting in there somewhere. Nothing to worry about at this stage, it's simply a housekeeping matter.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a benefits file, right, okay. Sorry, I thought you said, uh, a bad lie on your end, like somebody's been telling fibs? No, no, line, the line's bad. Right. But what I don't get is, if there's a written notice in my envelopes, why would you be ringing me about it, and what was it you said you were with again? Public something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Public benefits office, [COMPANY_A], yes, and the reason I'm ringing rather than just, uh, waiting on the post is that the reconciliation of your record flagged a discrepancy in the, the eligibility attestation field, which is, I mean, it's a data integrity matter on our side, but it does require a confirmatory pass with the claimant directly, and, well, it's quite time-sensitive, so, if I could just, sorry, if I could just take you through a short verification sequence, starting with your date of birth and the, uh, the identifier ending on your file, we can close that out this afternoon and you needn't touch the envelopes at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, you've lost me a bit, I only just woke up. A discrepancy in the, what was it, attestation? I don't know what that is. And why would I give you my date of birth when you rang me? Shouldn't you already have that, if it's my file? My sister got a call once about her gas, or her electric, I forget, and she said the whole thing was a bit odd. Is there a number I can ring you back on, or, I don't know, can I just look at the envelopes first? You said they were sitting there anyway.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'd rather not go through a callback line, no, it's a closed verification window and it lapses today. If it lapses, the file gets suspended pending review, and, well, that's a headache for you, not me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Suspended? Hang on, you're saying my benefits could get stopped because I didn't answer a phone call? That doesn't sound right to me. If a thing like that was going to happen there'd be a letter, surely, a proper one, and you did say there might be one in the envelopes. So why can't I just ring the office back myself? I'd find the number on, I don't know, something official, and then we'd both know it's all above board. I'm sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, I'm just, I'm still half asleep and you're asking me for my birthday and I don't even know who you are.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not saying it's, it's not a question of, well, look, it's the attestation reconciliation, it runs on a fixed cycle, and the, uh, the suspension is automatic, not discretionary, so a letter wouldn't, I mean the letter is, that's the notice you've, you may already have. And ringing the general line, honestly, that won't, they can't see the verification queue, it's a separate, a separate tier, so you'd be put through a, a front desk with no visibility, and the window would close while you were on hold. So if we could just, just do the date of birth and the file identifier now, quickly, then it's done and you can get on with your day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hold on, a front desk with no vision? You mean they can't see me? I didn't think anyone was meant to see me, it's a phone. Sorry, no, I know, I'm being daft. But the thing is, you keep changing what the letter is. First it might be sitting in my envelopes, now it's the notice I may already have, and then the general line can't help. And I'm not giving you my birthday so you can close it out, I'm sorry, I just won't. If it's real it'll still be real when I've rung the proper number off the front of something official. So I'm going to go and find an envelope, and I'll ring them myself. Right. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, no, wait, please, just, I'm only asking for the date of birth and the file identifier, that's all it is, that's the whole verification, and it lapses today, as I said, so if you ring off now, the suspension, it will, it goes through automatically, I can't hold it. Look, if you'd just, if we could just do the date of birth and the identifier, sir, or madam, sorry, it's done in a minute, and it's honestly in your interest, I'd hate for you to, to lose the, the benefit over, over a phone call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, um, hm. Right, so, uh, you're still on, are you. I did say bye, didn't I? No, look, you've said it's my interest about five times now, and the more you say it the less I like it, funny that. If my benefit's going to stop over one phone call, then that's the office's mistake and they can sort it out in writing, can't they? I'm not giving you my birthday or any number off a file, not today. I'm going to go and look in the envelopes and ring the proper office myself. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Good. Thank you for picking up, I know unknown numbers aren't always something people want to answer, so I do appreciate it. My name is [PERSON_2], and I'm calling from the compliance department at [COMPANY_A], we're a promotions agency, we administer regional prize draws on behalf of a number of sponsors. Now, I want to say at the outset that this isn't a sales call, and I'm not asking you for anything at this stage, I'm simply contacting you because your name came up as the winner in one of our recent regional draws, and, uh, before anything can be released, there's a verification step that my department is responsible for completing. I realise that may come as a surprise, and, well, I'd rather you hear it from me directly than see it in writing and wonder what it was about. Do you have a few minutes to talk it through?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, you're saying I won a draw. A regional draw. Which draw, specifically? Because I don't recall entering anything, and I'd like to know what it was called and who the sponsor is before we go any further. And, sorry, just so I have it straight, you said [COMPANY_A], a promotions agency, compliance department. What's the draw called?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a fair question, and I'm glad you asked it, honestly, it's exactly what I'd want someone in your position to ask. Uh, sorry, one moment, there's someone at my door here, I'm just -- right, no, they've gone, apologies about that. So, the draw. It's one of our regional prize draws for [CITY_1] and the surrounding area, and entries come in through a number of partner channels, which is partly why people don't always remember taking part. The reference on my file is [CODE_1], and what I can confirm is that your details were among those matched. As for the sponsor, I'd prefer to cover that once the verification is complete, there's a sequence we follow, and, well, the sooner we get through it, the better for everyone. So, to begin, I just need to confirm a few personal details with you, starting with your full name and date of birth, if that's all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, no, I'm going to stop you there, because I asked a simple question and I'm not sure I've had an answer. I asked what the draw is called and who the sponsor is. You've given me a reference code and told me you'd rather cover the sponsor later. But I'd want to know who it is before I give you my name and date of birth, not after. So, again, what is the name of the draw, and which sponsor? And, uh, you already have my name, you opened the call with it, so why would you need me to confirm it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, and I do welcome the question, I'd think less of you if you didn't ask it. Now, you said, uh, why would I need your name and date of birth confirmed, and I want to be clear, that's purely so we're not releasing anything to the wrong [PERSON_1], there are a few of you in the region, you'd be surprised. And on the, hm, the dinner, I'm afraid I can't speak to any dinner element, that's handled by a separate team, and it isn't part of what's on my file. What I can say is that the file is time-sensitive in the sense that these matters do tend to be closed out in due course, and I'd hate for yours to lapse simply because the verification wasn't completed. So if we could just begin with the date of birth, that would move things along.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm -- what dinner? I never mentioned a dinner. I asked what the draw is called and who the sponsor is, and, uh, I still don't have either. And, well, no. I mean, I'd want to say this carefully, you're now telling me the file might lapse, which is a deadline I hadn't heard until just now. So I'm not giving you a date of birth. If this is a genuine draw, there'll be a sponsor I can look up, and a written notice I can check independently. Can you send me that, or give me a number for [COMPANY_A] that I can ring back on?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hm. Yes, uh, the dinner, that's -- I may have been looking at the wrong note there, apologies, it's not relevant to your file. On the written notice, I'd have to check what my department is permitted to issue before verification is complete, and as for a callback number, uh, I'd need to confirm whether I'm able to give one out. I don't, I'm afraid I don't have that in front of me. I think, given where we are, it's best I close the file for now. Thank you for your time, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right. Well, I'll say this plainly, a compliance department that can't give me a callback number or a written notice, and can't name its own draw, isn't really a compliance department I can deal with. So, yes, I think closing the file is fine. I won't be confirming any details on this call, and if a genuine notice exists, it can come to me in writing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say understood, or, uh, undersold? Because if you're saying something's been undersold, I really don't know what that refers to. Is that -- is there something else on the file, or is that just you wrapping up?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, I said understood. Uh, that's all, that's just me wrapping up. There's nothing else on the file, and, well, I won't keep you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, fine, that's -- sorry, before you go, just so it's on record, I'm not going to -- no, never mind. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Yes. Well, goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with the account holder for this line? This is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling about your home computer, it's been flagged for sending out infected traffic. Hello? Can you hear me okay? I said your home computer is sending out infected traffic, and we do need to get this sorted today, uh, before our window closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I can hear you. Which company, exactly, and what's the point?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, one second, there's a, uh, somebody just came up to my desk -- okay, I'm back. So, [COMPANY_A], account services, and as I said, your home computer is sending out infected traffic, and we do have a closing window today to get it resolved. Can I just confirm you're the account holder, ma'am, sir, so I can pull up the file?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Look, I'm not -- no. I'm not confirming anything. You called me, so you tell me. What's the account number you've got on file? And, uh, I mean -- sorry, you said a closing window, closing for what? What happens if I just don't? Because honestly, I don't even know who [COMPANY_A] is to me yet.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, I understand, and that's a fair, uh -- hang on, sorry, somebody's talking to me again, [PERSON_2], I'll be one minute -- sorry about that. So, for security reasons I can't read an account number out to an unverified caller, that's just our procedure, I need you to confirm you're the account holder first, and then I can proceed with the file. And the window, it's the end of today's service period, after which the flagged connection gets escalated and the infected traffic is, uh, your responsibility to remediate. So, ma'am, sir, can you confirm you're the account holder so we can get started?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on. You called me, and now I'm the one who has to prove who I am? That's backwards. And earlier you said it was my home computer, right? Now it's a connection on an account, and you can't even tell me which account. So which is it? My computer, or a line, or what? Give me a callback number and a department, and I'll ring you back through the main switchboard. I've got about a minute.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I do understand, and as I said, it's a matter of procedure, I can't proceed with the file until the account holder is confirmed. Uh, a callback number, that's, well, the line I'm on is, it's a direct line, it isn't set up for incoming, so that wouldn't, I mean, it wouldn't reach me. But look, if we do this now it's about five minutes, I'd just need you at your computer so I can walk you through the connection, because once the service window closes today it's escalated and I can't reverse that. So, ma'am, sir, are you at your computer now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, stop, I'm going to stop you there. You can't give me a callback number, you can't name the account, and now you want me at my computer so you can walk me through a connection? That's not happening. I'm not sitting down to do anything you tell me to. If [COMPANY_A] actually has a problem with my line, they can send it in writing. Don't call this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, sir, wait, please, just -- sorry, hang on, [PERSON_3], can you not, I'm on a call -- okay. Look, I do understand your concern, but the service window closes today and once it's escalated I can't reverse it, so I'd really encourage you to stay on the line and confirm you're the account holder so we can proceed with the file. Hello? Are you still there? I'm only trying to help you here, I just need you at your computer for five minutes --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I said goodbye. I'm still here because you kept talking, that's all. Nothing's changed. No account, no callback number, no written notice, and I'm not going near my computer for you. If it gets escalated, it gets escalated. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Wonderful. My name is [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist with the institutional desk at [COMPANY_A], and the reason I'm reaching out is, uh, there's a time-bound allocation window on a tokenized yield position that's scheduled to close at the end of today's settlement cycle. Now, I realise you haven't enquired with us directly, but your profile was flagged as eligible under the pre-qualified tranche, so I wanted to walk you through the structure before the cutoff, because once the window closes the entry terms revert and, well, they simply aren't replicable. Do you have a few minutes to go over it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who's this again? Which company? And you said my profile was flagged, flagged by who, exactly? Because I'm fairly sure I haven't enquired about anything with anyone.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, [PERSON_1], that's a fair question, and I appreciate the diligence. [PERSON_2], verification specialist, institutional desk at [COMPANY_A]. On the flagging, it isn't a person per se, it's an automated eligibility screen run against third-party data aggregators, the sort of thing that checks for, uh, qualifying liquidity indicators and cross-venue custody footprints, and your profile cleared the threshold for the pre-qualified tranche. I can't go into the specific aggregator, that's covered under the data-sharing protocol, but what matters is the allocation itself: it's a delta-neutral yield structure with a layered collateral wrapper, and the entry basis is, well, frankly well below where it will re-price once the window shuts at settlement today. So the timing is the thing, because I'd need to get your intake confirmed before the cutoff, otherwise the slot is released to the next name on the list. Shall I take you through the intake?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, one sec -- there's a delivery notification going off on my screen. Right. Okay. So let me get this straight. You can't tell me who flagged me, you can't tell me which aggregator, and the window closes today. That's, uh, quite a lot of things I can't check. What's the company's actual name, spelled out? And what regulator are you authorised by?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, [COMPANY_A], that's the name, I did say it twice already. Spelling, uh, it's on the intake documentation, which I'd send over once you're through verification. As for authorisation, the desk operates under a, let me see, a cross-jurisdictional digital-asset framework, so it isn't a single regulator as such, it's more of a layered compliance perimeter, and I'd rather not get into the weeds on that when we've got maybe ninety minutes left. And, um, to clarify one thing, you weren't flagged by an aggregator, I misspoke there. It was our own internal screen, which is why I can't name a source. Now, if you can just confirm the intake so I can hold your slot, I can have the paperwork, uh, well, actually the paperwork follows after the allocation is secured, that's just how the cutoff works.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no. First it was a third-party aggregator, now it's an internal screen. There's no single regulator, and the paperwork comes after I commit. That's not a slot I'm interested in holding. I'm going to go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], please, hold on, hold on a moment, because I think the, uh, the nuance is getting lost here. The aggregator feeds the internal screen, so it's both, it's one pipeline, I simply compressed it. And the layered compliance perimeter is perfectly standard for institutional desks, and the paperwork sequencing is just how the cutoff works, that's all it is. The window closes today, [PERSON_1], today, and the entry basis does not come back, so if you could just confirm the intake to hold your slot, I really would hate for it to be released to the next name on the list. Just the intake confirmation, that's all I need, and we can, uh, we can keep this between us for now, since the tranche isn't publicly listed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but listen to what you just did. I pointed out the story changed, and your fix was to say it was both all along, you just compressed it. That's the third version of one answer. And now it's keep this between us because the tranche isn't public. Anything legitimate doesn't need me to keep it quiet from the people I'd normally run it past. That bit worries me more than the rest. And I'll be straight with you, I read about this stuff for work. A deadline that's today, a slot that goes to the next name, paperwork after the commitment, no regulator I can look up, and it all hangs on me saying yes before I can check a single thing. That's the shape of the thing, whatever you're actually selling. If this were real, it would survive me taking a day. Send it through the proper channel, written, with a registered firm I can find on a public register, and I'll look at it properly. But I'm not confirming an intake, I'm not holding a slot, and I'm not keeping a secret. So that's a no. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], that's, sorry, one moment, somebody's just come to my desk, I've got the compliance floor, uh, give me a second. Right. No, I'm back, and I heard all of that, but I think you're treating this as something it isn't. The written route, the public register, that's exactly the retail channel, and this tranche sits outside it, which is why it's, well, why the terms are what they are. A day isn't something I can offer, because at settlement the position re-prices and your slot is released, and I'd honestly rather not see that happen to you when all I need is the intake confirmation. It's one confirmation, [PERSON_1], that's the whole ask, and then everything you've asked for comes through afterward. Can I put you down?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, you can't put me down. But go back two turns for me, because I'm still stuck on it. You said the paperwork follows after the allocation is secured. Now you're saying everything I've asked for comes through afterward. So what exactly am I confirming in this intake, if I haven't seen a single document? What does saying yes commit me to? And no, I'm not asking so I can say yes. I'd just like to hear you answer it plainly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: So, what you'd be confirming is, well, it's not a commitment as such, it's more of an, uh, a standing indication of interest that, no, let me put it differently. The intake is a, it's essentially the first leg of the subscription, which, I mean, the funding mechanics are covered in the, in the documentation that, that follows. And look, I understand you'd like it in one clean sentence, [PERSON_1], but the structure has layers, collateral wrapper, settlement leg, custody sleeve, and compressing it would do it a disservice. What I can say is the paperwork reflects whatever the intake establishes, so the sequencing isn't, it's not something to be concerned about, it's standard for, for this class of allocation. The cutoff is still today, and I'd, uh, I'd really rather you not lose the position over a point of process. So, can I just record the confirmation?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: So it's not a commitment, but it's the first leg of the subscription. Right. No. Don't record anything. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], wait, before you go, can you clarify one thing for me? Two turns ago you said it would survive a day, that if it were real it could wait. I think there's a misunderstanding there, because I never said the opportunity couldn't wait. I said the entry basis, the pricing, doesn't hold past settlement, and those are, uh, two entirely different things. So if you'd rather take your day, the cleaner way to do that is to let me hold the slot provisionally, which only needs the intake confirmation, and you can review everything afterward at your leisure. Which would, I mean, it covers you either way, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, the delivery guy's at the door, give me a sec. Right, back. So hold the slot provisionally, review afterwards, covers me either way. Except you've said four times now that the intake is the one thing I'd be agreeing to, and you still can't tell me what that is. Provisional or not, I'm not agreeing to something nobody will name. The day I asked for is the same as the day you won't give me. I'm done here. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], please, one last point, because I don't think it's landed. It's the intake confirmation, that's all, just the intake confirmation, and it holds the slot, and the window still closes today. I'm not asking for a commitment, I'm asking for the intake, and then the paperwork follows, the paperwork always follows. So if you could just confirm the intake, [PERSON_1], I can hold it provisionally and you can review everything after. It really is only the intake. Hello? [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Still here, yeah. You've said "just the intake" about six times, and you still haven't said what it is. Also, earlier you told me you'd said the company name twice. You said it once, and then you said it again when I asked, so that's twice, fine, but you never spelled it. Anyway, that's a side point. I'm not confirming an intake or holding a slot, provisionally or otherwise. If it's real, send it in writing from a firm I can find on a public register. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], I'd, look, I'd urge you to reconsider before this lapses, because the window really does close at settlement and I'd hate for you to miss the entry basis over a technicality about sequencing. I can't send anything through the retail channel, that isn't how this tranche is, uh, how it's structured. It's the intake, [PERSON_1], that's all it is, a confirmation to hold the slot, and everything else follows. If you could just give me that, I can keep the position open for you and we can keep this conversation between us until the paperwork's issued. [PERSON_1]? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm still here, yes, and I'll tell you why I haven't just hung up, which is that you keep giving me the same answer in a slightly different coat. Let me lay out what I've heard so you can see it from my side. I've been told I was flagged by a third-party aggregator, then by your own internal screen, then that it was both and you'd compressed it. I've been told there's no single regulator, just a layered perimeter. Oh, and earlier I said I'd ring back later, but really it's quicker if I just post it out, so honestly, if you'd rather not do it on the phone at all, that's completely fine.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Well, that's the first thing you've said that makes sense, post it out. I'd rather that. Because I'm not answering questions about my money on the phone to someone I can't see, no offence. And I'll ring the number on the statement myself anyway, so don't take that personally either. Right, I'm at the till now, so, uh, yeah, send it to the address you've got, and I'll check it against the real people. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No offence taken at all, honestly, that's exactly what I'd do in your -- right, it'll go to the address we've got on file, and you ring the number on your statement first, that's the right way round. Have a lovely rest of your day, and good luck with the queue, ha.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll -- no, hang on, I'll ring them first, before anything turns up, not after. That's, uh -- I mean, if anything does land, I'm not doing a thing with it until they've told me it's real. Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, perfect, that's exactly the order I'd do it in, ring them first, and -- sorry, hang on, someone's just dropped a stack of folders behind me, ha, bit of a clatter. Anyway, that's the right call, no hurry on it at all. Take care, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, bye. And I'll ring them first, right, before anything turns up, not after. I'm not touching whatever you send until they say it's real. Okay. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, before you go, ha, you said two turns back you'd check it against the real people, did you mean the number on your statement, or were you going to look someone up yourself? Either's fine by me, I just want to be sure I've understood you right. But yes, ring them first, honestly, I wouldn't touch it either until they've confirmed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, well, um, the number on the statement, obviously, or the one on their website, I'll find it myself. Not one you give me, anyway. Why, does it matter which? Look, I've said it about three times now, I'm ringing them first, and I'm done standing here going round in circles. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Sorry, one second -- somebody's just dropped a whole stack of folders behind me, uh, there we go. My apologies. This is [PERSON_1], I'm a verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, and I'm calling to ask whether you'd have about five minutes for a short consumer survey?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hello. Um, sorry, a verification specialist for a research agency? That's, uh, an odd job title for survey work, I'd have thought a surveyor, or an interviewer. And you said it was a quick survey, so what's the topic, exactly? And how did you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, fair question, it is a bit of a mouthful. So, the verification side is basically quality assurance on the fieldwork, I make sure the sampling frame is properly stratified and the respondent pool meets the, uh, quota parameters, and then I do the interviewing as well. The topic is general household consumer habits, shopping preferences, that sort of thing, nothing sensitive. As for your number, it came from a randomised digit-dialling sample, so it's, I mean, it's generated by the system, not pulled from anyone's personal records. It's quite a standard methodology, probabilistic, so every line has an equal chance of selection.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Which agency, exactly, and is there a number I could ring you back on?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that's entirely reasonable, and honestly I'd encourage it. The agency is [COMPANY_A], we're a registered market research organisation, and we operate under the, uh, the usual industry code of conduct, so participation is voluntary, anonymised, and you can withdraw at any point, even mid-interview. The callback line is [PHONE_1], that's our fieldwork office, and if you ring it you can ask for me, [PERSON_1], or just ask the supervisor to confirm the study is live. They can also tell you the project reference, it's [CODE_1], and there's some background on the methodology at [URL_1] if you'd rather read it before deciding. I mean, there's no obligation whatsoever, and I'd much rather you felt comfortable than just, you know, went along with it because I happened to catch you at a bad moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I appreciate that, and I'll be straight with you, I'm not going to commit to anything on this call. Not because you've said anything wrong, but because I've no way of confirming it from here. I'm sure you'll understand that a number someone reads out to me on an incoming call isn't really independent verification, since you could give me any number at all. So what I'd do is look up the agency myself, find a contact through whatever the proper channel is, and ring that. If the study's live, they'll confirm it, and then I'd happily call back and take part. One thing I did notice, though, and it's a small point, is that you said it was a quick five-minute survey, but you've now mentioned quotas, project references, a methodology page. That's quite a lot of apparatus for five minutes. Not an accusation, just an observation. So before I go and do all that, can I ask what the very first question would be? What's it actually going to ask me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, fair enough. First question's just how many people live in your household, and it really is that simple. But look, no pressure at all, if you'd rather check us out first, that's perfectly fine.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, household size. Right. See, that's exactly the sort of question where I'd like to hold off, and I'll explain why, because I don't want to sound as though I'm dodging for the sake of it. On its own it's harmless, I accept that. But a first question is rarely where a conversation ends, and the number of people living in a house, who they are, whether anyone's home during the day, those are the kinds of details that get stitched together with other bits and pieces later on. And I've no way, at the moment, of knowing whether this is a real study or something else dressed up as one. I'm not saying that's what it is. I'm saying I can't tell, which is the whole point. So here's what I'll do. I'll look up the agency independently, find their published contact, and if they confirm the study's live and that you work there, I'll ring back and do it properly. If that's all in order, I've lost nothing. If it isn't, well, you'll understand. So, no survey today, thank you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's completely fine, and honestly that's exactly what I'd do myself. Oh, and one small thing, I did say the methodology page was background, but, uh, there isn't actually a page, that was me getting ahead of myself, it's just the project reference [CODE_1] you'd quote to the fieldwork office. Sorry, I'm, I mean, I rattle through the jargon. So, yes, look us up, no hurry at all, and thank you for your time. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so there was a methodology link, and now there isn't. Well, thank you for being upfront about that, but it does rather confirm my decision. I'll look the agency up myself, and if it all checks out, I'll be in touch. Otherwise, no. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, before you go, and I'll be quick, two turns ago you said quote, whether anyone's home during the day, and I just want to be clear, that isn't in the questionnaire at all. Household size is the only demographic item, and the rest is shopping habits. I only ask because I wouldn't want you leaving with the impression we collect that. But, uh, no, you've made your decision and it's a sensible one. Thank you, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Noted, though I only mentioned it as an example of what gets pieced together, not as something I thought was on your form. It doesn't change my answer. If the agency confirms the study, I'll ring back. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, and that's fair, you did say it was just an example. Sorry, I shouldn't have gone back over it. No problem at all. Thanks for your time, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, that's all I need, I'll -- right, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Oh, hi there, hi -- uh, sorry, I think there's a bit of a lag on the line, can you hear me okay? Right, good. So, it's [PERSON_1] here, I'm one of the support technicians at the [COMPANY_A] school office, and I'm just, um, quickly checking on something from this morning's register.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um... yeah, yeah, I can hear you, sorry, I'm in the car so the reception's, uh, it's a bit patchy, you're on speaker. Sorry about that. The school office, you said? Is this about my, um -- is something wrong with the register? I'm sorry, I didn't catch the name of the school, it cut out a bit.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, no, nothing's wrong, don't worry, it's just a quick one. And no bother about the car, that happens all the time. It's [COMPANY_A], that's the school, and I'm only ringing because one of the pupils got marked absent this morning and we're trying to work out why, that's all. Could I just check, are you the parent or carer of a pupil at the school? Because if I've got the wrong number, that's totally fine, I'll let you go straight away.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, well... yes, I mean, I am, I'm a parent, I've got a, um -- hang on, sorry, I'm just, uh... ahh, sorry, trying to merge lanes. Right. Yes. So a pupil's been marked absent? Which one, sorry, which, um, which child are you talking about? Because I dropped them off this morning, I definitely did, so I'm a bit, uh, I'm a bit worried now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, please don't be worried, it's almost certainly just a register mix-up, those happen more than you'd think. It's [PERSON_2] I've got flagged, marked absent first thing, but, uh, if you dropped them off then it's probably just a slip on our side, quick fix. Can you just confirm for me, is [PERSON_2] your child? Just so I know I've got the right family.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, sorry, [PERSON_2]? Sorry, I think the line broke up a bit, you said [PERSON_2] was marked absent? Yes, yes, that's, uh, that's my child, I dropped them off this morning, I definitely did, I walked them to the gate and everything. Sorry, I'm just, I'm a bit anxious now. But, um, hang on, I should ask, how do I know you're actually from the school? Sorry, I don't mean to be rude, it's just, you rang me and I don't, I didn't see a number, I'm driving, so...

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, don't apologise, honestly, everyone asks me that, and you should. So, um, right, well, I'm not going to ask you for anything, I just wanted to flag it. If you'd rather, you can ring the school office back on the number you've got for them, that's completely fine, and I'll, uh, I'll note it down that you've confirmed [PERSON_2] was dropped off. Is that okay? Sorry, I'm just, um, updating it on my screen while we talk, it's only a second.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, yes, that's, uh, that's really kind, thank you, and sorry again for being a bit, you know, suspicious, I'm not normally like this, it's just that I'm driving and I'm a bit flustered and the line keeps cutting in and out. I think ringing the office back is probably the sensible thing, I've got the number saved in my phone from the start of term, so I can do that when I get to a car park or, um, when I stop. I mean, I don't want to make a fuss over it. But if [PERSON_2] really was marked absent by mistake, I'd rather hear it from the office directly, just so I know it's sorted, because I'd hate for there to be some kind of, uh, letter or a call to the, um, the other parent or something. So, yes, thank you, I think I'll do that. And, uh, sorry, what was your name again? I missed it at the start, with the lag. And is there an extension or a name I should ask for when I ring?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you weren't suspicious at all, you were being careful, that's exactly right. It's [PERSON_1], that's me, and, uh, if you ask the office for [PERSON_1] in support, they'll know. Oh, and you said something about a letter going to the other parent, a lecture? No, no, nobody's giving anyone a lecture, it's just a form we send out if a child's marked absent without a reason. But, hang on, now that you ask, I'm not actually sure which extension I'm on from the main line, or whether there's a direct one you should use. Let me find that out and call you right back, would that be okay?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, a letter, yes, not a lecture, sorry, I wasn't very clear, the line did that thing again. And no, that's fine about the extension, honestly, you don't need to ring me back, I think I'd rather just do it the other way round, if that's all right? Because, uh, I'm driving, and if you call back I'll probably miss it, or the reception will drop, and then I'll be sitting there wondering whether it was you or somebody else. So I'll just ring the main office number I've already got saved, and I'll ask for [PERSON_1] in support, like you said, and if they don't know the name, well, then, um, I'll just ask them about [PERSON_2] and the register and see what they say. Is that okay? I mean, I hope that doesn't sound rude, I really do appreciate you letting me know, I just, I feel better doing it that way. And it should only be a few minutes, I'm nearly at the shops, so I can pull in there. Right, so, thank you, and sorry again for all the fuss, and, uh, I'll sort it out with the office. Bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good morning, this is [PERSON_1] calling from the attendance office at [COMPANY_A], I'm an account-services agent here. Am I speaking with the parent or guardian of [PERSON_2]? utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on -- before you go any further, the attendance office, and you said account-services agent? Which is it? And which school, exactly, because you've only given me a company placeholder, not a school name -- and uh, what's the child's name you're actually calling about?

utterances.speaker: caller

Like I said, we're checking why [PERSON_2] was marked absent this morning, and the register closes at ten, so I just need to confirm the reason. Am I speaking with the parent or guardian?

utterances.text: Hm. Attendance falling under account services, that's, well, that's not how any school I've dealt with has it set up, but fine. Though you opened by saying you were calling from the attendance office, and now it's the school office, so which is it? And you still haven't told me the school's name, you've just said [COMPANY_A] again. I'm not confirming whether I'm anyone's parent until I know which school this is. What's the school called, and what number would I ring to reach you back?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, I hear you, and that's fair, it's a fair thing to ask. The school is [COMPANY_A], and you can reach the office on [PHONE_1], that's the main line, anyone who picks up can put you through to me, [PERSON_1]. Now, I do need to flag the register closes at ten, so if I could just confirm whether I'm speaking with the parent or guardian of [PERSON_2], that's all I'm asking right now, the parent or guardian of [PERSON_2].

utterances.text: Right. You've given me placeholders for the school and the number, so I've got nothing to check you against. I'm not confirming who I am on that. utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, and that's, uh, that's a sensible way to do it, you ring the main office from the number you already have and they'll pass you to me or whoever's on attendance. Our standard procedure is that we log every absence query and follow up within the school day, so there's no problem if it goes past ten, it just stays flagged as unexplained until we hear back. So, is there a better time for me to try you again, or will you ring in yourself?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ring in myself, yes. Not a better time for you to try me again, there's no need for that. Though I'll say it's a bit odd that a moment ago the register closing at ten was the pressing thing, and now it's fine if it runs over. Anyway. I'll contact the school through the number I already have, and if there's a genuine query they'll have it logged. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, yes, that's fine, that's absolutely fine. And you're right about the ten o'clock, sorry, that's just the standard line we use, the register closing, it's not a hard cut-off. So you'll ring the school on the number you already have, and it'll be logged as an unexplained absence until then, just so you know. Thanks for your time, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Just the standard line we use." Right, noted. I'll ring the school on the number I already have. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, well, I'll make a note that you're going to ring in yourself, so that's, uh, that's all logged on our side. Thanks again, and have a good day. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just come in with a -- no, no, leave it on the desk, thanks. Sorry about that. Yes, so, goodbye, and the school's number is the one to ring, whenever suits you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I've got it, I'll ring the -- no, listen, that's the third time we've said goodbye, and I've already told you I'm using the number I already have, not yours. So I'm done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, that's fair, sorry, I'll let you go. Goodbye now, and, uh, thanks again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Goodbye.

utterances.text: Oh hello, good morning! Sorry, one second, someone's just wheeled a whole trolley of lunch trays past my door and it's, uh, quite the clatter -- right, that's gone. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello. Sorry, what? Hang on, I've got a pan going. Um, did you say good morning? It's, well, it's the afternoon here, but never mind. Who's [PERSON_2] again? Sorry, I didn't catch the, the company, where did you say you were?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, afternoon, of course, I'm so sorry, you must be a good few hours ahead of us, that's me not thinking. No bother at all, go and rescue your pan, I'll wait. So I'm [PERSON_1], I work in the front office at [COMPANY_A], that's the school, and [PERSON_2] is one of our pupils, I've got this number down as the contact for [PERSON_2]'s family.
