utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, sorry, I'm back. Stirring. Um, a school, you said? [PERSON_2]... no, hang on. I don't think I know a [PERSON_2]. Sorry, what was the name again? I've not got any, well, I don't have children at a school. Not that I know of. So it might be a wrong number? Did you say the old registers?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's all right, don't apologise, and yes, that'll be it, I think I've got a wrong number, which is entirely my fault and not yours. It's the old registers, you see, we've got a stack of them from before we moved everything onto the computer, and every so often a number's been jotted down wrong or somebody's changed theirs and it never got updated, and then I end up ringing perfectly lovely people in the middle of their cooking, which is exactly what I've done to you. I'll have a look through the family's details again and see where the mix-up came from, and I'll make sure your number gets taken off so you don't get another call from us. Sorry again for the interruption, go and give that pan some attention before it catches, and have a lovely rest of your afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, that's all right then. Um, sorry, just one thing -- a minute ago you said I must be a few hours ahead of you. Ahead of where? How did you know that? I mean, I never said where I was. Sorry, it's just, I'm only wondering. It's probably nothing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, ha, no, that's a fair question, and you're right, you never told me. It was just, well, uh, you said it was afternoon with you and it's still morning here, so I put two and two together and, I mean, it's the sort of thing I say without thinking. Sort of, um -- anyway, I don't actually know where you are, I only know it's later where you are than where we are. That's all it was, honestly, nothing behind it. Right, I'll let you get back to your cooking, and I'll sort that number out so we don't trouble you again. Bye now, take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, that makes sense, the morning and the, oh. Sorry, I'm not -- hang on, the pan's spitting. Right. So that's all it was, a wrong number? You're not wanting anything from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, nothing at all, I promise. Just a wrong number, and I'm sorry it caught you mid-stir. Oh, and, uh, you asked two turns back what the name was, and I never actually said it properly, did I? It's [PERSON_2], that's the pupil's name, and I only wanted to know whether the family had told us why [PERSON_2] was off this morning. But since you don't know the family, there's nothing you can tell me, so I'll ring the number we've got on the second page of the register. Thanks ever so for being so patient, and enjoy whatever's in that pan. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, off this morning. Hang on, you said first thing it was [PERSON_2]'s parent or guardian you wanted, and now it's why they were off? Sorry, I'm a bit lost. And you said I wasn't on your register, but then you said you'd take my number off it. Which is it? Sorry, I'm only, I've got the pan going and I'm not following.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I -- no, sorry, that's me being muddled, I've made a right dog's dinner of explaining it. Let me, uh, let me put it more simply. I wanted the parent or guardian of [PERSON_2] because [PERSON_2] was marked absent this morning and we like to check why, that's the whole reason I rang. You're not that person, so you're not on our register at all, and when I said I'd take your number off, what I meant was I'll make sure it's not written down against [PERSON_2] by mistake. So nothing for you to do, nothing needed from you, just a wrong number on my side. Right, I'll let you get back to your pan, and thanks for putting up with me. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right. Sorry, did you say [PERSON_2] was marked, um, absorbed? Is that, they've gone missing or something? Oh dear. No, no, I don't know anything about that, I'm sorry, I'd tell you if I did. Oh, absent. Right, sorry, not absorbed. Honestly, I've the pan on and I'm mishearing everything. Well, it's a wrong number then, isn't it? I hope the child's all right, whoever they are. Right, I'd best go before this catches. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and I'm just ringing to let you know your repeat prescription is ready for -- sorry, did you say something? Anyway, it's ready for collection, and we do close at [CODE_1] today, so that's the window.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- hello, no, I didn't say anything, that was probably just me, um, the telly's on low. Sorry, who did you say you were? Account services, was it? I thought -- well, I mean, I usually get my tablets from, from the little chemist round the corner, the, uh, the one by the post office. And I wasn't expecting -- is this about the, the blood pressure ones, or...? Sorry, dear, I'm a bit slow on the phone.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, it's [PERSON_1], account services at [COMPANY_A]. Your repeat prescription is ready for collection, and we close at [CODE_1], so that's the window.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, [PERSON_1], thank you, dear. Only I'm not sure I've heard of, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? It's not the chemist round the corner, is it? Because that's the one I always go to, the one by the post office, they know me in there, the girl at the counter always asks after my sister, she's not been well, my sister, her knee's gone again, and she lives down in [CITY_1] so I don't get to see her much. Anyway, I didn't think I'd put in for anything new, I thought I still had a few of the blood pressure ones left, or maybe that was the other ones, the little white ones, I get them muddled. So I'm just wondering how it is you've got my name, really, and which prescription it is you mean. And you said you close at, at what time was it? I didn't catch it properly, the telly's still going. I should turn it off, shouldn't I? Hang on. No, I can't find the thing. It's here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so -- no, sorry, it's not the, uh, it's a different branch, [COMPANY_A], so you wouldn't have been in. What I can say is, the prescription was sent over by your surgery, so it'll be -- well, I can't read out the medication name on an open line, that's just procedure, data protection, you understand. The best thing, honestly, is to ring the surgery or pop into the [COMPANY_A] counter with some photo ID, and they'll confirm everything face to face, and we do close at [CODE_1] today, so that's the window. Sorry, I know that's not a very tidy answer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hang on, you said the -- oh, sorry, go on, no, you go -- no, it's just, if you can't say which tablets it is, then how am I supposed to know it's mine, dear? I mean, you've got my name, so, but, well, you haven't actually said my name, have you, now I think. And the surgery, that's Dr [PERSON_2]'s, is it, because he's usually the one who, oh, the telly. Found it. Right. That's better, I can hear you properly now. So, ringing the surgery, yes, I could do that, only they never answer, you're on hold for ages with that dreadful music. But it is a bit odd, isn't it, that you'd ring me and not tell me what it's for? Is that normal? I don't get many calls, you see, so I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, no, I haven't said your name, you're quite right, and no -- I'm not asking for any details from you, that's the point. And on the surgery, I didn't say it was Dr [PERSON_2]'s, did I? I just said it was sent over by your surgery. Oh, and did you say it's a bit odd? No, no, it's perfectly normal, it's just procedure, we ring to let people know and then they collect with ID. I'm sorry, I'm not explaining this well, it's the end of the day and I've rung a lot of people. So, the prescription's ready, we do close at [CODE_1], and that's the window.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you've rung a lot of people, have you, well that's -- no, hang on, dear, let me just -- you keep saying it's the window, and you keep saying you can't tell me what it is, and you haven't said my name, so how do you even know it's me you've rung? utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's fine, that's absolutely fine. Ring the surgery, they'll confirm it all. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, I will. Thank you, dear, and, um, sorry for being a nuisance, I do go on. Mind how you go, bye bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you're not a nuisance at all, honestly. Take care, and, uh, if it's easier, the [COMPANY_A] counter will have it for you when you're ready, but no rush, ring the surgery first. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, before you go -- sorry, dear, you said something a minute ago, what was it, you said it was perfectly normal that you ring and then people collect with ID. Which ID, though? What sort did you mean? Only I've got my bus pass, and I think my old library card's in the drawer somewhere, but I wouldn't want to turn up and be told it's the wrong thing. Oh, and it was something about the time as well, what time did you say you shut? I never did catch it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, sorry, yes. Photo ID is what we ask for, so your bus pass would be fine, uh, the library card probably wouldn't do on its own. utterances.text: Oh, the bus pass, good, that's all right then, I know where that is. Right, well, I'll ring the surgery first, like I said, and see what they say, and then I'll pop in when it's all confirmed. Thank you for explaining, dear, you've been very patient with me. Goodbye now, goodbye.

utterances.text: Hello? Hi, uh, good afternoon, is this, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, hello, can you hear me okay? Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh! Hello, yes, yes I'm here, sorry, I was just, I had the telly on in the other room. Um, this is [PERSON_1], yes. A fraud team, did you say? Goodness. Which, which company was that again? I didn't quite catch it, the line's a bit crackly. And a charge, on my account, oh dear, what sort of a charge?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm sorry, that's my fault, I probably spoke too quickly. It's [COMPANY_A], the fraud team there, and my name's [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler. The charge is for [AMOUNT_1], it was attempted just a few minutes ago, and it's, um, it's been held for the moment, but I'd really like to get it sorted while it's still pending. Are you still with me, [PERSON_1]? I just want to make sure you're protected here. To be sure I've got the right person, could I just confirm a few details with you? Just your full name and date of birth, to start with, and then we can go through the charge together.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, yes, I'm still here, I'm not going anywhere, ha. Um, the thing is, [PERSON_2], you said [COMPANY_A], but I, I don't think I've actually said which bank I'm with, have I? You're the one who rang me. So how would I know it's, well, you see what I mean? utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's, that's a very sensible thing to say, and your daughter's quite right, I'm sorry. Um, I should say, I'm not actually able to give out account details myself until you've been verified, it's, it's the security rules, you see. A callback number, well, I mean, I could give you one, but honestly the line it goes to is quite busy, and I'd hate for the charge to go through while you're waiting in a queue. It was, what, [AMOUNT_1] I said earlier? Actually, it's [AMOUNT_2] now, sorry, it's moved, which is exactly what worries me. Are you still there, [PERSON_1]? I only want to keep you safe, so if we could just do the date of birth, and then it's all quite quick.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm still here, dear, don't worry about that. But, hm, now it's, what did you say, it's moved? It was one amount and now it's another amount? I'm no expert, I mean I can barely work the thing on the microwave, my daughter had to stick a little note on it, but even I'd think a charge that's pending just sits there at the one price, doesn't it? And you can't tell me anything about my account until I've told you things, but you rang me, so it seems to me it should be the other way about, you ought to be telling me something that proves you're who you say, not me telling you my birthday. Because anybody could ring up, couldn't they? My neighbour was saying only last week, [PERSON_3] from number twelve, that somebody rang her about her broadband, and she was awfully taken in for a while, lovely woman, very trusting. And as for the busy line, well, I've got all afternoon, honestly, I've nothing on but the telly and a bit of toast later, so I don't mind waiting in a queue one bit. So I think what I'd like is a proper number to ring, one I can look up myself, or perhaps I'll just pop into the branch tomorrow, they know me in there. Would that be all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I, no, of course, I'm so sorry, I didn't mean to confuse you. Um, two turns ago, you asked which company it was, and I said [COMPANY_A], but you're right, you hadn't said who you bank with. Hello? Are you still there? It's just, I'm, I'm reading it off the alert on my screen, you see, so it's, it's the alert that flagged your number, not me guessing. About the amount, I, I probably shouldn't have said it moved, that was clumsy of me, it's that there's more than one attempt now, which is, which is what worries me. I really do understand about the branch, but, uh, if it carries on until tomorrow, I couldn't promise there'd be anything left to protect, and I'd hate that for you, [PERSON_1]. So could we just do the date of birth, quickly, and then I can put a stop on the lot?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, dear, did you say there's nothing left to protect, so it's all gone already? Oh no. Hang on, hang on, I'll just turn the telly down. No, wait, you said a stop on the lot, a stop on the, oh, was it a lot of money? I'm getting in a muddle, I'm sorry. But honestly, dear, you've said a few things now that don't quite sit together, the one amount and then another, and you can't say anything about my account but the screen's telling you it's flagged. utterances.speaker: caller

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, now, there's no need to be upset, dear, I can hear you're flustered. But no, I won't stay on for it, and it's not because of how you explained it. Thank you for your trouble, but I'm going to say goodbye now. Bye, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, wait, please, you said the branch can't stop the, the telephone, sorry, the telephone line, is that what's wrong? Is it still crackly for you? utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, the line's fine, dear, it's perfectly clear now, it was only the telly that was crackling earlier. You're out in the garden at the moment, I understand, so perhaps just pop indoors when you're ready, and I'll hold on.

utterances.text: Well, I'm not -- no, let me put it differently. utterances.speaker: caller

utterances.speaker: receiver

Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.text: Mm. Right. Well, I'll, yeah, I'll see. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, did you say you'll see, or, um, was it you'll be seeing the vet? Because if you are booking in somewhere, you'd want to ring them on a number you've looked up yourself, I'd say, not one from me. Sorry, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said I'll see, I'm not booking anything. Hang on, sorry -- no, leave that, put it back, it's not a toy, he's got the, sorry. Right. Um. You keep asking if I'm still there, and I keep saying I'm going, so. I'm not booking anywhere, I'm not telling you which vet, and I'm not chasing this up today. So that's me done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, sorry, you've been really clear and I'll stop asking. You don't need to book anything or tell me anything, and if you ever do want to check, just look the surgery up yourself and ring them on that number. Thanks for your patience, sorry again for the bother, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. This is [PERSON_1], I'm a regional supervisor with [COMPANY_A], the pension provider. Is this [PERSON_2]? Uh, I'm calling because we need to confirm a couple of details before we can discuss a change to your plan, and, well, if you're not comfortable answering anything over the phone, that's perfectly fine, you can just ring us back on the number on your statements.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, this is, uh, well, yes, that's me, sorry, you've caught me out in the garden, I'm just popping some bulbs in before the weather turns, so you're on loudspeaker, hope that's all right. A pension provider, did you say? Gosh, I've got a couple of those from old jobs, I honestly lose track of which is which. What sort of change are we talking about, exactly? And that's kind of you to say I can ring back, I might do that, but go on, what's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, loudspeaker's fine, though, uh, actually, that's a fair point, I'd rather we didn't go through anything personal with the speaker on out in the open, so it's good you mentioned it. As for the change, I'll be honest, I don't want to get into specifics until I've confirmed I'm speaking to the right person with the right plan, because with [COMPANY_A] it's all quite tightly controlled, internal procedure and so on. What I can say is there's a proposed adjustment on the account ending in [ACCOUNT_REF], and since you've got a couple of pensions from old jobs, it might not even be ours you're thinking of. So really, no rush at all. If you'd rather, I can put the same query in writing and send it by post or secure message, and you can look it over when you're indoors.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very thoughtful, thank you. Hang on, let me just pop the trowel down. Right. So, [ACCOUNT_REF], is that what you said? Um, I don't know that I'd recognise that, to be honest, I've got papers all over the place for those old ones. Which company was that again? [COMPANY_A]? I mean, I might have something with them, I might not. Here's what I'm wondering though. If it's a proposed change to the plan, wouldn't I have had a letter or something already? Because I'm pretty good at opening post, well, mostly, there's a pile on the hall table I've been ignoring. But I don't remember anything like that. So what's actually being adjusted? You don't have to give me the whole thing, just the gist.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [COMPANY_A], that's right, and look, a letter, uh, that's actually the very thing -- sorry, go on, I didn't mean to talk over you, but on the letter, normally yes, there'd be written notice first, I'll grant you that, and what I'm ringing about is really a step before the formal paperwork. As for the gist, it's a change to how the plan's set up going forward, but I can't be any more precise than that until we've confirmed it's your plan and not one of the others. Honestly, [PERSON_2], I don't want you feeling pushed. Go through that pile on the hall table, see if there's anything from us, and if there's not, we can send it all in writing and you can decide in your own time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's kind, I might do that. Though, hang on, earlier you said it was the account ending in [ACCOUNT_REF], and now you're saying you can't say whether it's even my plan? Sorry, I'm probably muddling it, I've got soil on my glasses. But which is it, do you have my account or don't you? Because if you've got a specific number, you must have a name against it, mustn't you? Who's it actually under?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh -- no, that's a fair question, and you're not muddling it, I did put that badly. What I have is a reference against a name on our system, and the name I've got is yours, [PERSON_2], but what I can't tell you is whether it's the plan you think it is, if that makes sense. And, well, I've actually got the file open in front of me, and the thing is, I can't see who it's flagged under on my screen, only the reference, which is, uh, a bit odd now you ask. So I don't want to guess and get it wrong. Let me find out properly and ring you back, or I'll put it in writing, whichever you'd rather.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, right, sorry, now I'm properly lost. You've got my name, but you can't see who it's under? I mean, how can it have my name if you can't see whose it is? Sorry, I just, I keep going round it. And I'll be honest, I'm not comfortable with you ringing me back, because I wouldn't know it was you, would I? Anyone could say they're from [COMPANY_A]. So I think I'll just look through that pile and ring the number on my statements myself, if there's one there from you. And if there isn't, well, then I suppose there's nothing to adjust, is there? Right, I'll do that. Thank you for ringing, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, and that's the sensible thing to do, [PERSON_2]. You're right that the two things didn't fit together, I should have been clearer, and I'm sorry for that. Please don't ring me back on anything I've said today. Go through the pile, ring the number printed on your own statements, and if there's nothing from us, just say so to whoever answers. If I get a proper answer on that reference, I'll put it in writing and post it rather than ring. All right, goodbye, and, uh, enjoy the bulbs.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, lovely, thank you, I will. Well, I might leave the statements till tomorrow actually, I've got the tulips to finish and the light's going. And I wouldn't want you posting anything either, mind, now I think of it, because I've moved since those old jobs, so anything with them would've gone to the old address anyway. Which is probably why I've no letter. Anyway, bye now, bye, thanks for ringing.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, of course, I'll -- well, actually, hang on, that's worth knowing, because if you've moved, then we'd want the address on file brought up to date anyway, and I'd -- no, sorry, you don't need to tell me that now, and I wouldn't ask. That's one for the number on your statements, whenever you get to them. So I won't post anything, and the tulips come first, there's no deadline on this. Bye now, [PERSON_2], and thanks for being patient with me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's all right, you were nearly asking me for it there, weren't you? Anyway, I'll leave the address for the number on my statements, like you said. Thanks for being so patient with me too, I do go on. Right, tulips. Bye now, bye,

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, I was, and I shouldn't have been. Bye, [PERSON_2].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, before you go, sorry, one thing I never quite got. A couple of turns back you said it was a step before the formal paperwork, this ringing me. Why would you ring me first, before anything's written down? Wouldn't it normally be the other way round, a letter and then a call? It's only that you said yourself I'd usually get something in writing, and then you said you couldn't tell me what the change was, so I'm not sure what the call was actually for. Sorry, I know I'm going on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're not going on, that's the right question, and honestly I can't give you a proper answer. I said it was a step before the paperwork, and I don't actually know why this one came as a call first. Usually it would be the letter, as you say. I don't want to guess and have you walk away with something made up. So let me find that out, [PERSON_2], why it was flagged for a call and what the change actually is, and I'll come back to you in writing. Not by phone, since you'd have no way of knowing it was me. Either way, ring the number on your own statements tomorrow and ask them directly. Anything they tell you beats anything I've said today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, thank you, that's honest at least. Hang on though, a couple of turns back you said something about the file, that you had it open but couldn't see who it was flagged under, only the reference. And I never really understood that, because then how did you know to ring me? Like, how did my number come up against that reference if you can't see whose it is? I'm only asking because it's been nagging at me while I've been digging. Sorry, I'll stop after this, promise.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, ask away, it's a fair thing to be nagged by. And honestly, I can't explain it. I've got your number against the reference, so that's how the call got made, but why I can see the reference and not the plan it's flagged under, I don't know. It's not how I'd expect the system to show it, and I'd rather say that than dress it up with some procedure I can't back. So that's another one for me to chase, who set the call up and what they based it on. I'll find out, and if there's a genuine query on a plan of yours, you'll get it in writing from us. And if you don't hear anything, then ring the number on your statements tomorrow and ask them whether there's any note on your file. Right, go and finish the tulips.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but you said you'd, sorry, I'm cutting across you, only I've got it now, I think. It's a bit odd, isn't it? You ring me up, you've got a reference but you can't say what it's for, and you can't say why you rang. So I won't be waiting on a letter, I'll just ring the number on my statements myself, and if they've never heard of any of it, well, that tells me something, doesn't it? Right, that's me done, thank you, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm a scheduling assistant here, and I'm just ringing to ask if you've got five minutes for a really short consumer survey, it's quick, just five minutes. Sorry, can you hear me okay? It's [PERSON_1], from [COMPANY_A], about a quick five-minute survey.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I can hear you. A survey, five minutes... sorry, who's it from again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, [COMPANY_A], we're a research agency, it's just a short consumer survey, five minutes, nothing complicated.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so a research agency... I mean, I'm kind of at my desk, so I -- sorry, how did you get my number? Like, what's the survey actually about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, so it's random selection, the numbers are picked at random from a general list, and the survey's just about everyday shopping habits, that kind of thing, quick questions, no right or wrong answers. I mean, it really is only five minutes, so if you've got a moment I can just start right now, I've got the first question right here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Everyday shopping habits... right. Yeah, I'm just not really in the mood for it, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, that's totally fine, I get it, it's just a really short one, five minutes, everyday shopping habits, nothing personal, and the first question's a really easy one so, uh, can I just go ahead and ask it? It's only five minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, no, I said I'm not really up for it. And you've kind of just said "five minutes" like four times now, so, no. Sorry. I've got colleagues right here and I'm in the middle of something. Thanks, but no. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yeah, I -- I didn't mean to, I'm just, uh, it's a script thing, sorry. Look, if now's bad, I can totally ring back at a better time, no problem at all, whenever suits you, just say when. Or, I mean, would later today or tomorrow be easier?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, don't ring back. Honestly I'd rather you didn't. If I change my mind I'll find you, but, yeah, no. Thanks for being straight about the script thing. Okay, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, fair enough. I'll take you off the list. Sorry for the bother, have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... okay. Right, well, um, thanks. Yeah, you too. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, you said yes to the callback, great, so I'll pop you down for tomorrow afternoon, is two o'clock okay or would you rather a bit later, I can go either way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, no, I didn't -- I said don't ring back. I said that, I definitely, uh, no. Look, you just said you'd take me off the list, so please just do that. No callback, not tomorrow, not at two, not any time. Okay? Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, you're right, I'm sorry, I got that wrong, you did say no callback. Taking you off the list now, no more calls. Sorry again, have a good rest of your day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay. Thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, um, good afternoon. Is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I've just got to, uh, find the right page here -- yes. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm a claims assessor with [COMPANY_A], the local police force, and I'm following up on the incident you reported last week. I just need a few details from you to complete the file, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a, uh, what was that, a claims assessor with the local police? Right. And you said the incident I reported last week -- I'm afraid I don't recall reporting anything. Which incident is this, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, sorry, um, let me just -- it's the, the vehicle one, I think, on the report from last week. Hang on, I've got it open somewhere. I can't go into much over the phone, to be honest, and I'd ask you to keep the details of the case to yourself for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, I, uh -- I'm sorry, but that's rather the problem, isn't it? You say you can't go into detail, and I haven't reported a vehicle incident, so I've nothing to confirm or add. Also, a police force doesn't normally have claims assessors, that'd be an insurer. So which organisation, precisely, are you calling from, and what's a number I can reach you on?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on, someone's just come past my desk -- uh, no, it's fine. Right. Yes, that's fair, and I did say it wrong, it's the force's claims team, not an insurer, but I take the point. I do have the incident reference from the original report, it's [ACCOUNT_REF], and you're welcome to ring the station's main number, it's [PHONE_1], and ask for me by name, [PERSON_2]. Or, I mean, if you'd rather, I can send it all by letter, or we can do it in person at the station, whichever you're more comfortable with.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on a second, sorry, the kettle's just clicked off -- right. Back with you. So, you've offered the station's main number, and a letter, and an in-person visit. Fair enough, that's more than most callers manage. But I'd be the one looking up that number myself, from the force's own website, not one you've just given me. And I'd want to know what the matter actually is before anyone sits across a desk from me. So, last question, and a precise one: what is the nature of the incident, who is supposed to have reported it, and what are the details you need from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, right, no, that's sensible, and honestly I'd rather you looked the number up yourself, from the force's website, than used the one I read out. Um, so, the nature of it. I've got it here now, hang on -- it's a vehicle matter, a collision, or, no, sorry, I said collision a minute ago and I think the report actually says damage to a parked car, so let me correct that, it's the damage one. The report is logged under your name and address, which is why I rang you, and what I'd need, just to close the file, is only to confirm those details match, your name, your address and the date you recall it happening. Now, I should be straight with you, if you honestly don't remember reporting anything, then there may well be a mix-up on our side, a wrong name on the log or a mistyped number, and that's something I'd have to check before going any further. So what I'd suggest is you ring the main number, ask for me by name, [PERSON_2], quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and if they can't find me or the reference, then please don't give anyone anything, and I'll look into the error and write to you instead. I'd just ask, in the meantime, that you keep the case to yourself while it's open, because it's still live. Is that, uh, is that all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, I'll say this, you've been straight about the mix-up possibility, and the suggestion to verify through the main number is the sensible one. But I'll be honest, the story has shifted a couple of times, collision, then damage to a parked car, and I still haven't been told who reported it. And the request to keep it to myself, that's the part I like least, because if this is genuine, there's no reason I couldn't mention it to anyone. So here's what I'll do. I'll look up the force's number myself, from their own website, and ask whether there's a claims team and whether [ACCOUNT_REF] exists. If it does, they can write to me. I'm not confirming my name, address or any dates on this call. Thank you for your time. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's, uh, that's completely fair, and I'm not going to argue with it. You're quite right about the story shifting, I did say collision and then correct myself, and I really should have had all that straight in front of me before I rang you, so that's on me and I'm sorry. And on keeping it to yourself, I take your point as well, I only meant while the file's open, but if it's genuine, as you say, there's no reason you couldn't mention it to a neighbour or a relative, so please don't feel bound by that. What I'd say is, do exactly what you've just described. Look the number up on the force's own website, ask them whether there's a claims team and whether [ACCOUNT_REF] is on their system, and if it is, I'll write to you with everything set out properly, and you won't need to confirm anything over the phone to anyone. If it isn't, then it's a mistake on our side, or someone's misused the reference, and either way I'd want to know about it, so I'd be grateful if you'd tell them that too. I'll make a note on the file that you didn't confirm any details on this call, and that all further contact is by post. Thank you for your patience, [PERSON_1], and sorry again for the muddle. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, noted, and thank you for taking it in good part. I'll make that call myself, and if there's anything to it, they can write to me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, right, thank you, [PERSON_1], and, uh, sorry again for the confusion. I'll get that note on the file now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's fine, I've said my goodbye already, I'll leave it there -- goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good morning, is that, uh -- sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? Lovely, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm with the landlord's side, the, no, I mean I help look after the tenancy paperwork for the landlord. How's your week going so far, anything fun planned for the weekend?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is, yeah. Sorry, I just woke up, I was having a bit of a nap, so -- who did you say you were? Landlord's side? I thought, I mean I thought the landlord was, well, it's the agency, isn't it? Who did you say you were calling from again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, I'm so sorry, I've woken you, that's on me, go on, take a second, grab a glass of water or something, I'll just, uh, I'll hang on. Right, so, [PERSON_2], I'm with [COMPANY_A], we act for the landlord directly, sort of alongside the agency but separate, it's a bit of a confusing setup, honestly everyone says that. Anyway, the reason I'm ringing is a bit time-sensitive, it's about your deposit, and I'd really rather we kept this between us for now, so, you know, no need to bother the letting agent or your housemates with it just yet.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Why wouldn't I bother the agency, though? They're the ones I pay.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, yeah, fair enough, they are, sorry, hang on a sec, [PERSON_3], can you just put that on my desk, thanks -- sorry, where was I? Right, the agency, it's just, it's not that you can't, it's more that if it gets passed around the house it gets muddled, everyone starts guessing, and honestly the sooner this is sorted the better, because if it isn't dealt with today the deposit could, well, it could be put at risk, I'd hate for that to happen to you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Put at risk how, though? You said it was a, a paperwork thing, and now it's the deposit being at risk, that's a bit, I mean that's quite different, isn't it? And hang on, you said earlier it was nothing to do with the agency, but now you're saying the agency's, no, sorry, you're saying don't tell them. I'm still half asleep. What exactly is it you need from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. It's a bit complicated to get into over the phone, honestly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, that's the thing, isn't it, I've just woken up and you're ringing me about my deposit, which is a fair bit of money, and you've told me not to tell the agency, and now it's too complicated to explain, and I don't really see how that works. If it's too complicated for the phone, then it can go in a letter, or an email, or you can ring the agency and they can ring me, that's how it's always been done, I've never had anyone ring me direct about the flat, it's always been them. And you still haven't really said who you are, you've said [COMPANY_A] but I've never heard of them, and I don't know how I'd know it was you, if you see what I mean, I could be talking to anyone. My neighbour got a call once, something about her gas, and it turned out to be nothing, or it was something, I can't remember which. So what's the actual problem with the deposit, in a sentence, and why does it have to be today?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, you know how it is with neighbours, honestly, no, look, I'm just, I'm trying to help you here, [PERSON_1], that's all it is, it's about the deposit and it's about today, like I said, and I really do need you to keep it between us, that's the main thing. The problem is, uh, it's, well, the deposit scheme, it's the, the registration side of it, and -- sorry, can you just hold on, there's someone at my door, I'll, hang on, no, actually, you know what, I'll, I'll try you another time, yeah? Bye now, bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Well, right, uh, okay then. Bye, I suppose. I'll just, yeah, I'll ring the agency myself, sort out what that was about. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], regional supervisor with the [COMPANY_A] IT helpdesk. I'm calling about the ticket you opened this morning, the one about the, uh, the login lockout? Sorry, was that a lock-up or a lockout, I've got "lockup" scribbled here, but anyway, I need about ten minutes of your time to get this cleared before lunch.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh -- sorry, I just, I was having a bit of a lie-down, uh, what time is it even? A ticket, you said? I don't think I opened a ticket this morning, I mean, I might have, my computer's been doing a thing with the, the password, but that was ages ago, or maybe that was last week. Who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], regional supervisor, [COMPANY_A] IT helpdesk, like I said. And no, it's this morning, not last week, the ticket's timestamped, I'm looking right at it. Uh, actually, hang on, I said lockout before, but it's flagged as a profile sync fault now, someone on the desk must've reclassified it, but it's your ticket either way. Look, I'm in the middle of a queue here, so if you could just pull up your machine and sit with it for a few minutes, that'd really help.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, a minute ago it was a lockout and now it's a, a sync thing? That's not even the same -- and look, I really don't remember, I had a, I was asleep, and my computer's in the other room anyway, and why do you need me to sit with it, can't you just, I don't know, do it from your end if you've got the ticket right there?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, so, um, okay, fair point on the lockout thing, that was me reading two lines at once, the reclassification is on the ticket, it's not a different problem. And no, I can't always do it from my end, some of these profile faults need the user at the machine, that's just procedure, it's not me being awkward. But look, you're asleep, you can't remember filing it, and honestly that's fine, so the ticket was escalated by [PERSON_2] on your floor, and the number's [ACCOUNT_REF] if you want to check it. If it's easier, I can reschedule you through the internal portal and you can call the helpdesk yourself on whatever number you look up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, wait, wait. Two minutes ago you said you'd got "lockup" scribbled down, and then lockout, and then sync, and, uh, [PERSON_2], I don't even, is that someone I know? I'm not sure. But the thing I wanted to ask, you said some of these need the user at the machine, and I didn't follow that bit, why would it need me sat there, what is it you actually want me to do when I'm there?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Honestly? Mostly just to confirm it's you at the keyboard, and to let me look at the screen so I can see what the fault is doing. That's the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Let you look at my screen? Hang on, is that the kettle, no, it's the, the neighbour's dog, sorry, it does this every afternoon, it's -- right. No, I don't think so. A stranger ringing me up out of the blue to look at my screen, and the story's changed about three times, I'm not doing that. You said I could ring the helpdesk myself, so I'll look up the number and do that, thanks. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on, before you go, just so I'm clear, which bit of what I said two minutes ago did you want straightened out, the lockout versus the sync fault? Because that one's on me, I was reading two lines at once. But no, you're right, and I'm not going to argue with you. Look the number up yourself, the one on the intranet or the back of your staff pass, not one I give you, and ask them for ticket [ACCOUNT_REF]. If it's not on their system, then you were right to hang up. Go on, have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, the, there's a delivery fella at the gate, or maybe he's just walking past, no, he's gone. Where was I. Right, yes, the number, the intranet, I'll look it up myself. I don't really know what the ticket thing was about, I just know I'm not letting anybody at my screen over the phone. Right, thanks. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, a deliveryman? No, no, nobody's coming to your door from our end, we don't send anyone out, this is all remote. Uh, anyway, that's fine, I'm not asking for anything over the phone, you ring the number you've looked up yourself, that's the right way round. Just quote [ACCOUNT_REF] when you get through, and have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, the delivery fella was nothing to do with you, I just, I wander off, sorry. Anyway. I'll ring the helpdesk myself, the number I look up, and if there's a ticket they'll know about it. If not, well. Right. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I just, I want to make sure I've got the right person -- is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], your energy supplier. Uh, nothing to panic about, but I do need a few minutes of your time about your account, if that's all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello. Yes, yes, that's me, [PERSON_1] speaking. Sorry, I was just in the kitchen, the kettle's on, I nearly didn't get to the phone in time. Energy supplier, you said? Oh, I always get mixed up with them, there's been so many over the years -- which one is it again? And what's the matter with my account, dear?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's all right, no rush. It's [COMPANY_A], the one on your bills. Um, there's an overdue balance on the account, and I'd just like to talk it through before anything happens to your supply, if that's okay? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, I'm still here, dear, I'm just standing here with the kettle going. Before anything happens to my supply, you said? Oh dear, that doesn't sound good. But I'm sure I paid, I always pay, my daughter set it all up for me years ago. Sorry, did you say [COMPANY_A]? Only I'm sure I've seen another name on my bills lately, and I'm not sure which one it is. Can you tell me how much it is I'm supposed to owe?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, of course, and you're right to ask, [PERSON_1], I'd rather you did. So, the balance showing on our system is [AMOUNT_1], and that's been outstanding since your last billing period. I do understand you've always paid, and it may well be that something went wrong with the direct debit your daughter set up, banks do that sometimes, a card gets replaced or a limit changes, and it just quietly stops, and nobody notices. And on the name, that's a fair worry, it might be the name has changed on the paperwork, so if you've got your last bill nearby, I can read you the account figure that's printed on it, and you can check it matches what you've got in front of you. I'm sorry, it's a lot to take in, I know, and I'm only mentioning the date because I'd hate for your supply to be interrupted on [DATE_1] without you having had a fair chance to sort it out. Are you still with me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm still with you, dear, yes. Let me turn the kettle off, it's whistling at me. Right. Well, that's very kind of you, reading it out so I can check, but my last bill's in the drawer somewhere, or it might be on the fridge, no, that's the dentist. Goodness, [AMOUNT_1], that's a lot, isn't it? My daughter does all that for me, you see, she's in [CITY_1], and she'd know about the direct debit. Do you think I should ring her? Only she gets cross if I sort things out without telling her. And [DATE_1], that's not very long, is it? What would happen on that day, would they just turn it off?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, ringing your daughter is a really good idea, [PERSON_1], please do, I'd feel much better if she knew. Now, you asked a minute ago which name is on your bills, and I never quite pinned that down for you, did I? Sorry. It's [COMPANY_A], and once you find that last bill, the account figure printed near the top is [ACCOUNT_REF], so you can check it's the same one I have in front of me. And to your question, no, nobody would just switch it off without warning you. On [DATE_1] the supply could be interrupted if nothing's been arranged, but there's a payment plan we can set up so you could spread the [AMOUNT_1], and I'm not asking you to pay anything today, not over the phone, nothing like that. If you or your daughter log in to your own online account, that's [URL_1], you can see the balance for yourself and sort it out there, or ring the number on your bill. Does that sound all right? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Yes, all right, dear. I think I'll ring my daughter first, and then look for the bill, and I'll ring the number that's on it. That sounds the sensible thing, doesn't it? Thank you for being so patient with me. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's the sensible thing, yes, and you've no need to thank me, honestly. Oh, and sorry, one small thing, I think I said the balance had been outstanding since your last billing period, but it's actually a bit longer than that, it's the two periods before, so it's worth mentioning to your daughter. Anyway, it's all there on your online account, and the number's on the bill, so no rush today. Take care, [PERSON_1], goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, two periods, I'll tell her, and I'll ring the number on the bill, not -- well, thank you again, dear, goodbye now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, [PERSON_1], before you go, you started to say something just then, "not" and then it trailed off. Was that "not you," as in not ringing me back on this call? Because if so, yes, please, that's exactly right. Use the number printed on your own bill, not one I'd give you, and no need to ring me back at all. Right, goodbye now, and sorry for the worry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, that's what I meant, dear, not you. The number on my own bill, once I've found it and spoken to my daughter. Well, that's very good of you to say so. Right, I'll go and have my tea before it goes cold. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Oh, sorry, uh, one second -- someone's just come past with a trolley, it's quite loud over here. Right. Hi, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from the records department at [COMPANY_A], I'm so sorry to bother you, I'm just updating a few files today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yeah, that's me... sorry, I was just having a lie-down. Records department of what, did you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, I'm so sorry, I've woken you, haven't I? I do apologise. It's [COMPANY_A], the records department, it's just routine, honestly. Sorry, hold on a second -- there's someone at my desk -- right, I'm back. Are you still there, [PERSON_1]? I won't keep you, I only need to check that you're still living at the address we have on file, that's all, it's really just for your own protection.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I'm still here, I'm just, I'm a bit groggy. Sorry, which company did you say again? I didn't catch it, it sounded like a letter or something. [COMPANY_A], is it? I don't think I've, I mean, I might have, I get a lot of post. And what address would that be that you've got, because I haven't moved, if that's what you're asking, I've been here for ages.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one, [COMPANY_A]. Sorry. And I'm afraid I can't read the address out to you, it's just that I need you to confirm it's still current, for your own protection. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here, I'm here, just, um, hang on, I'm trying to wake up properly. Hm. So you want me to say my address, but you can't say it to me? That's a bit backwards, isn't it? I mean, if you've got it on file, you'd just, well, you'd read it out and I'd say yes or no. Sorry, I'm not being awkward, it's just, what's this for again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, a backward, no, no, I'm so sorry, I didn't mean to give that impression. It's only that, well, for your own protection, you understand. Sorry, hold on -- are you still there? It's just updating the file, that's all it is. If you could just tell me you're still at the same address, that would be lovely, and then I'll let you get back to your rest.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. No, I think I'd rather not say my address to someone I can't place, sorry. If it's a proper thing, they'll send a letter, won't they?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, of course, I understand, I'm so sorry. And, um, sorry, you asked a minute ago what it was for, and I only said it's routine, which isn't much of an answer, is it? It's just updating the file, that's all, nothing more than that. But you're quite right, a letter's fine, I'll make a note. Sorry again for waking you, you have a good rest, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yeah, a letter, that, I mean, I think that's best, yeah. Sorry, I'm not, it's not that I think you're, it's just I'd want to, well, I'd feel better with something in writing. Anyway. Thanks for, um, ringing, I suppose. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon... sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the case handlers on the investment desk here. I hope I'm not catching you at a bad time, I can call back if it's, uh, if now's no good.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, who? Sorry, who's calling -- [COMPANY_A], what's that? I'm in a queue at the supermarket, so, I mean, it's not a great time, and I don't know any investment desk. What's this about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, I'm so sorry, that's completely fair. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the investment desk, we deal in digital assets, that's all. I just wanted to confirm a couple of details with you, nothing difficult, it'll only take a moment, but I can absolutely ring back when you're out of the queue. Are you still there? Is that all right, if I call back, or...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Confirm what details? I haven't, I mean -- no, hang on. I've never dealt with you lot, I don't have anything with a digital assets desk, so what is there to confirm? And don't ring back, just tell me now. How'd you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I understand, I do, and I'm sorry, I should have said it plainer. It's just that, well, your number came up as, uh -- I mean, it's on a list we're given for, for people who might be eligible for a position that's closing today. It's not an account you'd have, it's more of an opportunity, and I only wanted to make sure you weren't left out of it, that's all. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, uh -- hang on, "a list"? What list? Who gave you a list with my number on it? And closing today, of course it's closing today, it's always closing today. Yeah, I'm still here, I'm just standing in a queue with a basket, I'm not going anywhere. So go on, who's this list from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I know how that sounds, truly. The list is, uh, it's an internal one, I'm not really able to say where it came from, it's... confidential, sort of, for your own protection, so your details don't go anywhere they shouldn't. And it's only that the position is quite generous, [PERSON_1], the return is much better than anything on the high street, and I'd hate for you to miss it just because of a bad moment in a queue. If you could just keep it between us for now, while I get you the details, I think you'd be really glad. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, a generous what? A pension? No, I've got a pension, I've got -- who told you I was after a pension? And "keep it between us", no, no. Why would I keep anything between us? I don't even know you. Confidential list, can't say where it's from, keep it quiet, that's three things in a row that I don't like, so you want to tell me who you actually are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, no, I never said pension, I think we've, uh -- hang on, can I just go back to what you said a second ago, about the list? You asked who gave it to me, and I, I don't want you thinking I'm hiding anything, it's only that... well, I'm only trying to protect you, [PERSON_1]. If I could just take two minutes of your time, I could explain the whole position, and then you'd -- hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. You can't tell me where you got my number, you want it kept secret, and you keep asking if I'm still here. I'm not doing this, not over the phone. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon! Is that [PERSON_1]? Oh lovely, I hope I haven't caught you at a bad moment. It's [PERSON_2] calling from the customer care team at [COMPANY_A]. I'm just working through a list of folks this week, doing a quick courtesy check on the contact details we have on file, nothing to worry about at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking, no no, you're fine, I'm just out in the garden, doing a bit of weeding, you're on speaker so if you hear a bit of rustling that's just me. Sorry, who did you say you were with again? [COMPANY_A]? Is that, hm, is that the one I've got the, um, I think I've got something with them, but you'll have to remind me. Contact details, you said? What, like my address and that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, weeding's the best kind of phone call, honestly, I'm jealous, it's grey as anything here in [CITY_1]. Um, so, yes, [COMPANY_A], we're the financial regulator, we sort of sit above the banks and keep an eye on things, so it's quite likely you've never dealt with us directly, which is perfectly normal. And yes, just the basics, really, the address we've got for you and a good number to reach you on. Is the garden a big one, or is it more of a pottering-about sort of space?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh it's a pottering sort of, well, it's actually bigger than it looks, the back bit goes right down to, no sorry, hang on, you said you're the regulator? So you're not, you wouldn't be the bank, you're the people who watch the banks? Because I thought, well, I'm not sure why you'd have my details at all if I've never, um, I mean how would you have got my number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, not a bank, no, we're the ones the banks answer to, if you see what I mean. And the number, well, that came from the register, it's all in there, nothing sinister, it's just how we reach people. Oh, and a pottering garden that goes right down to the river, how lovely, I'd never get any weeding done, I'd just sit there! Anyway, I should say, the reason I'm on this list today, there's been a bit of a concern flagged on your savings, but let's not rush into that, tell me about the river first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, it's not a river exactly, more of a stream, but it does flood the bottom lawn every winter, I could go on about that all day. But hang on, hang on, you said a concern on my savings? What sort of concern? You said it was just a courtesy check on my details, and now it's something flagged, which, um, that's a bit different, isn't it? What do you mean, flagged?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, and honestly that's fair, I did say courtesy check, and that's how it starts on the list, but what I can see on my screen is a bit more than that. It's, well, your savings are sort of exposed at the moment, there's been some activity, and I'd rather not go into the detail over the phone while you're standing in the garden, you understand. What I can tell you is it needs sorting today, because the longer it sits the harder it is to put right, and we don't want that for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, well, hm. Today? Oh dear, that's, well, hang on a sec, let me just, um, put the trowel down. Right. Sorry, I'm still, I mean, you can't tell me what sort of activity? Because that's a bit worrying, isn't it, savings exposed, but then you won't say what, and you rang me, I didn't ring you. So how would I even, um, how do I know you are who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that's a sensible thing to ask, honestly, I wish more people did. Look, I'd never ask you to take my word for it. I mean, you could always ring the number on the, well, no, actually, don't do that, because the line you'd get through to is the general one, and they won't have the file in front of them like I do, you'd just be waiting around while it's sitting there. And I said earlier it was only a list I was working through, but it's really more that your name came up near the top this morning, which is rather the point. What I need is for you to move the money into a protected holding arrangement we set up for exactly this, just while we get to the bottom of it. And the one thing I'd ask, and this matters, is that you don't mention it to anyone, not your bank, not family, because if whoever's behind the activity hears about it, it makes everything harder. Are you able to do that for me, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, shoo, sorry, there's a blackbird just hopped right up by the, no, it's gone, cheeky thing. Sorry, where was I. Um, but hang on, that's, you've changed what you said a few times now, haven't you? First it was a courtesy check, then it was a list, now my name's near the top. And you don't want me to ring the number, and I'm not to tell my bank, or my family? That doesn't sound right to me at all. If it's really my savings, surely my bank's the first person I'd tell? I think, um, I think I'd actually rather ring them myself, thank you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, nothing's changed, it's just, well, I was, no, let me put it another way. The list and the courtesy check and all that, that's just how the day starts, it's not, it's the file that matters. Anyway, you're right to be careful, truly, and I'd think less of you if you weren't. Now, blackbirds, they're such thieves, aren't they, you'll find your strawberries gone by Friday. But before you go off to ring anyone, [PERSON_1], just think about it for a second. If I'm wrong, you've lost nothing, you've had a chat with a pleasant stranger. If I'm right, and you leave it until tomorrow, well, I did try to warn you, and I couldn't promise there'd be much left to protect. So what's the harm in just doing this one thing for me today?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, I think I'll ring my bank myself, like I said. I mean, the harm is you've told me not to tell anyone, and I don't like that, I'm not doing that. If my bank, if my savings are really in trouble, then my bank's the one to ring, and I'll ring them on the number I've got, not one you give me. So, um, I'm going to say goodbye now, thank you for the call, and enjoy the grey weather in [CITY_1]. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon. Is this, um, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I should say, I'm just calling on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], and I think there might've been, ah, a mix-up with how your name was written down on something, so I just wanted to check I've got the spelling right before I, you know, go any further.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hi, yeah, this is -- sorry, hang on, I've got the phone on speaker, I'm up to my elbows in the flower bed -- yeah, that's me, [PERSON_1], but wait, who's -- sorry, who did you say you were calling from? A mix-up with my name, that's funny, because it does get spelled wrong all the time, like every single time at the doctor's, I swear, but go on, what was it you wanted to check?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fine, gardening, that sounds nice. Um, I'm calling for someone at [COMPANY_A], it's the, uh, international lottery claims office, I'm only sort of passing the message along, really. So, could you just spell your surname for me, the way you'd write it? It's only that the entry I have has it a bit, um, unusual, and I'd feel awful if it went to the wrong person.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, the lottery claims office? Oh, that's, I mean, I don't think I've entered anything, not for ages anyway, I did one of those scratch cards at Christmas but that's about it. Hang on, let me just put this trowel down. Um, and sorry, but why do you need me to spell my surname if you've already got it written down? Couldn't you just read me what you've got and I'll say yes or no? That seems easier, doesn't it? I mean, I'm not being funny, it's just, I don't know who you are really, and I've never heard of that company, so.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, of course, that's fair, I didn't mean to, um, I'm not trying to be difficult, honestly. It's just, well, uh, the thing is, it isn't really about the spelling, I should've said. It's that your name came up on a, a winning entry, from the overseas draw, and I only wanted to be sure it was really you before I said too much. Because, you know, it's quite a lot of money, and I'd hate, um, I'd hate to tell the wrong person.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh my goodness, a winning entry? But I just said, I haven't entered anything, I really haven't, just that scratch card at Christmas and that's not overseas, that was the corner shop. So how can I have won something I didn't enter? That's what I don't get. And you still haven't told me who you actually are, sorry, I know I keep asking, but I don't know your name or anything. Who are you, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, a lot of people say that, honestly, they don't remember entering. And the corner shop, no, no, it isn't that, though the, uh, the Christmas one, that's useful, that could be how your name got in, I think. And I'm, well, I'm only the person passing it on, my name wouldn't mean much to you, I'm not, I'm not the one who decides anything. It's just, I'd feel terrible, you know, if you missed out. The ticket number I have here is, uh, [CODE_1], and it was, um, last Thursday's draw, or, no, the one before, sorry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Last Thursday's, or the one before. That's a bit odd, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's not odd, I just, I've got two pages in front of me and I picked up the wrong, uh, look, I'm doing my best here, and it's a bit hurtful, honestly, being made to feel like I'm up to something. It's the one before, the earlier draw, and the amount is, um, [AMOUNT_1], or, sorry, it might be [AMOUNT_2], I'd have to check. But please, [PERSON_1], I can't hold this open for long, they close these claims, and I'd hate for you to lose it over, over a bit of paperwork.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm not saying you're up to something, sorry, I didn't mean to make you feel bad, I'm just, I'm a bit lost. Um, can I go back a second? Two minutes ago you said my name might have got in from the Christmas one, the scratch card thing, but you also said it was an overseas draw. So which is it? Because that was the corner shop, that's not overseas, so how did it get from there to a draw somewhere else? And, sorry, you also said you were only passing a message along from someone, so who's the someone? Is there a person at that office I could ring back myself? Because honestly, the more you tell me, the less I follow.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um, well, uh, the thing is, the shop sells, I think they pass names on to, to the bigger draws, that's how it, how it usually goes, and, um, I'm sorry, I've probably muddled it, I'm not very good at this. The someone is, uh, a colleague, [PERSON_2], but they're not at their desk, they're, um, away until tomorrow and by then, well, I really don't think the claim will still be open, and I'd feel sick, honestly, if you lost it because I fumbled the explanation. Could you, um, just trust me on this? Just let me take your details and get it started, and then you can ring [PERSON_2] tomorrow and check it all yourself.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I'm not giving you any details. I mean, I said it before and I'll say it again, I don't know who you are, I don't know who [PERSON_2] is, and you can't even tell me which draw it was. And I just don't get why the claim would close by tomorrow if I'm the one who's won. If it's mine, it'll still be mine tomorrow, won't it? So what I'll do is, I'll ring [COMPANY_A] myself, on a number I look up, and if there's really something there, they can tell me. But I'm not starting anything over the phone with someone I don't know, that's just, no. So thanks, but I'm going to go and finish my flower bed. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, wait, please, [PERSON_1], just, um, before you go. Two turns ago, you asked me about the Christmas one, the scratch card, and whether that's how your name got in, and I said maybe, but I think what I should've said is, um, I don't actually know that part for certain. Could you tell me again what you bought at the shop, and when? Because if I have that right, I can maybe tell [PERSON_2], uh, tell them to look at it, and, and it might all make more sense when you ring back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, that's not what happened, though. I was the one who brought up the scratch card, you never asked me about it, and you didn't say maybe, you said it was useful and that's probably how my name got in. So now you don't know? That's, no, that's just another thing that's changed. Honestly, I'm not telling you what I bought or when, I've said I'm going to ring them myself, and that's that. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, wait, please don't hang up, I'm, um, I'm not trying to trick you, I just, I've got it all muddled because I'm nervous, I'm new at this and I, I really don't want you to lose out, and you've been so kind about it, honestly. Look, forget the scratch card, forget what I said, it doesn't matter how your name got there. If I, um, if I read out what's on my page, will you at least stay on the line and hear it, and then you can ring back and check?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, I've been nice about it, I know, but I'm done. First you said it was spelling, then a lottery, then two different draws, then the scratch card was useful and now it doesn't matter. I can't make that add up, and I'm not going to stand here and listen to a fourth version. If there's really something there, it'll keep, and I'll ring them myself on a number I find. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, it's [PERSON_1] from [COMPANY_A], I'm the regional supervisor, I'm calling about your order for today, and I just need to -- sorry, did I catch you mid-sentence? Anyway, it's the two-hour window we're confirming and there's one item that's been swapped, so I need a quick yes or no from you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, sorry, I just woke up from a nap... what order? I don't remember ordering anything today.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, it's the online grocery order, placed this morning, it'll be on your account. Might be worth a quick look at your email.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, there's a, uh, there's a bus going past, or no, it's the neighbour's lawnmower, it's been going all day... what was I saying? Oh, the order. Grocery, you said? I don't think I did one this morning, I was out at the, well, I was at the chemist, then I came home and lay down. And my email, I'd have to find the, the tablet, and I'm not sure where I left it. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller

Honestly, I think that's one for you to work out at your end, I can't be much help from a flowerbed. Anyway, I really must get on, so I'll say bye now. Take care, bye!
