utterances.text: Oh, no, that's fine, that's completely fine, and I'm sorry for holding you up. I'll look into how the number got on the file, I will, I'll find out and, um, and if there's anything I can tell you I'll ring you back, though honestly I'm not sure I'd have an answer. Sorry, I'll let you go, I'll let you get back to your garden. Bye now, and thank you again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no need to ring back, honestly, don't go to the trouble. Ooh, hang on, there's a blackbird right on the fence watching me dig, cheeky thing, he's after the worms. Sorry, where was I? Yes, no, just take me off the list and we're all sorted. Right, bye now, take care!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, hi. Am I speaking with -- sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm, I mean, my name's [PERSON_2], and I'm calling on behalf of the card services team at [COMPANY_A], they asked me to, well, there's a transaction that got flagged on your card and they'd like to talk to you about it. I'm not, um, I can't actually go into any of the details on this call, so I'll just be asking you to ring them back on the number printed on your card, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... right. Hm. Sorry, say that again? You're calling on behalf of the card services team, so you're not actually from [COMPANY_A] yourself? And you can't tell me anything about the transaction, just to ring the number on the card. Well, that's, I mean -- who am I speaking to, exactly, and how did you come by this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I know, I know how it sounds, I'd be suspicious too -- but I'm [PERSON_2], I'm, uh, I'm working with the card services team, I'm not the one who can see your account, that's the whole -- and the number, I mean, they gave me the number to ring, I didn't go looking for it, they just -- Look, you don't have to take my word for any of it, that's actually what I'm trying to say. Please hang up and call the number on the back of your card, not one I give you, and tell them the reference is [CODE_1]. I'll, uh, they'll keep it open for you, so there's no rush, you take whatever time you need.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. So just so I've got it straight, you're not asking me for anything, no card number, no codes, nothing like that. Just to hang up and ring the number on the back myself. Which is, I'll be honest, exactly what I'd do anyway. But I do have a couple of questions first. Who exactly is "working with" the card services team, are you an employee of [COMPANY_A], or some outside firm they've contracted? And what's the reference for, is it tied to my account or just to this call?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, nothing, I won't ask you for any of that, I wouldn't -- and that's, yeah, that's exactly right, just hang up and ring the number on the back -- Sorry, sorry, the other question. I'm, uh, I'm not an employee, I mean, I'm with an outside firm, [COMPANY_B], they do outreach for the bank, so I'm not on the bank's own staff. Um, the reference is just for this call, it isn't your account number, it's so whoever picks up at card services can see someone tried to reach you and match it up. If they can't find it straight away, that's not a, you know, a red flag on you, just tell them [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_B] rang and they'll sort it out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So an outside firm, and the reference might not even be findable at the bank. Which means if I ring the number on my card and they've never heard of any of this, I've learned nothing either way, you see. One more thing, was it your firm that flagged the transaction, or the bank? Because you said it was flagged, but you can't tell me what it was, and I'd want to know who's actually saying it's suspicious.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It was the bank that flagged it, not us, we just, we only make the calls, we don't see anything, I don't even know what the transaction was, honestly. And, uh, I did say it might not come up straight away, and that came out wrong, I'm sorry, it should be findable, [CODE_1] is logged on their side against this call. But you're right, if they've never heard of it, then that tells you something, and that's, I mean, that's fine. Then you'd know not to trust this call, and I'd rather you found that out than just took my word for it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I'll give you this, that's an oddly honest way to put it. You've asked me for nothing and you've told me to verify it myself, which is the right instruction, so I'll do that. I'll ring the number on the back of my card, not anything you've given me, and I'll see what they say. If they've got a flag on my account, fine, and if they've never heard of it, then I'll know what this call was. So, thank you, I suppose. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, yes, thank you, that's, um, that's all I'm after, honestly. Ring the number on the back of the card, quote [CODE_1], and they'll take it from there, and it'll stay open for you, so no rush at all. And, uh, sorry for the muddle earlier, I'm not very good at these calls. Goodbye, then, take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'll -- no, let me put it this way. I'll ring the number on the card myself, and I'll decide what to make of it from what they say. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's, that's exactly right, and I'd want you to. Um, one small thing, so you don't get tangled up. If you do ring and they ask who called, it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_B], and the reference is [CODE_1], that's all they'll need from you. Right. Thank you for hearing me out, I know it was a strange call to get. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on, did you say tangled up, or, uh, tangled in? Because if you're telling me I'll be caught up in something, I'd like to know what. No, never mind, I think I've got the gist of it. I'll ring the card number, I'll mention a call came in, and I'll see what they make of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, tangled up, I just meant so you wouldn't get muddled on the phone, that's all, there's nothing you're caught in, nothing at all. I'm sorry, that came out sounding worse than I meant it, I'm, uh, I'm not good at saying things plainly. Yes, ring the card number, mention a call came in, and let them take it from there. Thank you for your patience, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yes, fine, I -- sorry, hang on, there's something at the door. Right, no, it's nothing, just the post. Anyway, yes, I've got it. Ring the number on the card, tell them a call came in, and see what they say. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you, I just, yes, that's all of it. Ring the card number, tell them a call came in, quote [CODE_1], and that's us done. Goodbye, then, and thank you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, understood. I'll ring the number on the card, and I'll decide from there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling on behalf of [COMPANY_A], about your meter reading.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. Sorry, which company did you say? I didn't quite catch that. And, um, what exactly about my meter reading?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yes, [COMPANY_A]. The energy supplier. I'm, uh, not actually with them myself, I'm calling for them, for someone there. It's just that they found two readings on your account that don't match what they have, and, I mean, it's their records that are off, not anything you did. So they asked me to ring and see if you could read out the current figure on the meter, so the bill can be corrected.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, hang on. So you're not with [COMPANY_A], you're calling on their behalf, for someone there? Who exactly is that someone, and who are you with? Because that's, uh, a couple of steps removed for me. I'm not going to read out anything off a call I didn't expect, but I'd like to understand how this is meant to work. If their records are off, they'd have my account reference, so what's the account reference they're showing for me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, right, no, that's fair. I'm with [COMPANY_B], we do their, um, customer follow-ups, and the person who asked me is [PERSON_2] on the billing side. Or, sorry, it might be [PERSON_3], I've got two names here and I think I mixed them up. And I mean, I do have the account reference in front of me, it's [ACCOUNT_REF], but, uh, I'd honestly rather you didn't just take my word for it. If you'd rather, you can check it against your account online and ring [COMPANY_A] back yourself, I'm, I'm not trying to rush you into anything.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. I'll do that, then. I'll log in, check the reference, and ring [COMPANY_A] on the number on my bill. Thanks for the call.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, okay, yes, uh, that's, that's completely fine. I didn't mean to, I mean, I know it must have sounded strange, me being a step removed like that. Just so you know, the reading's all they need, nothing else, no card details or anything like that, and nothing gets changed on the account until you've checked. Maybe, um, would it be easier if I rang you back in a day or two, once you've had a chance to look into it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Well, uh, no, I'd rather you didn't ring back. If there's a genuine problem with my account, [COMPANY_A] can contact me directly, and I'll be contacting them anyway, so there's nothing left for you to follow up. Right, so, I'll leave it there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, yes. Sorry, I just, I wasn't trying to, it's only that it's their records that are off, not yours, and, uh, nothing changes until you've checked. That's all I wanted to say. Honestly. So, um, goodbye then, and sorry to have bothered you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Actually, hang on, before you go. A couple of turns back you said the reading was needed so the bill could be corrected, and then you said nothing changes on the account until I've checked. Those two don't quite fit together, do they? Which is it, that the reading corrects the bill, or that nothing's touched until I've verified? Not that it changes what I'm doing, I'll still ring them myself. But I'd like to understand what you actually meant.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, no, you're right, that came out muddled, sorry. What I should've said is, the reading is what they'd use to correct the bill, but they wouldn't actually change anything until you'd checked it's all legitimate, I mean the call, with them directly. So, uh, it's one after the other, not both at once. I think I made it sound like two things at the same time. And, um, I'm not really that practised at these calls, I'll be honest. I just, I didn't want you thinking I was hiding something.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, one after the other. Right. Sorry, hang on, there's something at the door -- no, it's just the post. Uh. Where was I? Yes, so, the order makes sense on paper, but I'm still going to ring [COMPANY_A] first, and I won't be giving a reading to anyone but them. That's not a reflection on you personally, it's just how I handle this sort of thing. Thanks for explaining, anyway. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1], I'm a regional supervisor with [COMPANY_A], the maintenance contractor -- sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a pallet out in the yard, hang on -- right, I'm back. I'm ringing about the boiler service visit you've already got booked with us, I just need to confirm the time window for the engineer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, the boiler service visit? Right, and you're, uh, from -- who was it again? I didn't quite catch the company, there's a bit of noise over here. Hmm, I mean, I do think there's something booked, but I'm at work, so, um, can you just say that again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, it's [COMPANY_A], the maintenance contractor, [PERSON_1] here, regional supervisor -- sorry, hang on, there's a lorry reversing right outside, it's got that beeper going, give me a second -- okay, it's gone. Look, it's a straightforward call, your service visit's already in our system under [ACCOUNT_REF], I'm only confirming a morning or afternoon window so the engineer can be routed properly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, [COMPANY_A], and you're saying it's under [ACCOUNT_REF], and you just want morning or afternoon. Uh, the thing is, I didn't ring you, and I can't really remember who I booked the boiler with, so I'm not sure I can just say yes to that. How would I check this is the same booking? Like, is there a number I can ring back on, or something I could look at on my end?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, yeah, that's, I mean, that's fair enough, but honestly it's a bit much for a scheduling call, isn't it? We do this for every customer, it's standard procedure, the engineer can't be routed without a confirmed window. Look, if you want to check, ring the office on [PHONE_1], that's the number on your booking confirmation, and quote the reference. Or just look at the confirmation itself, it should be in your email. I'm not asking for anything here, just morning or afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so ring the office on, uh -- no, wait, I'll just -- yeah, I'll check the confirmation first, if it's in my email. Because, I mean, you've given me the number, which is, uh, fair, but you also said it's the one on the booking, so if I look at the booking I can see if it matches, right? So I'll go and look, and if it's all there, then I'll ring the office myself and sort the window out with them. Is that, uh, is that okay with you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's, I mean, that's fine, that's exactly what you should do, look at the confirmation and match the number. I just, uh, I don't see why we couldn't have sorted it in thirty seconds, that's all, but it's your call. Ring the office when you've found it and quote the reference, they'll slot you in. I won't keep you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so I check the confirmation, match the number, and ring the office myself with the reference. Yeah, I'd rather do it that way, sorry if it's a bit of a faff. It's nothing personal, it's just I'm at work and I didn't expect the call. Okay, thanks, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's -- yeah, fine, I get it, just ring the -- right, okay. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, bye. Oh, and, uh, just so I've got it straight, you said it was a morning or afternoon window earlier, didn't you? Because now I'm thinking you said the engineer's already routed, and that doesn't quite fit, does it? Anyway, I'll sort it with the office. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say the engineer's already rooted? No, no, nobody's rooted anything, I don't know what you mean by that. I said morning or afternoon, that's all, so he can be routed -- r-o-u-t-e-d, you know, sent round. Look, I'm not going to stand here and argue about what I did or didn't say, if you'd rather ring the office, then ring the office. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. I'll ring the office. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, before you go, what was it I said two turns back that didn't sit right? You said something about the engineer being routed already, and I'm honestly not sure what you mean. But look, I'm not going to chase you over it. Ring the office, and, uh, have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, it's nothing, honestly, I probably just muddled it. Morning or afternoon, engineer gets sent round, I've got it. Like I said, I'll check the confirmation and ring the office myself. Thanks, have a good afternoon. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hello, good afternoon! Sorry, sorry, one second, someone's just wheeled a trolley right past my door and it is not quiet -- there, gone. Right, hi, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from the outpatient administration office at [COMPANY_A], and how are you doing today, anything exciting planned for the weekend?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- no, I'm not buying that, the till's -- yeah, put it on the belt, thanks. Right. Who is this? And I'm not doing small talk, I'm stood in a queue. What's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, of course, sorry, I'm a chatterbox, I'll be quick, honestly. Um, so it's [PERSON_2], outpatient administration at [COMPANY_A], and it's about a recent appointment of yours, nothing dramatic, but, uh, I can't actually go into any of it until I've confirmed I'm speaking to the right person, that's just the privacy rules on our end. So, yeah, that's really the whole reason for the call, and I can see you're in the middle of something, so is now a bad time?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, it is a bad time, I'm in a queue -- and hang on, you ring me up, you don't tell me a single thing, and then you want me to confirm who I am to you? That's backwards. What appointment? Which hospital? Because you've not said, you've just said [COMPANY_A], and I've heard that one before. Tell me what it's about or I'm putting the phone down.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair enough, you're right, it does sound backwards, and I'd think the same. It's the privacy rules, I'm just not allowed to say anything about an appointment to someone I haven't confirmed, even whether there was one. Tell you what, don't confirm anything to me. Put the phone down, ring the main switchboard at [COMPANY_A], the number's on the hospital's website or any letter you've had from us, and ask for outpatient administration and for [PERSON_2]. If it's easier, I can send a letter instead. And when you said you've heard that one before, what did you mean, someone's rung you using our name?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I know, ring the number, I heard you the first -- no, listen. What I meant is none of your business, alright? I'm not getting into it in a shop. But yeah, fine, that's the first sensible thing you've said. I'll look the number up myself, not off anything you give me, and I'll ring them if I've actually got an appointment. If I don't, I'll not bother. Right, I've got to pay, so. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's exactly right, look it up yourself and, uh, if there's no appointment on your side then honestly don't give it another -- and listen, if you do get through, just ask for me by name, [PERSON_2], and I'll, oh, you're paying, I'll let you go. Lovely, thanks, [PERSON_1], and sorry for the bother. Bye now!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what, a letter? I don't want a letter, I've had enough post off people like you. Don't send me anything. Look, I've got to pay, I said. If there's an appointment they can tell me themselves when I ring them. Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair enough, no letter, I'll make a note of that. Sorry again, bye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, before you go. Two minutes ago you said if I ring I should ask for you by name, and then something about "I'll" and you cut off. You'll what? What were you going to say? And what was that name again, I wasn't listening properly, the till's beeping at me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, yeah, sorry, I trailed off there, that was me being a chatterbox again. All I was going to say was I'll let them know to expect you. Nothing more to it. The name's [PERSON_2], and you really don't need it, though. Just ring the main switchboard for [COMPANY_A], ask for outpatient administration, and anyone there can help, so don't worry about me at all. Go on, sort your shopping, and thanks for being so patient with me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, I'm not asking for you by name, I'll ask for whoever picks up. And you don't need to let anyone know I'm coming, I'll say what it's about when I'm talking to them, off their number, not yours. Don't ring me back either. Alright, I'm paying now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, I mean, that's completely sensible, and I won't ring you back, I'll put that on the note as well. If there's an appointment, they'll, well, you'll find out when you ring them, and if there isn't, then, uh, then it's probably just a mix-up on our side and no harm done. Sorry for the faff, [PERSON_1], honestly. Enjoy the rest of your day, and good luck with the queue. Bye now!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Whatever. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bye, [PERSON_1], take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I said bye already, I'm hanging up --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with the account holder for the service address on, uh, [CITY_1]? I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], just a routine records check on the meter side of things.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, I've got a pan on. Uh, yes, I think so, I'm the one who pays the bills anyway. But I only just moved in there, well, no, sorry, it's been years, I always mix that up. Who did you say you were calling from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No trouble at all, take your time with the pan. It's [COMPANY_A], the utility provider, and I'm a verification specialist in the account integrity department. It's nothing dramatic, I'm just reconciling the service address against our billing ledger, because there's a, uh, discrepancy flag on the file. Could I just confirm I have the right household before I go on?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um... right. Sorry, what, a discrepancy? Is that bad? Hang on, let me just turn this down, it's spitting. Uh, well, you've got my address, haven't you? You're the ones who ought to know it. How do I know who you are, really? Sorry, I'm a bit all over the place.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question, and no, not at all, you're right to ask. So, the address is on our side, yes, but the discrepancy relates to the, uh, settlement reconciliation against the meter-read interval, which is why I need the account holder confirmed on the line before I can proceed. It's a standard authentication gate, nothing to be worried about. I'll just say, the flag does carry a time sensitivity, because an unresolved reconciliation can trigger a disconnection protocol, and that window is, well, it's under the hour, so I'd like to get ahead of it for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Disconnection? Sorry, what, under the hour? No, hang on, I haven't had any letter or -- I pay that, I'm sure I pay that. And you still haven't, uh, you haven't said anything I can check. What do you want from me, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, you asked a moment ago who I am, and I'd, uh, I'd rather not go round that again, because it won't change the interval. What I need is a, a remittance against the arrears, [AMOUNT_1], settled through a remote clearance channel, not the usual billing portal, because the portal posts overnight and we simply don't have the overnight. I realise that sounds irregular, but the reconciliation window closes at the top of the hour, and once the disconnection protocol is queued I can't recall it. Do you follow the sequence, or shall I run through the, the ledger logic again?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um. Uh... hang on, sorry. Not the usual portal? Why wouldn't it be the usual way? That's -- no, that doesn't sound right. I've got a pan, and you're rushing me, and I don't, I mean, I don't pay anything over the phone to someone I can't check. You still haven't told me anything I can look up. I think I'm going to ring the number on my actual bill. Sorry. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please, don't -- look, I, I understand the hesitation, I do, and ringing the number on your bill, that's, well, that's entirely your prerogative, but I'd caution that the main line can't see the flag, it sits in our, uh, our back-end reconciliation tier, so they'd only tell you the account looks standard, and by then the window... no, let me put it differently. If you just settle the [AMOUNT_1] now, through the clearance channel, I can, I can suppress the disconnection protocol myself, and then you can verify afterwards, at your leisure, with whomever you like. Can I put you down for that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. No, sorry. You've just told me the number on my own bill can't see it, and that I should pay first and check after. That's backwards, that's -- no. I'm not doing that. I'm going to ring them. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], supporters team. Uh, I'm looking at your file here and it shows your monthly gift of [AMOUNT_1] lapsed back in the spring, so I'm calling to say thank you for the support up to that point and ask whether you'd want to renew.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- no, put that down, we don't throw that. Sorry. Uh, who is this again? And, my file -- what file is that, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, it's [PERSON_2], [COMPANY_A], the charity. The file's just our supporter record, so, your name, the gift history, that sort of thing. Uh, and I said spring, but I'm reading it again and it's actually the end of last year the payment stopped, so sorry, that was my mistake. Without a renewal the gift just stays closed on our system, that's all that happens.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- no, wait. First it was spring, now it's the end of last year? I mean, that's, uh -- how do you even get that wrong if it's right there on your screen? And I'm still not sure I gave to, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? Can you tell me what the gift was actually for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, so, I read the wrong line, that's -- no, let me put it properly. The record has two dates on it, the date the gift was set up and the date it stopped, and I gave you the wrong one first. The stop date is the end of last year, that's the one that matters. Uh, as for what it was for, it's showing as general giving, not a specific appeal, so the money went to our core programmes. I can't tell you more than that from this screen. And if you don't remember giving to us, I'm happy to note that on the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. General giving. So, uh, nothing specific I'd remember it by. Right. And you're not asking me for anything today? Like, you're not taking a card number or anything, you just want to know if I'd renew?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No card number today, no. Uh, sorry, you said you'd want to know if I'd remove it? No, I'd only be asking whether you want to renew, that's the whole call. If it's a yes, the supporter line takes it from there, I don't take payment details on this call. And if it's a no, that's fine, I'll note it and that's the end of it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. I didn't say remove, I said -- never mind. So the supporter line, what, I'd ring them? Or they'd ring me? Because I'd want to look up a number myself, not use one you give me. And honestly, I don't really remember setting anything up, so I'm not going to renew something I can't place. Can you just put that on the file for me, that it's a no for now?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, noted. No renewal, and you couldn't place the gift, so it stays closed. And looking up the number yourself is fine, it's on our website, [URL_1], or on any past statement, I wouldn't ask you to use one from me. utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine, take your time, I know how that is -- is that a horn? Anyway, the event, it was the evening one, the [CITY_1] reception, you spoke with a couple of our board members near the end of the night and said you'd be glad to help, and they noted it down as [AMOUNT_1], so it's really just a matter of me confirming it with you so it doesn't fall through. I mean, you did say it out loud, and the people it's meant for are counting on that, so I'd hate for this to be the thing that slips.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, that was just a truck, I'm so sorry. Um, the reception, in [CITY_1], right? I mean, I did go to something, I think, but I don't, I really don't remember saying a number out loud to anyone. Sorry, I know that sounds terrible. And I don't want you feeling bad about not remembering, these things get said in the moment over a glass of something, which is exactly why the board wrote it down, so it's really just me closing the loop on [AMOUNT_1] so the families who were counting on it aren't left waiting.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Sorry, I just... I really don't remember agreeing to that. Could you maybe send me something in writing, and I'll look at it when I'm not driving?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, yeah, in writing, of course, and we'll get that over, but honestly the records from the evening are confidential, I can't send out the board's notes, so a letter wouldn't really show you anything more than what I'm telling you right now. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, I don't think so. If I can't see anything in writing, then no, I can't confirm that today. I'm sorry. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, wait, wait, before you go, it's [PERSON_2] at [COMPANY_A], scheduling, calling about the pledge from the [CITY_1] reception, and I just need to confirm it today, that's really all it is, [AMOUNT_1], that's the number the board has down. I know I can't show you the notes, they're confidential, but the pledge was made, it was said out loud, and the families are counting on it, so I'm only asking you to say yes and I'll sort the rest.

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, someone's just walked in with a delivery, one second -- no, put it on the desk, thanks -- okay, I'm back. Right, so, [PERSON_2], [COMPANY_A], and look, you've told me twice now you don't remember, and that's completely fine, but honestly I think you did say it, and I'd feel awful if the families heard it fell through over something as small as paperwork, so can we just call it confirmed at [AMOUNT_1] and I'll worry about the rest?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. I can't, I really can't just say yes to something I don't remember. And I'm sorry about the families, I am, but I'm not going to confirm it like this. Please don't call about this again unless there's something in writing. Goodbye.

utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], I'm the regional supervisor, I was out at yours last week about the bathroom tiling. Can you tell me what address you've got down for the job, because if it's the wrong house I'd rather know now?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, no upstairs bathroom? Okay, that's -- right, that might be me getting my notes crossed, I do a few of these a week. As for my name, it's, uh, I'm one of several specialists on the queue, and the individual designation isn't really material to the process, it's the record that matters, so if we could just do the one confirmation, it's a matter of seconds, honestly --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh huh. So you won't give me a name, and the, the cut-off's coming, and I just say yes to whatever you read out. No, I'm not doing that. If it's real, I'll ring [COMPANY_A] myself.

utterances.speaker: caller

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that's a fair thing to ask. It's the national tax office, [COMPANY_A], and I do understand why you'd want that pinned down before we go any further. utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.text: No, I think you're right, it does sound backwards, and I'm glad you said so. I'd rather you were a little suspicious than not. utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, I mean, that's a perfectly reasonable question, [PERSON_1], and what we, what happens is the file holds the data at rest, and the validation is a, a dual-factor cross-match against what you state live, so it isn't that we lack the details, it's that the protocol requires them to be, uh, corroborated by the account holder on the call. It's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a solicitor's office, we handle estates, and I'm, uh, a claims assessor here, sort of an assistant on the team really.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you. Who's speaking, though? You've given me a name and a company, but I didn't catch what it is you're actually calling about. And before we go any further, how did you come by this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, sorry, I should've led with that. So it's, um, an estate we're handling, and your name has come up as someone who may be named in it. May. I can't say more than that over the phone at this stage, there's a formal letter going out to you, and it's, uh, a confidential matter until that arrives, so I'd ask you not to discuss it with anyone just yet. As for the number, I'd have to, hang on, let me see where it's listed -- it's, um, it came off the file, I'll have to check which record exactly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said a formal letter is going out, and that I shouldn't discuss it with, with anyone, fine. But what was the word you used for the thing I'm named in? An estate, or an estimate? Because if it's an estimate, I haven't asked anyone for a quote on anything. And I'm a bit stuck on the number. You said it came off the file, but you can't tell me which record. So which file is that, and whose? If I'm only maybe named in someone's estate, I'd expect you to be able to say whose it is, or at least which firm's name is on the letter.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Estate, yes, an estate, not an estimate, sorry, I can see how that came across. Like a person's estate, after they've passed. And the firm is [COMPANY_A], that's the name that'll be on the letter, we're in [CITY_1], and honestly, please don't take my word for it. Look us up in a proper directory, not anything I give you, and ring the main number listed there and ask for me, [PERSON_2]. Um, as for whose estate, I'm, hang on, I'm not sure I'm meant to name the deceased before the letter goes out, I'd have to check that with the solicitor. And I'm not asking you for any money or bank details or anything like that, at any point, just so that's clear. All I'd need today is for you to confirm your full name and the address you'd want the letter sent to, which is what the letter will already carry anyway.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so I'll look the firm up myself, that's sensible, and I will. But hang on, you said the letter will already carry my name and address, so if you've got that on file you don't need me to confirm it, do you? Why ask me to say it out loud? And you can't tell me whose estate it is, but you want my details first. That's, I mean, that's the wrong way round, isn't it? I'd want the deceased's name, or the solicitor's name, or a reference for the matter, something I can quote when I ring that main number. Do you have a reference?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um, yeah, no, that's fair, that, that is a fair point, I mean, the file does have a name and an address, it's just, uh, we need to be sure it's the right [PERSON_1] before anything goes out, there could be more than one, so that's, that's why I asked. But you don't have to say anything, honestly, if you'd rather wait for the letter. A reference, right, hang on, let me, uh, pull that up, I thought it was on this screen but it's, um -- is it [ACCOUNT_REF]? No, sorry, that's the old format, that's, hmm, I'd really have to check that one with the solicitor, I don't want to read you the wrong one. And the solicitor's name, that I should have, it's, um, I'm sorry, I've just, I've gone blank on it, which is embarrassing. [PERSON_3], I think? I'll confirm it, so that you've got something right to quote when you ring.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, but that's still the same problem. You've got a name and an address on file, you say, but you want me to confirm them. And you can't give me a reference, you can't give me the deceased's name, and you've gone blank on the solicitor, though now it's maybe [PERSON_3]. That's, I mean, that's three things I could quote when I ring that number, and I've got none of them. So I'm not confirming my name or my address today. Not on this call. If a letter does arrive, I'll look the firm up myself and ring the main number, like you said. I don't mean to be rude. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's, hang on, someone's just put a folder down on my desk, sorry -- no, you're right. You're completely right, and you're not being rude at all. Please don't confirm anything, wait for the letter. But before you go, the reference and the solicitor's name, those I should've had ready, so let me find out properly and call you back with them, rather than guess at it. Would that be alright, or would you rather I didn't ring at all?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'd rather you didn't ring at all, no. If there's a letter, it'll have the reference and the solicitor's name on it, and I'll deal with it that way, through the number I find myself. So no callback, please, and no need to note anything down on my account. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, yes, understood, no callback, I'll make a note of that on the file straight away, uh, that you'd rather not be rung, and that nothing's been confirmed on your side. And I do want to say, I'm sorry, this should have gone better than it did. I rang without the reference to hand and without the solicitor's name settled in my head, and that's on me, not on you, because anyone getting a call like this ought to be given something they can check, and you weren't, really. So what I'd say is, if the letter comes, it'll be on the firm's headed paper with a reference at the top, and the sensible thing is exactly what you've said, look [COMPANY_A] up in an independent directory, ring the main number listed there, and quote whatever's on the letter. And if no letter turns up, then, um, well, that tells you something too, and you've lost nothing by hanging up. I'm sorry again for the muddle, and thank you for hearing me out as long as you did. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Thank you for saying that. I'll do exactly what I said, and if nothing arrives, I'll leave it there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Thank you, that's, yes, that's all I'd ask. Take care, then. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, take care. And just so we part on a clear note, I'm not being unfriendly. It's only that in my line of work, an unsolicited call asking me to confirm who I am before the caller can tell me anything checkable is a pattern I've learned to stop at, whatever the intentions are. If a letter does come, with a reference and a solicitor's name on it, I'll go through the directory, ring the main number, and quote it, and if it all lines up, I'll deal with it properly from there. If it doesn't, then nothing's lost on either side. So, no callback, nothing confirmed, and I'll wait on the post. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, it's me. Listen, I need you to stay calm and just tell me you know who this is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, who's this? You said "it's me" but I -- I don't actually know the voice. And hang on, why would I be calm, has something happened? Hold on, one second, [PERSON_1], put that down please -- sorry, go on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I don't have time for a guessing game. Just say the name, you know who I am, it's me. And I didn't say anything had happened, I said stay calm, that's -- that's different. Something's come up, that's all, and I need you to listen without asking me a string of questions.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, hang on, I'm not saying a name. You say who you are, because I honestly don't -- and "stay calm" is exactly what you say when something's wrong, so which is it? And why can't I ask questions? Why would that be a --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. It's a security matter, it's with [COMPANY_A], and it's not something I'm going to go through on an open line. I'm asking you to trust me on this, and I need it handled today. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but that's, I mean, that's a lot of things you've just said and none of them are an answer. You still haven't told me who you are. First it was "it's me," now it's "trust me," and I don't even know who I'm supposed to be trusting. And a security matter with [COMPANY_A], well, why would that be something you can't talk about on the phone, when you're the one who rang me? If it's that serious, surely there's a proper way to do this, like I ring [COMPANY_A] back on a number I already have, or you tell me something only the real person would know. Because honestly, we had a thing in the family last year, someone got caught out, and I'm not going to say more than that, but it's made me a bit, uh, guarded about anyone who says it's urgent and then won't explain. So what exactly do you need handled today? What would I even be doing?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh -- look. I'm not here to be interrogated. I'm telling you this is a matter that carries consequences if it isn't dealt with today, and every minute you spend asking about my name is a minute lost. I'm not going to repeat myself. You're asked to cooperate, that's all, so are you going to cooperate or not?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], no, not on the sofa, off. Off, please. Sorry, sorry, I'm back. Right, so, cooperate with what? You still haven't said what you actually want me to do. And "consequences if it isn't dealt with today", what consequences, from who? Because I'm sorry, but I'm not agreeing to anything when you won't tell me your name or what it is. So no, I'm not going to cooperate with something I can't even see. I'll ring [COMPANY_A] myself on the number I already have, and if it's real, they'll tell me. Okay? Right, I'm going to go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I wouldn't, no. That's not -- I'd advise against ringing anyone, it'll only slow things down, and nobody there is going to know about this. Look, if you hang up, that's on you, I've given you the chance to -- hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, [PERSON_1], that's hot, don't touch -- sorry, I'm here, I'm still here. But no, that's, uh, that's not helping you. You just told me not to ring them, and that nobody there will know about it. Why would that be? If it's a real matter with [COMPANY_A], they'd be the very people who'd know. So no. I'm going to ring them on the number I already have, and I'm not doing anything today because you've told me to. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Do what you want.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what, "do what you want," did you say do what I want, or, hang on, did you say "do what you wan' -- " no, wait, is that, are you saying something about a warrant? Because that's, I mean, that's a different thing entirely, who said anything about a warrant? You haven't said a word about one. No, you know what, I'm done. I'm ringing [COMPANY_A] on the number I already have. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I said do what you want, not warrant, there's no warrant, I never said that. Look, two turns ago you asked what I needed, and I said it needed handling today. That's what I meant, today, and I can't go into more than that. I'm not trying to trick you, I just, I can't be seen to be discussing it like this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, "I can't be seen to be discussing it" -- seen by who? That's a strange thing to say, isn't it? And two turns ago, hang on, what was it you actually said? Something about it needing handling today, but handling what? You never said what the "it" is. You said a security matter, you said [COMPANY_A], and that's all. So what is the thing that needs handling? Because I'm still not clear what you're even asking me to do.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I've told you what I can tell you. It's a matter that needs handling today, and I'm not going to put the particulars on an open line, that's all there is to it. If you want to ring [COMPANY_A], go ahead, but don't expect me to be around when you do. I've done what I was asked to do on this end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you've done what you were "asked" to do? Asked by who? No wait, hang on, [PERSON_1], not the cupboard, come here. Sorry. So somebody asked you to ring me, is that it? Who? Because you've still not told me a name, not yours, not theirs, and I'm not doing anything on the say-so of someone I can't even put a name to. You've given me nothing I can check. So no. I'm going to ring [COMPANY_A] on the number I already have, and if there's really a matter, they can tell me themselves. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a fulfilment verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], the supermarket home-delivery service. I'm calling to confirm the two-hour delivery window on the order you placed online, and, uh, just to flag that one line item has undergone a like-for-like substitution at the pick-and-pack stage.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- no, I'm not buying that, the lad in front's got a trolley across the whole... sorry. Who? Company what? I'm standing in a supermarket, I haven't got a delivery on, so what order are you on about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, my apologies, I can hear you're mid-shop, so let me simplify that. It's [PERSON_2], calling from [COMPANY_A], the home-delivery service. We have an online order under this number for a delivery today, and if that's not one you recall placing, that may well be a mix-up on our side, or possibly someone else's order with your number attached, uh, from a contact-record perspective. I'm not asking you for anything other than a yes or no on one substitution, so if it's not your order, just say so and I'll flag the record for review.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but -- no. I didn't place an order, so that's your yes or no, it's a no. And I don't, I mean, why would you even... how'd you get this number? Because I've had people ringing me with a story before, and it always starts with something small like this, so what's the catch here?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a tray of something behind me, uh, right, I'm back. No catch at all, honestly. The number would have been entered in the contact field when the order was created, which is a manual-entry step on the customer side, so a mistyped digit can attach a stranger's mobile to the record, and I think that's what's happened here, because the order sits under a different name. It's a routine record-validation call, and, I mean, I haven't asked you for anything, no payment, no details, nothing. I'll flag the contact field as erroneous and that should stop any further calls to you about it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I, no, hang on. If it's under a different name, then why are you even ringing me and asking if I'm, uh -- you rang up and said my name first, didn't you? You said [PERSON_1], so it's not a different name, is it? Or, I mean, which is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's a fair catch, and I should have been clearer. When I said [PERSON_1], I was only checking who I'd reached, which is how we open a verification call. The order itself sits under a different customer name, which is why I'm treating it as a likely mistyped contact field. Sorry, that wasn't well explained. Look, you've got no reason to take my word for any of it, so if you'd rather, you can look up [COMPANY_A]'s customer line yourself and ring in to check.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I, no -- hang on. That's, uh, I mean, that's what they all say, isn't it, ring the number yourself. Except, hmm, it's actually not a bad... no, look. I didn't order anything, so it's not mine, and I'm not telling you anything else, and I'll sort out the rest myself if I want to. So you just, yeah, you flag your record and that's us done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, and that's completely reasonable. Do ring the customer line yourself, using a number you've looked up independently, if you'd like to check anything at all. I'll flag that contact field now, so you shouldn't hear from us again about it. Sorry for the interruption, and enjoy the rest of your shop. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, right. Well, if I get another one of these, I'll know, won't I. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, hello. Is this, um, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling, I'm sort of calling on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], the vehicle warranty people, and it's about your car's coverage, which is, uh, about to lapse.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who -- hang on, I just woke up, I was having a little lie down. Which car, because I've only got the one, and it's, uh, it's not even that old, my sister says it's the green one, but anyway --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, I didn't mean to, uh, wake you. That's, I feel terrible. Um, so the car, yes, the one you've got, the, uh, well, I don't have the make right in front of me, but the, the file says it's due today, the renewal, and I'd hate for you to be, you know, left with nothing if something happened on the road.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Due today? Hang on, hang on, I just, I don't, you said you don't have the make, so how do you know it's my car? Because it's the green one, I said, the green one, and you don't even know what it is. And who did you say you were again? Company, something, A? I was half asleep, I didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, no, I'm not, I'm not saying it's a green one, I mean, I wouldn't know the color, that's not, that's not on my sheet. And I'm, uh, I'm [PERSON_2], calling for [COMPANY_A], well, for someone there, I'm just, I'm helping out. I really didn't mean to upset you, I just, I know it's hard to be woken up and I wouldn't want you to lose your coverage over, over a nap.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not upset, I'm just, I'm tired, that's all. But going back, you said the file says it's due today, the renewal, and then you said you don't have the make in front of you. So what file is that, if it hasn't got the car on it? And I've never, I don't think I've ever had a warranty with, uh, with whoever you said, because the car came with whatever it came with. My sister would know. She does all that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um, the file, it's, it's the renewal file, it's just, uh, it doesn't have the make on my screen, that's all, it's, the details are with the, with the other person at [COMPANY_A]. And I mean, you wouldn't have to have bought it from us, that's not, it just carries over, so it's still due today, it's still due today, and I'd really hate for you to be stuck, you know, if something happened and your sister had to, to deal with that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, that doesn't make sense though, does it? How does something carry over if I never signed up for it? And you keep saying it's due today but you can't tell me one thing about the car, not the make, not anything. So what are you actually wanting from me? Because I'm not, I'm not doing anything today, I've only just got up. If it's real, then, uh, the company can post me something and I'll show my sister. How would I even check you're who you say? Is there a number I can ring that's not just, you know, you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, a number, right, well, that's, I mean, I understand why you'd ask, that's, that's fair. It's just, the line I'm on is, it's an internal line, so it's not one that, that takes calls from outside, and the, uh, the person at [COMPANY_A] would be the one to ring you back, they, they usually do that, same day, or, or around then, I couldn't say exactly when. And the post thing, I, I don't think that'd work, because it's, it's the confirming today that matters, once it lapses, it's, it's sort of harder to, to get back, and I'd feel awful, honestly, if you were out on the road and, and nothing was covering you, and your sister, she'd, she'd be worried too, wouldn't she, and I just, I don't want to be the one who, who didn't ring you in time, you know?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hmm. No, see, that's, that's the bit that's put me off, if I'm honest. You can't give me a number, you can't tell me the car, it's all got to be today, and now my sister's being brought into it. I only mentioned her once. If it's a real thing, it'll still be real tomorrow, and I'll ring the number on whatever paperwork I've got, or my sister will. So I'm going to leave it there, love. Sorry. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, wait, please, I, I wasn't bringing your sister in, I only, well, you said she does all that, and, and I didn't mean anything by it. And it's, um, it's not really today, I mean it is, but it's, it's more like by end of the week, sort of, I, I got that wrong, sorry. I just, I'm not, I'm only trying to help here, and now I feel like I've, like you think I'm, I'm up to something, which, that's, that's quite hurtful, honestly, when I only rang to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Now it's the end of the week, though, isn't it? A minute ago it was today. That's, no, that's the second time the story's changed, and I've only been up ten minutes. I'm not saying you're a bad person, I just, I don't know you, and you can't tell me one thing about the car. So I'm going to ring off now and sort it with my sister. Bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, but, I wasn't, it's not that the, I mean, the date is, it's more of a, no. Sorry, let me, I only meant that the, that the, uh -- Right. I, I don't have that in front of me, I'm sorry. I'll, um, I'll pass it on, and someone will, will be in touch. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, all right. I wouldn't ring back, though, if I were you. If it's real, I'll hear about it in the post and my sister will deal with it. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, sorry, one second. Two turns ago, you said the green one, it's your sister who says it's green, is that right? And, um, is it her car, or yours, because that, that sort of changes who I'd, who they'd, uh --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not going into that. I've said bye twice now. It's my car, the one I've got, and that's all you're getting. If it's real, it'll come in the post, I'll show my sister, and that's the end of it. I'm not telling you anything else about her or the car. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: But if you'd just let me, if I could just, I only need the one, uh, the registration, or even just the, no, hang on, I, I can't, that's not, I don't have the, the number for you to ring, and I, I don't know when anyone would, um -- sorry. I've got to go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, no, I'm not giving you a registration, you've no business asking for that. And you've got no number for me to ring, so, that's that. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi [PERSON_1], it's [PERSON_2] calling from the outpatient administration office at [COMPANY_A]. Uh, I'm ringing about your recent appointment with us, nothing to worry about, but before I can go into any of the details I just need to confirm a couple of identity bits with you first, it'll only take a minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Speaking, yeah. Sorry, who? Outpatient admin at what, exactly? I've got about two minutes. What's this about, and what's the appointment?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no problem, [PERSON_1], I'm [PERSON_2], outpatient administration at [COMPANY_A], the hospital. Um, here's the thing, I can't actually say what the appointment was about until I've confirmed I'm talking to the right person, privacy rules, you know how it is. So all I'd need is a quick confirmation of a couple of details, and then I can tell you everything.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, see, that's backwards. You rang me. You tell me what the appointment was, which clinic, what date, and then I'll decide if it's mine. I'm not confirming anything to a number I don't know. And what's the hospital called, actually? You've said hospital twice and not given me a name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I hear you, [PERSON_1], and honestly that's fair, a lot of people say the same. It's just that I'm not allowed to say anything about the clinic or the date until the identity check's done, that's the rule on our side, it's not me being awkward. The hospital's [COMPANY_A], that's the full name. But look, it's only a couple of quick questions, takes no time at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. No. Then ring me back once you've got something you can actually tell me. I'm not doing it this way. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, yeah, that's, I mean, I'm not going to -- look, [PERSON_1], if you'd rather check me out first, that's completely fine. Ring the [COMPANY_A] switchboard yourself, ask for outpatient administration, and they can confirm I rang. Or I can send you a letter instead. No pressure at all, you take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, someone's just waved at me through the glass, I've got to -- right. Yeah. Look, I'll look up the number myself, not one you give me. If it's real, they'll have a record of it. Letter's fine, whatever. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, sorry, someone's just come in with a trolley, bit of a racket here. No, that's exactly right, [PERSON_1], look the number up yourself, that's the sensible thing, and I'll get a letter sent out to the address we've got on file. Take care, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, fine, right, but don't send anything till I've checked it, I'm not -- no. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, right, no, of course, [PERSON_1], I'll hold off on the letter until you've had a chance to check with the switchboard, that's no trouble at all. Um, anyway, I'll let you go, you take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, one thing. Two turns back you said a letter to the address you've got on file. Which address? Read it to me, because if you've got one for me I want to know what it is. Actually no, don't, I'll check it with them. Just tell me which department's name to ask for, exactly, so I'm not getting passed around.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, I won't read an address out, same privacy thing, and you're right to ask about it. Ask the switchboard for outpatient administration at [COMPANY_A], that's the exact department name, and if they ask who rang, say [PERSON_2]. They'll be able to tell you whether a call went out today and what number it came from. And honestly, if they can't find any record of it, then just leave it, no harm done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, got it, outpatient administration, [PERSON_2]. If they've got no record, I'll assume you're not who you said. Right, that's me done, I'm not going back and forth on this. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said you're not going back to the record on this? No, no, [PERSON_1], please do check, that's what I'd want you to do. Ring the switchboard, ask for outpatient administration, and if there's nothing logged, fair enough, you carry on with your day. I won't ring again till you've had the chance. Take care, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Right. I'll check. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller

Because I'm not going to confirm an address to someone who rang me, I'd need to know who you are first.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, understood, and that's fair. So I'm with [COMPANY_A], account services, records department, and this is a routine address verification. It's standard procedure, nothing on your account needs attention. I do just need a yes or no on whether you're still at the address on file, and like I said, we're closing out the batch at four.

utterances.speaker: receiver

If it's genuinely routine, then it can wait while I ring the number printed on my own paperwork. So what's the reference on this account, and what's your name?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, I'm not able to read out account references over an outbound call, that's, that's part of the verification procedure. And my name, it's, uh, [PERSON_1], records department. Look, all I'm asking is whether you're still at the address on file, and the batch does close at four.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So, to be clear, you can't tell me which account this is, and you won't give me a reference, but you do want me to confirm an address. That's, uh, that's backwards, isn't it? utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, that's, that's absolutely fine, you're entirely within your rights, and I'd never push anyone to confirm anything they're not comfortable with. Like I said, it's a routine records exercise, and if the address on file is wrong or out of date, it'll simply get picked up in the next cycle, so there's no harm done on your end whatsoever. You're welcome to ring the number on your own paperwork if that's what you'd prefer, and, uh, I'll just make a note on my side that you declined. Right, I'll let you go. Have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you'll make a note that I what? Declined to be "arrested"? No, sorry, that can't be what you said. Say that again, please, because I'd like to be certain what exactly goes on a record with my name against it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not arrested, I said declined, as in declined to confirm. That's all it is, a note that the verification wasn't completed on the call. Sorry, one second, there's, uh, someone at my desk -- right, I'm back. It's just a line in the file, nothing more than that. Anyway, you've been very clear, so I'll leave it there. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, I'll, uh -- no. Look, a note saying I declined to confirm, that's fine, I've got no objection to that. What I'd, what I'd want is for that company to tell me itself, through the number on my own paperwork, not through you. And I'd still like it noted that you never gave me an account reference. utterances.text: Oh, hello, good afternoon, um, sorry to trouble you. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Um, yeah, I'm here. I've got a pan on, so, who's calling again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, [PERSON_1], from the records department at [COMPANY_A]. Hang on one second, sorry, someone's just come past my desk, um -- right, sorry, I'm back. I can be very quick.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the pan's fine, I've just turned it down a bit, it's only onions, so, yeah. Sorry, but, um, which company did you say? I didn't quite catch it, the extractor fan's going and I've got the radio on in the other room, I keep, I mean, I'm not very good on the phone at the best of times. And records for what, exactly? utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, please don't apologise, that's perfectly fair, I'd want to know too. It's [COMPANY_A], the records department, sorry, I know I said it quite fast. It's only that one thing, I just need to confirm you're still living at the address we have, and then I'll let you get back to your onions.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, yes, I'm still here, sorry. Just, uh, stirring. Hang on. But, sorry, you still haven't really said, have you? Which company is it? And if you've got my address, why do you need me to tell you it? Wouldn't you just read it out to me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's a very fair question, and I'm sorry, I'm not explaining it well at all. Um, it's [COMPANY_A], that's the name, the records department, and I'm [PERSON_1], I'm a case handler. utterances.text: Hang on, a parsnip? Did you say a parsnip? No, I'm, I don't have anything to do with, sorry, I think that line went a bit funny. So the reference is the tracking number, and the charge only goes through the tracking page, not through you. Right. I'll check my messages later, and if there's nothing in them, I'm not doing anything. Okay, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Um, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? ... Thank you. My name is [PERSON_2], I'm a compliance officer at [COMPANY_A], the tenancy deposit protection scheme. I'm calling about a pending matter connected to your tenancy, and, well, before I say more, I'd just like to check that now is an alright time to talk.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Um, sorry, what? ... Yeah, that's me. I'm just, I've got a pan on, so, sort of cooking. Tenancy deposit, did you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Tenancy deposit protection, [COMPANY_A]. Look, go and see to your pan, it's no trouble, I can hold, or I can ring back later this evening if that's easier.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, it's fine, I've just turned it down, I can -- sorry, what's it actually about? Is something wrong with my deposit? Because I thought that was all sorted, I mean --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, thank you, and please don't be alarmed, because nothing is wrong with your deposit as such. What's happened is that a dispute has been raised on a tenancy at the address, and I'd like to be careful here, because I'm not saying it's your dispute, or that it involves you personally, only that the scheme has a pending matter connected to the property, and that part of my job is to contact the people who live there so that, uh, the process is run properly and nobody is surprised later. Now, the one thing I do need to ask, and I'll explain why in a moment, is that you keep the details of it private from the other tenants until both sides have been formally notified, and that's, um, that's really the heart of why I'm ringing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, the pan's spitting, sorry -- one second. Right. Sorry, what? Keep it private? Private from who, my housemates? I don't, I don't really know what you're on about. Whose dispute is it, if it's not mine?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, I understand why that sounds strange, and I'm glad you asked it straight out, because you're entitled to ask. So, the housemates, yes, the other tenants at the address. The reason is a procedural fairness one. When a dispute is open, the scheme has to notify both sides formally, in writing, at the same time, so that neither the landlord nor the tenant who raised it has been pre-empted, pressured, or talked round by anyone else in the house before they've had their proper notice. If word gets about informally first, it can compromise the process, and in some cases we have to restart it, which helps nobody. That's all the confidentiality is. It isn't about keeping anything from you, and I'd rather not name whose dispute it is over the phone, uh, because I haven't yet verified that you're the right person to receive that, and I'd be doing the very thing I'm asking you not to. What I can do is send exactly what I've just said to you in writing, with a case reference, and you can check that reference on the scheme's official website, at [URL_1], before you do anything at all. And, to be plain, nothing is lost if you'd prefer not to continue now. There's no particular rush on your part, though the notifications do need to go out in good time, so the sooner it's all settled the better, really.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I've lost the thread a bit. Two minutes ago you said you needed to check I'm the right person, before you could say whose dispute it is. But you rang me. So how, um, how did you not already know that? And you said something about me not being surprised later, what did you mean by that? Surprised by what?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, right, well, no, I wouldn't say I rang you without knowing who you were, uh, I have your name and the address from the tenancy record, that's why I asked if you were [PERSON_1]. What I haven't confirmed is whether you're the named tenant on the deposit or one of the other occupiers, and that does matter, because the notification goes to the named parties only. And you said you've been, sorry, sort of cooking surprises? No, no, I think I heard that wrong, you asked what I meant by surprised. Well, I only meant that nobody should hear about a dispute from a housemate before the formal letter reaches them, that's all. And, um, I'd welcome this, honestly, if you're uneasy, then please do look us up yourself, on [URL_1], and ring the main line from there instead of anything I give you. Quote the case reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and they'll confirm I'm who I say I am, and ring me straight back through the switchboard. There's no harm in that at all, and I'd rather you did it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, no, I didn't say anything about cooking surprises, I think you've -- hang on. So you've got my name, you've got the address, but you don't know if I'm the one on the deposit? Sorry, what? I mean, I am, I think. I'm on the agreement. But if I tell you that, what happens then? Because you still haven't said what you actually want from me. You just keep saying don't tell anyone.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yes, no, you're right, I did muddle that, you never said anything about cooking surprises, that was me mishearing, I apologise. And you're right on the other point too, I've gone round the houses, so let me be plain. What I want from you is very little. Nothing today, in fact. No money, no codes, no details read out to me. If you are on the agreement, all that happens is the formal notice goes to you in writing, and the only thing I'm asking in the meantime is that you don't discuss it with the others in the house until that notice has landed. That's it, really. Um, and I'd rather not take your confirmation over the phone at all, now that I think about it, since you've only just heard from me. So the better route is the one you're edging towards. Look up the scheme yourself, find the main number, not anything I give you, and ring them. Quote [ACCOUNT_REF], and they'll tell you whether I'm who I say I am. I'll be at my desk, and nothing's lost by waiting.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. Okay, that's, yeah, that's a bit more sensible, sorry. But hang on, you said earlier you'd send it in writing with a reference, and now you're saying I ring them with the reference. Which is it? And I never said I was edging towards anything, I've just got a pan going and I'm lost. Oh, and you said you'd ring back this evening, but now you're at your desk. Sorry, I don't mean to be rude. I just, I'd feel better looking it up myself first. I'll find the number on my own, I won't use anything you've said. Is that alright?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely alright, and you're not being rude at all, you're doing exactly the right thing. And to answer you fairly, it's both. The written notice comes to you either way, and the reference is there so you can check me independently, so no, those two things don't conflict, though I did explain it clumsily. On the other point, I did say I could ring back this evening, and then I said I'd be at my desk, and that was untidy of me, so just ignore that. Don't wait for me to ring you. Find the number yourself, on the scheme's own site, ring whenever suits you, and if they can't match what I've told you to a record, then please don't go any further with it. I'd rather lose the call than have you uneasy. Go and see to your dinner, [PERSON_1], and thank you for being so careful about it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Okay. Sorry, one thing though, and then I'll let you go. Two turns back you said it's not about keeping anything from me, it's about the others, the housemates. But you also said you wouldn't tell me whose dispute it is. So I've got a secret I'm meant to keep that I don't even know the content of? Sorry, what? That's still a bit odd to me. Anyway, I'm going to look the scheme up myself and ring them, and if it's real they'll tell me. Thanks. I need to see to my pan. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, uh, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is -- well, my name is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the [COMPANY_A] public library, I work in, uh, compliance, which sounds rather grander than it is. I'm ringing because -- no, let me put that differently. A book you reserved with us last week has come in, and we're holding it for you at the front desk.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, this is [PERSON_1], sorry, I'm just out in the garden, you've caught me with my hands in the dirt, I've got you on speaker so if there's a bit of a rustle that's just me and the roses. A book, oh that's nice, which one is it, do you know? I put in for a couple of things last week, I think, so I'm not sure which one's come in first.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, roses, lovely, I'll try not to keep you from them for long. Now, uh, I don't have the title in front of me, actually -- I'm calling from the compliance side rather than the lending desk, so what I can see is the notice that a reserved item has arrived against your card. If you pop in, the staff at the front desk will have it set aside with your name on it, and they can tell you precisely which one it is, and whether the other is still on its way. I do want to say, it's a perfectly ordinary notice, nothing to be concerned about. It's just that, well, items on the hold shelf can't sit there indefinitely, you understand, so it's best not to leave it too long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's fine, I'll pop in, I'm in town on Thursday anyway. Sorry, can I just go back a second though, you said you're from compliance, and I didn't quite catch what that means for a library? Like, what do you actually do over there? I'd have thought it'd just be the lending desk ringing about a book, so I'm just curious why it comes from you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm glad you asked, truly, it's a fair thing to wonder, and I'd much rather you ask than just wonder about it. So, uh, compliance at a library is, well, mostly the unglamorous side of things. Making sure we handle borrower records properly, that holds and reservations are processed the way our policies say they should be, that sort of thing. And, I mean, our lending desk has been rather stretched lately, so a few of us in the back office have been taking on the courtesy calls to help out. That's really all it is here. Now, I won't keep you from the roses much longer. Thursday would be perfectly all right, I'd say, it's, uh, well within the time we'd expect. You needn't bring anything special, just your library card, and the desk will sort the rest.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, so it's a bit of a back office thing, that makes sense. Sorry, did you say I need to bring a special card? Because I've got my library card, but I'm not sure where it's got to, it might be in my other coat, I'll have a look. Is it a different one for reserved books, or is it just the normal one? Honestly, I've got that many cards in my purse, I never know which is which.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, a special car -- no, no, sorry, I think we've got our wires crossed there, there's no car involved at all, I wouldn't ask you to drive anywhere you weren't already going! I think what you heard, or what I may have said badly, was just the library card, the ordinary one, nothing different for reserved books. And if it's in the other coat, well, that's no trouble, the desk can look you up by name if it comes to that. I'd hate for you to turn the house upside down over it, so, uh, please don't worry on that score.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I said card, not car, but never mind. Right, so just the ordinary one, or my name. Thursday, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, yes, card, quite right, my apologies, I misheard you entirely. Thursday is lovely. Now, one thing, and I may have put this poorly earlier, I said the desk would have it set aside, which is true, but I should be clearer that they'll hold it for ten days from now, not indefinitely, so Thursday sits comfortably inside that. And, uh, I also said it might be a bit stretched at the desk, but I wouldn't want you thinking it's a long wait, it's usually quite quick.
