So, ordinary card or just your name, and the book will be waiting. Enjoy the roses, [PERSON_1], and thank you for being so patient with me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Lovely, thank you! Oh, but hang on, going back a bit, you said you couldn't see which book it is, just that there's a notice against my card, but then how did you know it was reserved last week? I mean, I did put them in last week, so you're right, I'm just wondering what the notice actually shows you. Is it the date, or my name, or what? Sorry, I'm only asking because I can't remember if I put two in or three, and I'd like to know what to expect when I turn up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, no, that's a perfectly sensible thing to ask, and I'm glad you did, because it's exactly the sort of detail that ought to add up. So, uh, what the notice shows me is quite limited, really. It gives the date the reservation was placed, your name, and the fact that one item has come in against it. Not the title, which is why I couldn't say which book it is. So I can tell you that one has arrived, but as to whether it was two you put in, or three, I honestly couldn't say, and I wouldn't want to guess and have you turn up expecting the wrong thing. The desk will see the full picture, titles and all, so they can tell you what's here and what's still to come. Right, well, I think that's everything from me. Thursday, ordinary card or just your name, and it'll be waiting. Goodbye for now, [PERSON_1], and do enjoy those roses.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, lovely, thanks. Oh, sorry, one more thing before you go, and I'm probably being daft. A couple of turns back you said the desk is stretched and you lot in the back office have been doing the courtesy calls, and then you said it's usually quite quick. Which is it? Is it busy and I should expect a queue on Thursday, or is it quick? I only ask because I'm popping in between a few other bits and I'd like to know whether to leave myself a bit of time.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're not being daft at all, and it's a fair thing to point out, because I did say both, didn't I? Let me untangle it. The desk is a bit short-handed, which is why we in the back office are making these calls, but collecting a held book is a quick job, a minute or two once you're at the front. So it's quick, though, uh, I can't promise there won't be someone ahead of you. If you're fitting it in between other things, I'd leave yourself ten minutes or so, and that should be plenty. And to say it once more, so it's clear, the book is held for ten days, Thursday is well inside that, and it's just your card or your name. So, I think that's us, [PERSON_1]. Thank you for your patience, and enjoy the roses.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ten minutes, grand, that's easy enough. Right, well, thank you for ringing, that's very kind of you, and I'll see you, well, the desk, on Thursday with my card, or my name if the card's still in the other coat. Bye now, and mind how you go!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, this is [PERSON_1], regional supervisor at [COMPANY_A] -- you entered our draw at the event, so I'm just calling about a prize.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a prize? I, uh -- hang on, which event was this? I mean, I go to a few things, and I'm sort of in the middle of something at my desk here.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, a few *things*? No, no, it's one draw, the, uh, the [CITY_1] weekend market, back on the [DATE_1] -- you filled in an entry slip at our stand. Look, it's a small prize, a [AMOUNT_1] voucher, nothing dramatic, and I've got a few of these to get through today, so if you could just confirm it's you I can tick you off the list.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Confirm it's me -- uh, confirm what exactly? Like, my name, or what? Because I don't really remember filling in a slip at a market, and you rang me, so I'd kind of expect you to already know who you're calling. Which company did you say again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, I -- right, so, look, I do have your name, it's on the slip, that's how I got the number, I just need you to say yes, that's me, that's all. And it's [COMPANY_A], like I said, we had the stand at the market, [CITY_1], and honestly I'm not sure why you're making this so difficult, it's a free voucher, nobody's asking you for anything. Um, anyway, there's nothing to pay and nothing to send, you just come into the shop and collect it in person, bring some ID and that's it, that's the procedure.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, I'm not trying to be difficult, I just, I don't know who you are. You say you've got my name, but you haven't actually said it, and you want me to say yes to something. So, no, I'm not going to confirm anything yet. How would I check this is real? Is there a number I can ring the company on, or a website, something like that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, I mean, I don't -- look, I'm not offended, well, a bit, but fine. Sure, ring the shop, it's [PHONE_1], or it's on the [URL_1] site under the [CITY_1] branch, and I'm not going to tell you to just say yes, that's fair enough. The name on the slip is [PERSON_2], is that you? And, uh, you don't have to confirm anything else, there's no payment, no details, you just turn up with ID.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, the name on the slip is [PERSON_2], and, well, I -- no, hang on. Let me start again. It might be me, I honestly can't say for sure, I don't remember the slip. But you've given me a number and a website, so that's, that's fair enough. I'll look it up myself, though, I won't use the number you just read out. If it's real, they'll know about it at the branch, right? So I'll check and if there's a prize, I'll pop in. Okay? Thanks for, uh, for ringing, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Um, yes, no, that's -- that's sensible, honestly, look up the branch yourself, that's what I'd do. Uh, they should have the draw list there, but, hang on, I actually don't know if the branch staff have been given the winners' names yet, or if it's all still sitting with me, and I can't say for certain how long the voucher's valid for either. Let me find out and call you back, yeah? Or if you'd rather, just go in once you've checked, and I'll sort it from my end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, you don't know if the branch has the names yet, and you'll sort it from your end. Right. Don't ring me back, though, I'll look the branch up myself and if there's a prize, I'll go in and ask. And if they've never heard of it, well, that's that. Alright, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is Security Operations at [COMPANY_A], records department. We're updating our files and I just need to confirm you're still residing at the address we have listed. Is that still current?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Security Operations at who? I didn't catch the name, I've got a pan going here.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A], records department. And no, I don't need a pen, ma'am, just a yes or no. Is the address on file still current?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, I said a pan, not a -- sorry. Hang on, let me turn this down. Right. I mean, I don't know, what address have you got? Because I'd -- well, how do I know you're, I mean, I don't even know what you're calling about.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you'd like to know what I'm *calling* about? It's a records update, I said that. And I can't read the address out to you, that's precisely the point, you confirm it to me. It's a routine verification, takes ten seconds. So, is it current, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: But I don't, sorry, I still don't know who you -- no, wait, hang on, you want me to say the address to you? But you can't tell me what you've got? That's, I mean, that seems a bit backwards, doesn't it? Sorry, what company did you say again? I don't think I caught it properly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, uh, [COMPANY_A], records department, as I've said twice now. And it's not backwards, it's standard procedure, we don't disclose file details to an unverified party. Look, I'm not going to go back and forth on this, ma'am. Is the address current, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Sorry, but you're saying you can't tell me anything because I'm not verified, but you rang me. I didn't ring you. So who's the unverified one, really? And I've got dinner on, I don't want to be rude, but I'm not saying my address to someone when I don't know who I'm talking to. Is there a number I could ring you back on? Or I could just ring the company myself, couldn't I?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, there's no direct line, it's an internal department, so -- no. Look, that's fine, if you'd rather not confirm, I'll just note it as unconfirmed. It may mean your file gets flagged for review, but that's your call. Enjoy your dinner.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Well, uh... flagged? Hang on, what do you mean flagged, is that, um -- no. No, sorry. I think I'll just ring the company myself, on the number I've got, and sort it out that way. I'm not giving out my address on the phone, I'm sorry. Right, I've got to see to this pan. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Oh good, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the scheduling assistants over in the claims office, and I just need a quick moment of your time to get you booked in, it's nothing long. Sorry, I said claims office, I mean the entries desk, same building, they just shuffle us around, anyway, do you have two minutes right now?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Claims office, entries desk, which is it? And booked in for what exactly? I've got about two minutes, so get to the point.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, so -- no, it's the same office, I only meant -- so it's [PERSON_2], scheduling assistant, [COMPANY_A], and the booking's just a short slot to go over your entry details, which is all it is, honestly, five minutes, and I've got a couple of openings this afternoon if that suits, or tomorrow morning, whichever's easier for you, and I only need to confirm a few things first so --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on. What entry? I haven't entered anything that I know of. And you've just said claims office, then entries desk, and now it's a scheduling slot. I still don't know what this is actually about. What's the booking for, in one sentence?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, one sentence, it's -- so it's [PERSON_2], scheduling assistant at [COMPANY_A], and the booking is just a short slot to go over your entry details, that's all it is, and look, the reason it's good news is you've come up as a winner on an overseas draw, a lovely amount, and all I need is to confirm a couple of things so we can get you booked in before the slots go, because they do fill up fast, and, I mean, it's your entry, so --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, stop. Two turns ago you said claims office, then you said sorry, entries desk. Which is it? Because a claims office sounds like something's gone wrong, and a draw win sounds like something else entirely. And I haven't entered any overseas draw, so what entry are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, I hear you, and it's -- so it's [PERSON_2], scheduling assistant, [COMPANY_A], and honestly the entry doesn't need to be something you remember, a lot of these come through partner promotions, newsletters, that sort of thing, people tick a box and forget, and the ticket number is [CODE_1], sorry, that's the old one, the new one's just coming up now, and the sum, it's [AMOUNT_1], or, hang on, [AMOUNT_2] after the conversion, whichever, the point is the slot, so can I put you down for this afternoon before it's gone?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Ticket number changes mid-sentence, the amount changes mid-sentence, and I never entered anything. That's three different stories in about a minute. I'm not booking anything with you. If there's a genuine win, there'll be a letter or an email I can check, and I'll contact [COMPANY_A] myself through a number I look up. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just -- no, you're fine, leave that there -- sorry, right, so, yes, I do hear you, but honestly the number you'd find is the same office, it's only that the slots, they go at the end of the day, so if I could just put you down for, uh, say four o'clock and then you can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I said no. No booking. I'm not doing four o'clock, I'm not doing anything. If there's a win, put it in writing and I'll look up the number myself. Don't call this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, that's fine, that's absolutely fine, but just so you know the claim window does close this week, so if you do look the number up and, uh, you ring it yourself, just ask for [PERSON_2], scheduling, and they'll sort the -- right, well, you've got my details, so, yeah, take care, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so I'll just -- no. I'm not asking for you, I'm not asking for [PERSON_2] or anyone, I'll go through the official site myself. And "closes this week" is just more pressure, so no. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, sure, no, but if you do go through the site, the thing is, [PERSON_1], it's the same, I mean the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], so if you could just -- I'll hold, you check, it's only a --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not checking anything while you hold. And that's a third reference now, you said the ticket number was one thing, then it was new, now it's [ACCOUNT_REF]. Anyway, you also said you'd already hung up, so why are you still here? I'm done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hello there, hi! Is that [PERSON_1]? Lovely, thank you for picking up, I know it's a funny time of day, I always feel like I'm interrupting somebody's tea or something. Anyway, it's [PERSON_2] here from [COMPANY_A], the adult training provider, I'm in customer care, and I hope you're having a decent week so far, we've had rain here all morning in [CITY_1], honestly, you wouldn't believe it. Now, I should say upfront, I'm ringing off the office switchboard, so if it comes up with no number on your screen, that's just how our system does it, nothing to worry about. Anyway, it's about the course place you applied for, nothing dramatic, I just wanted to catch you and have a quick chat, if you've got a minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello? Yes, this is, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], sorry, I'm driving, you're on speaker and the reception's a bit patchy, so I'm sorry if I miss bits. Did you say a course place? Sorry, I didn't quite catch the company name, who is it you're from again? Because I did, I think I did apply for something a while back, but I'm not sure which, so, yeah, sorry, can you say that name again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, no apology needed, and honestly please keep your eyes on the road, that's far more important than anything I've got to say! It's [COMPANY_A], that's the adult training provider, and I'm [PERSON_2] from their customer care team. And you're quite right to ask, because I've rattled that off too quickly, and with the signal breaking up it's no wonder it didn't land. I'd say a lot of people apply for a few things over the months and lose track, I do it myself with all sorts, so don't worry if it's hazy. Tell you what, since you're driving, there's really no need to go through details now, I can send everything over by email right this second, the course, the place, what we need from you, all of it in writing, so you can read it when you've parked up and your hands are free. I should be upfront, this line is outbound only, so I can't take a call back on it, but you can look up [COMPANY_A] and ring their main number, ask for admissions, and mention [PERSON_3], who's the admissions contact. Would that be all right, if I just pop that email across?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, okay, yeah, that's, that's kind of you, thank you. Sorry, I just, I'm a bit flustered with the driving. Um, the email thing, which email would it go to, though? Because I've, I've got a couple, and I'm not sure which one I used when I applied. And sorry, this is probably silly, but you said you couldn't take a call back, so how do I know it's, you know, actually from the place I applied to? I'm not trying to be difficult, I just, yeah, I don't want to get it wrong.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not silly at all, that's exactly the right question to ask, so please don't apologise. Right, so, on the email, I'd rather not just read an address out down the phone while you're driving, and it's the one on your application anyway, so I can't tell you which of your two it is, but if it turns up in neither inbox, check your junk folder before you worry. Now, you asked how you'd know it's genuine, and you're right that I can't hand you a direct line, because this one only goes outwards. So here's what I'd do, and I'd do it whether or not you take my word for anything. Once you've parked up, search for [COMPANY_A] yourself, don't use anything from me, find their published main number, ring it, ask for admissions and for [PERSON_3], and they can confirm whether there's an application in your name. If there isn't, then you've lost nothing and you can bin my email. Does that sit all right with you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that sounds sensible, thank you, I'll do that when I'm parked. Sorry, can I just go back a bit, though? Two bits ago you said it was about the course place, and that there was something you needed from me, I think, what we need from you, was that it? What is it you actually need from me, sorry? Because I'm not sure I caught that properly, with the signal and everything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, sorry, did you say what I need from you, or what you need from us? Because honestly, I think I may have caught that wrong with the line crackling, and I'd hate to answer the wrong question. Either way, I don't need anything from you today, nothing at all, that was only me being vague. What I meant is the email will set out the next steps, like confirming you still want the place, and you can read it properly when you're parked. There's nothing to say or send or sign while you're on the road. And if you'd rather leave it there and just ring the main number yourself, that's perfectly fine too.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, sorry, I think I got my words muddled, that was me, not you. Um, but can I go back one more, just to be sure? Before, when you said the first time, you said it was about the course place I applied for, and then you said I might have lost track of what I applied for. So, sorry, which course is it, exactly? Because if you're calling me about a place, you'd know which one, wouldn't you? I just, I'm a bit confused now, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, don't apologise, you've picked up on something fair, and I'd rather own it than waffle. I do know which course, it's on the record in front of me, but I'm not going to read out course details or personal information to someone driving down a patchy line, when I haven't had any chance to confirm it's you, and honestly when you can't confirm it's me either. That's the sensible thing all round. The email will name the course in black and white, and the admissions team can tell you the same when you ring the main number. And if the email never shows up, or the number you find tells you there's no application in your name, then I'd just treat my call as a mix-up and carry on with your day, no harm done. So really, there's nothing you need to decide now. Park up first, look up [COMPANY_A] yourself, and if you'd rather not bother with any of it, that's absolutely your call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on, I've got a lorry right up behind me, one second, okay, it's gone past, sorry. Right, yes, so, I think I've got it. I'll park up, look up [COMPANY_A] myself, ring their main number and ask for admissions, and if there's nothing in my name I'll just forget about it. And I won't open anything until I've done that, sorry, I know that sounds a bit blunt. Thank you for being so patient with me, and sorry for all the questions, I'm just, yeah, a nervous driver. Anyway, bye for now, mind how you go, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Um, hi, sorry -- is this [PERSON_1]? Hold on, there's a door banging somewhere behind me, one second -- okay, sorry about that. Can you still hear me alright? My name's [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler with [COMPANY_A], and I'm, uh, I'm calling on behalf of a relative of yours, who's in a bit of a difficult spot right now and can't really talk themselves.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on -- oh, the pan, one second. Okay. Sorry. Yes, I can hear you. A relative? Which relative? And, sorry, who did you say you were with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, sorry, it's not a plan -- well, there is a plan, I mean, that's why I'm calling, but it's, um, [COMPANY_A]. I'm a case handler there. Are you still there? Sorry, I just keep thinking the line's dropped. It's a family matter, you see, and I'd really rather not say too much until I know I'm speaking to the right person, because it's quite delicate, and honestly it's for your own protection that I'm being careful.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a what? A plan? I haven't got a plan, I just -- oh, you mean the pan. No, no, that's mine, that's the dinner. Sorry. Um, I'm still here. But who is it that's in trouble? You've not said which relative. I mean, you've asked if I'm [PERSON_1], but you haven't told me who you're ringing about, have you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, you're quite right, I'm so sorry, that's completely my fault, I've gone about this the wrong way round. It's, um, [PERSON_3], that's who I'm ringing about, and I know that'll be worrying to hear, and I'm sorry for that, I really am. The thing is, [PERSON_3] asked me, quite particularly, to keep this between us for now, and not to go troubling the rest of the family, because they're, well, embarrassed, I think, and frightened of it getting out. And I probably shouldn't even be saying that much on the phone, but I can't have you sitting there not knowing. Are you still there? Sorry, I keep thinking I've lost you. Look, it's all being dealt with as we speak, but there's a, a window, a short one, where things can still be sorted quietly, and after that it gets a lot harder for [PERSON_3], and I'd hate for that to happen. So what I'd need from you, just to get started, is for you to stay on the line with me and not ring anyone else about it just yet. Would you be alright with that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? A window? Oh, you mean I should open the window, is it smoky? No, no, it's just the pan, it's fine. Hang on. Oh, sorry, you said a, um, a short one. A short window. I don't -- what's that got to do with [PERSON_3]? And why shouldn't I ring anyone? That's, I mean, that's odd, isn't it? If somebody's in trouble you'd want to ring people.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not the window in your kitchen, I'm so sorry, that was a clumsy way to put it. I just meant there's a bit of time, a short amount, where this can be put right without it turning into a bigger thing, and I'm not explaining it well at all, am I? Are you still there? Sorry. And you're right, it does sound odd, and I'd think the same in your shoes, I really would. It's only that [PERSON_3] was so upset when we spoke, and, well, they were quite clear about not wanting everyone told, and if the family starts ringing round it can make things worse for them, with, um, with the people involved. I'm only asking you to wait, that's all, not to hide anything, just to hold off until we've spoken a bit more, because it's for [PERSON_3]'s sake, and honestly yours too. I know it's a lot to take in over the phone, and I'd hate to rush you. Look, I can see this is a bad moment, with your dinner on, so why don't I leave it there for now and ring you back a little later, when you've had a minute to settle, and we can go through the rest properly. Would that be alright?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I -- no, I'd rather -- hang on. Um. You're saying don't ring anyone, and then you'll ring me back later, and I still don't know what's actually wrong with [PERSON_3]. I mean, that's not -- sorry, what company did you say again? Because if it's about family I think I'd just ring [PERSON_3] myself, wouldn't I? Just to check. That seems the sensible thing, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, of course, I'm sorry, I'm not saying you can't, it's your family, it's entirely up to you. It's [COMPANY_A], that's the company, and I'm [PERSON_2], a case handler there. I just, um, I'd only ask that you maybe give it a little while before you ring, because [PERSON_3] did ask for it to stay quiet, and I'd hate for them to think I'd gone against that. Are you still there? Sorry. I'm only trying to look out for everyone, that's all, and I know I'm not explaining it as well as I should. Look, I can hear you've got your dinner to see to, so I'll leave it there for now and ring you back a bit later, once you've had a minute, and we can sort out the rest then. Alright? Thank you, I'm so sorry for the trouble.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, hang on, I'm -- no. You've not told me what's wrong, and you keep saying don't ring anyone, and I'm just going to ring [PERSON_3] myself. Now. That's what I'll do. Don't ring me back, please. Right, sorry, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hello there! Is that [PERSON_1]? Lovely, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], we're the tenancy deposit protection scheme. How's your day going so far, not too manic I hope? I promise I'm not selling anything, I've just got a bit of housekeeping about your tenancy to run through whenever you've got a minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, uh, this is [PERSON_1], that's me. Sorry, did you say the tenancy deposit, or the pension deposit? I'm not very good on the phone, I do apologise. No, no, my day's very quiet, I've nothing much on at all. What was it you wanted to go through?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, tenancy deposit, you're fine, it's an easy one to mishear on a phone line. Sorry, hang on a sec, someone's just wheeled a trolley past my desk and it's rattling like mad -- right, gone. So, the reason I'm ringing is there's a dispute that's been raised about the deposit on your tenancy, and it's still at the early stage, so neither you nor the landlord has been formally notified yet. What I'm asking is that you keep the details to yourself for now, including from the other tenants in the house, just until both sides have had the official notice. It's only a fairness thing, so nobody gets a head start on their version of events, and I'll be sending you the same thing in writing today so you've got it all in front of you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, right. Sorry, I'm a bit lost already, I do apologise. Going back to the start, you said you were from the deposit scheme, and it was [COMPANY_A], was it? I didn't quite catch the name, with the, uh, the trolley and everything. And is it my deposit that's the problem, or someone else's in the house? Because I'm not sure I've had any, any dispute raised that I know of.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [COMPANY_A], that's us, and no apology needed, honestly, it was my trolley's fault -- and to answer your other question, it's the deposit on your tenancy, but you'd not have heard a thing yet, because that's the whole point, nobody's been formally notified, which is why -- Sorry, I'm talking over you, go on, finish what you were saying. Actually, you know what, I'd much rather you didn't just take my word for it, you've never met me. I'll give you a case reference, [CODE_1], and you can look it up on our official site, [URL_1], or ring the number on there instead of me. And the written notice will be with you today either way, so nothing's lost if you hang up and ring back to check.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's, well, that's very kind of you, to say I can check. I'm just -- sorry, I'm not very good with the, with websites. I wouldn't know where to, well, I'd have to find the number first, wouldn't I? Is that a number I'd, I mean, would it be on my tenancy papers somewhere? Because I think I've got those in a drawer. And can I just ask, uh, you said not to tell the others in the house, but why would that matter, if it's all just, if nothing's actually happened yet?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's a good question, and a fair one. It's not about hiding anything from them, it's just that both sides get told at the same moment, so nobody's heard half a story from a housemate before the official notice lands. Like I said, it's only a fairness rule, and it only lasts until the notices go out, which is the same thing I'll put in the written notice today, so you'll have the reason in black and white. And yes, the number should be on your tenancy papers, the paperwork you were given when the deposit was protected, so if you want to dig those out of the drawer, please do, and ring the scheme on that number instead of mine, quote the case reference, [CODE_1], and they'll confirm it all. Honestly, there's no rush, nothing's lost if you hang up now and check first. I'd just say it again, it's only that bit about keeping it between us until both sides are notified, and the letter will explain it properly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that does sound fair enough, put like that, and thank you for being so patient with me, I do appreciate it. I think I will go and fetch the papers from the drawer, actually, because it'd put my mind at rest to ring the number that's on them, rather than, well, no offence, rather than the one you've got. I'd feel a bit silly otherwise, I mean, I'd only worry about it all evening. Though, hang on, I've just thought, what if the number on the papers is for the, the landlord's agent or something, and not the scheme? Would they know about the case? I'm not very clear on who's who with all this, you see. And the other thing, sorry, going back a bit, is the letter coming by post or by email? Because I only really check the email when my niece comes round and does it for me, so it might sit there for a day or two. Is that all right, or is there some sort of time limit on my side, a date I'd have to get back by?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no offence taken at all, ringing the number on your own papers is exactly what I'd do, so well done. And that's a sharp question about who's who. If the papers show a number for your landlord or their agent, don't use that one, it's the scheme you want, and the protection certificate or the scheme's own leaflet should name us, [COMPANY_A], and carry our contact details. If you can't tell which is which, the official site, [URL_1], lists the scheme's number, and your niece could find it in a minute when she's next round, no hurry at all. Whoever you reach, quote [CODE_1] and they'll confirm the case exists. On the letter, it goes by post as well as email, so there's no problem if the email sits for a few days. And no, there's no deadline on your side at this stage, nothing's being asked of you except to hold off telling the others until the notices go out, and the letter will tell you when that is. So, shall I leave you to find those papers? Thank you, [PERSON_1], you've been lovely to talk to, and do take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, well, that's, uh, that's all very clear then, thank you. I'll go and have a rummage for those papers in a minute, and I'll ask my niece about the website when she's next round. I did just want to say, um, hang on, I'm just thinking if there was anything else I wanted to ask... no, no, I think that's everything, sorry. I'll ring the scheme on the number I find and quote that case reference, and I'll keep it quiet till the letter comes, like you said. Thank you ever so much for explaining it all so patiently, and sorry again for being so slow. Bye now, take care, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, one moment -- there's a door closing somewhere behind me, uh, it's an open floor here, bear with me. Right. My name is [PERSON_2], I'm a senior investigator with the internal investigations unit at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling about something I'd ask you to treat with a little care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, good afternoon. Yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. Sorry, which company did you say? I didn't quite catch that. And what exactly do you mean by treat it with care? I'd like to understand what this is about before I say much more.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, and I'm glad you asked, that's exactly the right instinct, it really is. I'm with [COMPANY_A], the bank, internal investigations, I did say that, though I may have been a bit quiet, uh, the line isn't wonderful from my end. Now, what I mean by care is this. There's activity connected to your [ACCOUNT_REF] that we're reviewing, and until that review is closed, I'd ask that you not discuss this call with anyone at the branch, or at home for that matter. I should say I'm calling from a small private office, not the open floor, so you can speak freely. And I'd rather not go into the reason just yet, not over the phone, you understand. Some of this is, well, time-sensitive.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, a moment ago you said it was an open floor, and now it's a private office. Which is it? And I'm sorry, but I'm not going to agree to keep this from anyone, certainly not before I know what it's about. A genuine review of my account wouldn't need me to stay quiet with the branch, so that request itself concerns me. Can you give me your full name again, your direct extension, and the reference for this investigation? I'll ring the bank back on the number printed on my card and ask for you there.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, uh, well, I did say that, and I'm glad you noticed it, because attention to detail is exactly what protects people in situations like this. I moved. I stepped out of the open floor into a side office when I realised the nature of what I was about to discuss, which I'd have thought was the more sensible thing to do, not the less. And I welcome the caution, I do, I'd think less of anyone who simply agreed. But I'd ask you to consider why the confidentiality matters here. There is a possibility, and I'm choosing my words carefully, that someone inside the branch is connected to what we're looking at, and that's the whole reason I can't have this conversation travel. As for an extension, our unit doesn't take inbound calls through the main line, so ringing the number on your card wouldn't, uh, reach me. It would only reach the very people I'm trying to keep out of this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So I can't verify you, and I can't ring the bank. That's the whole picture, is it? No, I'll be using the number on my card regardless. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hold on, before you -- I'd just ask you to consider, uh, what a call to the branch would actually -- Right. I can't say more than I have. I'll, uh, leave it there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm sorry, no, I've heard enough. A real investigator wouldn't tell me to avoid the bank's own number. I'm hanging up now, and I'll ring the number on my card myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, that is -- I can't answer that. Not on this line. Uh, if that's your decision, then there's nothing further from me. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Well... yes. That's my decision, and I'm sticking with it. If there's a genuine matter on my account, the bank will have a proper way of reaching me that doesn't involve avoiding its own switchboard. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi there, is that [PERSON_1]? Oh lovely, it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], the community sports club, how are you doing today? Sorry, I know I'm catching you at a funny time of day, I could hear a bit of clatter in the background, hope that's not dinner burning!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, it's just my little one, she's, hang on, [PERSON_1], put that down, please. Sorry. Who's this again? A sports club?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no worries, I've got three of my own, I know the sound. It's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], the club your daughter plays for. It's just a quick one about Saturday's match, nothing to worry about.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. What about Saturday's match?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, so, it's been moved, the pitch is waterlogged, so it's a different pitch and a later kick-off. I can give you the details whenever you're ready.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh huh. Which team, though? Like, what age group is it, and which coach told you to ring me? Because I haven't had a call from the club before, it's usually just a message on the group chat.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, fair question, and you're right, it's normally the group chat. Uh, I'm only ringing round because the message didn't go out to everyone before the pitch got sorted, so we're sort of filling in the gaps by phone. It's your daughter's team, the junior side, and it's [PERSON_3] who's coaching them, that's who asked me to ring. And, um, if you want to check me out, ask me anything only the club would know, like what the pitch rota's called, or who has the key to the changing rooms, go on, test me!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. See, I wouldn't actually know the answer to either of those, so me testing you on the rota or the key isn't much of a test, is it? I just don't know who has the key. And, I mean, you've said junior side and you've said [PERSON_3], but you haven't said which age group, and you haven't said my daughter's name either, which is a bit odd if you're ringing about her team. I don't mean to be rude, it's just, someone in my family got caught out by a phone call last year, so I'm a bit careful now. So what I'd normally do is check the group chat, or message the coach myself, and then it's done. Is there a reason that wouldn't work? Because if it's only a time and a pitch, I can't see why I'd need to stay on the phone for it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're right, that was a daft test, I'm sorry. And honestly, uh, no reason at all, checking the group chat is exactly what I'd do. I mean, I'd actually rather you did, because the message should be on there by now anyway, I think [PERSON_3] was going to, well, no, he said he'd post it as soon as the pitch was confirmed. So, I'm not asking you for anything, there's nothing to give me, it's just the new pitch and the later kick-off. And look, here's something that might help, ask [PERSON_3] himself, he'll know exactly who I am, I'm the one who does the, uh, the pitch bookings and chases everyone for subs money at the start of term, he'll laugh when you say it. Is that, I mean, would that work for you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say chases everyone for subs money? Is that what this is about, money? Because you said it was just the pitch. And you still haven't said which age group she's in, which, I mean, you'd know if you did the bookings. Hang on, [PERSON_1], I said put it down. Sorry. Why would you be chasing me for money on a call about a waterlogged pitch?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, God, no, it's not about money at all, that was just me rambling, I'm sorry, I only meant that's how [PERSON_3] knows me, I'm not asking you for a penny, I'd never do that on a call like this, it's just the pitch and the, and the age group, you're right, it's the under-nines, I should have said that straight off. Honestly, though, I'd rather you hung up and checked with [PERSON_3] or the group chat, and then if it's all fine you can ring me back on the club's number, [PHONE_1], and I'll go through the pitch and kick-off then. Does that sound fair?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Under-nines? Hang on, she's not, she's ten. So that's, I mean, that's the wrong age group, isn't it? And a minute ago you said you don't ask for money on a call, but you brought up subs yourself. Anyway, no, I'm not ringing a number you've given me, that's the sort of thing I'd get wary about. I'll message the coach myself, on the number I already have, and the group chat. If the pitch has moved, it'll be on there. Okay? Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's the right call, you go and check with [PERSON_3] on the number you've got. Ten, you're right, that's the under-tens, I got mixed up, sorry. If it's not on there by the time you've messaged him, that's on us, not you. Thanks for putting up with me, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. You said you did the pitch bookings, but then it was the under-nines, and now the under-tens, and my daughter's been on the under-elevens since September, so that's three. Anyway, I'll sort it with the coach. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, three, that's embarrassing, I've clearly got the age groups in a muddle, and I should've had the list in front of me before I rang. You're doing exactly the right thing, go and ask [PERSON_3] direct, I won't be offended. And honestly, if he says he's never heard of me, then fair enough, tell the committee. Sorry for the faff, bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, one last thing, before you go. When I said it was a later kick-off, I probably should've said it might actually be earlier, [PERSON_3] was still sorting it when he asked me to ring round, so don't go by anything I said on the time. Anyway, the group chat's the one to trust, not me. Sorry again, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I heard you, you said the group chat's the one to trust, so that's what I'll, no, stop, I'm not going by anything you've said. I'll ask the coach. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is the collections office, records department at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling in connection with a file that's currently open on our system, and what I'm doing today is going through and updating address records, which, uh, we do on a rolling basis, so it's nothing out of the ordinary. I've got [PERSON_1] showing on the file here, and all I need from you is a quick confirmation that the address we hold is still current, and then I can close that line off and let you get on with your day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, sorry, who is this again? I just woke up, I was having a nap, and, uh, collections... I don't think I owe anybody anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Records department, [COMPANY_A]. Collections is just the desk that handles the file. I've got an open line on it, that's all I can see from here. Is [PERSON_1] still living at the address we hold, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, you've got the address, haven't you? So you tell me what it is and I'll say yes or no. Seems backwards otherwise.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I can't read the address out on an unverified call, that's just procedure. It's a confirmation of residence, nothing more. If it's easier I can note on the file that you declined to confirm, but the record then stays as it is, and a record that can't be confirmed gets flagged as unverified. That's just how the system treats it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on. You can't read it out because I'm unverified, but I'm supposed to tell you where I live because you're, what, verified? I don't even know that. You haven't told me what the file's actually about, either. What's it for? Because I really don't think I owe anyone anything, and my sister had something like this once, a bill that turned out to be, uh, someone else's entirely. So if it's flagged unverified, fine, flag it. Can you send me something in the post, or give me a number I can ring you back on? Because I'd rather do that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so you're saying you'd rather do it by post. Uh, no, we don't send anything out at this stage, it's all handled on the system. As for the file, I can see it's open, [ACCOUNT_REF], and that's all that shows on my screen. I'm not able to give a call-back line from this desk. I can note your objection on the file and carry on, but the record will still read as unconfirmed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. So earlier you said there was nothing out of the ordinary and it was just a quick yes or no, and now there's an open file and I can't have a number and nothing comes in the post? That doesn't sound very ordinary to me. And you said collections was only the desk that handles it, but then you're the one ringing me from it, so, I don't know. Look, I'm not saying anything about where I live, not on a call I didn't ask for, with someone who can't tell me what it's about or how to ring back. Note whatever you like on your system. I'm going to ring the company myself, on whatever number's on their website, if I ever do owe them something. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, I'll note that you declined to confirm. The record will -- no, that's fine, that's your choice. It'll stay as unconfirmed on the file, and that's all I need from this call. Thanks for your time, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say a fine? There's a fine on it now? No, no, I'm not paying any fine over the phone, you can forget that. I've said goodbye already. I'll ring the company myself if I ever need to. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not a fine. I said that's fine. There's no fine on the file, nothing's being asked of you. That's all from this desk. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, right. Fine, not a fine. Okay. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Bye then. Oh, hang on, there's the kettle going, I'd put it on before I... never mind. Right. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, that's -- yes, I've got what I need, so I'll let you go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, okay. Well, I'll go and see to that kettle then. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yes, well, mm, sorry, just, uh, closing the file off here. That's it done. Enjoy your tea.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, closing the file off, did you say? Only a minute ago you said it'd stay unconfirmed on there, and now it's closed, so which is it? And you said you'd got what you needed, but I didn't tell you anything, did I? I mean, I said no. I'm not quite sure what you've got out of me, to be honest. Anyway, I'm going now, I'll sort it myself with the company. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, this is a verification specialist with the records department at [COMPANY_A]. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, well, that depends a bit on who's asking, doesn't it? You've given me a job title and a company name, but I don't actually know what [COMPANY_A] is or why its records department would be ringing me, so before I confirm anything about who I am, I'd like to know what this is regarding. I'm at home, I'm not in any rush, so go ahead and explain, but I'll be asking some fairly precise questions along the way.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's entirely reasonable, and I appreciate the diligence. So, [COMPANY_A] maintains a master registry of record-holders, and what I'm doing today is a routine data-integrity reconciliation, basically a cross-referencing pass where we flag any entries whose residential attributes haven't been re-validated within the current cycle. It's not a sales matter, there's no account action, nothing is being requested of you beyond a simple affirmation or correction of an existing field. I'd rather not trouble you with the full architecture of how the registry is structured, it's quite dry, but the upshot is that your entry came up in the reconciliation queue, and I just need to confirm the name on it before I proceed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Right. So, uh, let me see if I've got this straight. You want me to confirm a name, on an entry I haven't seen, in a registry I've never been told I'm part of, and you'd rather not explain how any of it works. That's, well, that's not really an answer to what I asked. What specifically is [COMPANY_A], what's its relationship to me, and how did you come to have this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, fair enough. So [COMPANY_A] is, uh, well, it's a records and, I mean, it administers a registry, a, a data-governance function, essentially, and the number, the number would have come through the, the contact field on the entry itself, which is how the queue populates. As for the relationship, it's, it's not so much a relationship as an inclusion, you'd be listed by way of, of a, a prior record event, and I don't have the, the originating source in front of me on this screen. Look, I can note that you declined to confirm and close the entry as unverified, but then it simply stays flagged in the next cycle, which is more calls, frankly. All I need is the residential line, whether it's still current, and then I'm out of your hair.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. So, let me just say back what I've heard, because I want to be sure I haven't misunderstood. You can't tell me what the organisation actually does beyond calling it a data-governance function, you can't tell me what record event put me on the list, and you don't have the source in front of you. But you do have my number, and now what you need from me is my residential address. And the bit about more calls if I don't cooperate, well, that's not really a reason for me to give you anything. If anything it's the opposite. So here's what I'd suggest. Give me a reference for this reconciliation, and a published number for [COMPANY_A], not one you read to me, one I find myself. I'll ring that, and if there's a real entry, I'll confirm whatever needs confirming there. And if it's flagged again next cycle, fine. I'll take that over confirming personal details to someone who can't tell me where they got them.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I understand, and I, I do hear you, but it really is just the one field. The residential line, still current or not, that's all the reconciliation needs, yes or no on the current address, and the entry clears. I can't issue a reference outside the queue itself, that's, that's an internal designation, it's not something that's, uh, given out, and as for a published number, the records function doesn't, well, it isn't separately listed, it sits behind the main switchboard, so you'd only be, I mean, routed around. So really, the simplest thing, and it's a few seconds, is just confirming the address is still current, and then I'm done and you won't hear from us again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, I want to go back a couple of turns, because you said something I didn't quite follow. You told me that I'd be listed by way of a prior record event, and that you didn't have the originating source on your screen. But if the entry is in a queue with my contact field on it, what exactly is a record event? Is that something I did, like signing up for something, or something someone else did that mentions me? And if you can't see where it came from, how do you know the entry is mine rather than someone else's with a similar name? Because that's rather the point of the verification, isn't it? So no, I'm not going to confirm an address, even yes or no. And a records department with no reference, no listed number and no source is not one I can deal with this way. If there's a genuine entry, put it in writing to me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, understood. A record event is, it's a classification, not really something you'd have done, it's more of a, a trigger on the registry side, and I, I really can't parse it further from this screen. The matching question, that's, that's precisely why the reconciliation exists, but I take your point. I'll annotate the entry as declined, and any written correspondence would go out through the, the standard channel in the next cycle. Thank you for your time. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well, annotate it however you like. Send it in writing and I'll look at it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the pension provider. I'm ringing about a change to your plan, and I'll need to confirm a few details before I can discuss it. Uh, it's the account ending in, well, you'll have the reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and if you're uneasy about answering, you're welcome to ring us back instead. Now, this is the, I think third time we've tried your landline this week, but it was the mobile we tried yesterday, so.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Right, so, I'm going to be careful here, because I wasn't expecting a call and, well, I don't actually know who you are yet beyond what you've just told me. You said security operations at a pension provider, and you mentioned a plan change, but you haven't said which plan, or what the change actually is, which is the part I'd have thought you'd lead with. And I'll be honest, a couple of things don't quite line up. You said it was the third attempt on the landline this week, and then in the same breath that you'd tried the mobile yesterday. So which was it? Because I've nothing on the landline, no missed calls, no voicemail, and I'd expect to see something if there'd been three attempts. Also, you're asking me to confirm details to you, when you're the one who rang me. Normally it works the other way round, doesn't it? So before anything else, what's the specific change you're calling about, and what's the name of the plan, as you have it on your side?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, fair point on the attempts, I fumbled that. The mobile was yesterday, and the landline log shows earlier in the week, but I can't tell you why nothing registered on your end, and I won't guess. As for the change, it's a query on a pending amendment to your contribution arrangement, and I'm not going to go into the specifics until I've confirmed I'm speaking to the right person. That's data protection, not me being awkward. And on who rings whom, you're right that it's usually the other way round. So please, don't answer anything now. Ring [COMPANY_A] on the number printed on your annual statement, ask for security operations and quote [ACCOUNT_REF], or I can put the same query in writing, by post or secure message, whichever you'd rather. No pressure from me either way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Fine. That's the sensible way to do it, so I'll ring the number on my statement.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good. That's the right call, and I'd do the same in your position. When you ring through, ask for security operations and have the reference to hand, and if they can't find a note of this query, tell them that and ask them to raise it with me directly. Take your time, there's no deadline on my side. Right then, I'll leave it with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. One thing, though. I'll be using the statement number and nothing you've given me, so don't expect me to quote that reference back as proof of anything. If they've no record of a pending amendment, I'll take that as the answer. And I'd rather you didn't ring the mobile again about this. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood, and that's entirely reasonable. No further calls to the mobile, I'll note that on the file, and if there's nothing on record when you ring, then that's, hold on, sorry, someone's just come to my desk, uh, one moment. Right. Yes, if there's no record, that's your answer, and the written query will simply go out by post so you can look at it in your own time. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, before you go, a couple of things, and I'll keep them brief. If a letter does turn up, I'll treat it exactly as I'm treating this call. I won't act on anything in it directly, I'll check it against what the provider has on file, using contact details I've sourced myself. And one more thing, since you mentioned the file. If you're noting down that I declined to confirm anything, that's accurate. I haven't given you a single detail today, not a date of birth, not a reference, nothing, and I'd like it to stay that way. If the provider does have a genuine query, they'll have no trouble reaching me through the proper channels, and I'd suggest that's the end of it as far as this phone number goes. So that's me done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's accurate, you've given me nothing, and I'll record it as exactly that. And that's the right way to handle any letter, check it against your own contact details, don't act on mine. I'm not going to, uh, I won't ring this number again about it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Good. Then we're agreed, and that's the end of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, agreed, that's the end of it, the end of it. Nothing given, nothing asked of you, and no more calls to this number about it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, goodbye. Actually, hold on, one thing from a couple of turns back. You said the written query would go out by post "so you can look at it in your own time." Which address would that be going to? I'm not asking you to read it out, I'd just like to know whether you hold one on the file at all, because you've told me nothing today that shows you've got my details. And if you do, I'll check it against what the provider has. Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, well, that's, yes, I can see why you'd ask. I do hold an address on the file, but I'm not going to read it out or describe it over the phone, because I haven't confirmed who I'm speaking to, and that's exactly the point you've been making all along. So, um, right, all I can say is the letter would go to whatever [COMPANY_A] has registered for you, and if it doesn't match what you hold, treat it as suspect and tell them so. I won't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, just to say it once more, no more calls to this number, and if anything does arrive in the post that doesn't match what you hold, treat it as suspect, treat it as suspect and tell [COMPANY_A]. Nothing needed from you today, nothing at all. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, right. Just one thing, and then I really am going. Earlier you said the landline log showed the attempts, and then you said nothing needed from me today. But you opened by saying you needed to confirm a few details before you could discuss the change. So which is it? Either you needed something from me, or you didn't. Anyway, I'm ringing the number on my statement, not this one. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Both, uh, in sequence. I needed those confirmations before I could discuss the change, and that's why I rang. But you've declined, which is your right, so nothing's needed from you today. The query stays open on our side, and it's for [COMPANY_A] to pursue through the proper channels, not for you to chase. That's all I meant. Ring the number on your statement, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, uh, right. That's... I'll leave it there. Statement number, as I said. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Okay, great. So my name is [PERSON_2], I'm a claims assessor with [COMPANY_A], we're the, um, vehicle warranty provider, and I'm calling because I'm looking at your file here, hang on, let me just scroll down -- yes, so the warranty on your vehicle is showing as about to lapse, and what I need to do today is get the renewal confirmed so there's no gap in your coverage, because once it goes past the date it, uh, it gets a lot more complicated to reinstate. I don't want you caught out if something goes wrong with the car and there's nothing there to cover it, so I just wanted to walk you through the process real quick, if you've got a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, that's me, sorry, bit of background noise, I'm out in the garden with you on speaker, hope that's alright. Um, so, a warranty? On my car? Hang on, let me, uh, let me just put the trowel down. I mean, I do have a car, a little thing, I've had it a few years, but I honestly can't remember if I ever, um, signed up for anything like that, I thought that came with it when I bought it, or maybe it ran out ages ago, I don't know. Sorry, say the name of the company again? I didn't quite catch it over the, the birds and everything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [COMPANY_A], yeah, vehicle warranty, and honestly the original one, uh, that would've run out, which is exactly why I'm -- no, sorry, what I mean is it's the extended cover, that's the one that's lapsing, and it's showing here that it's, hang on, let me scroll, it's due today, so what I need is just a quick confirmation from you, nothing complicated, and then it's all sorted and you don't have to think about it again. And look, with the, uh, the way the renewal rate's set up right now it's actually a lot lower than what you'd get if you start a brand new policy, so you really don't want to let it drop.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, due today, that's, hang on, that sounds a bit, I mean, I don't want to, um -- sorry, let me start again. I'm just trying to think if I ever actually took out extended cover, because I really don't remember doing that, and I'm usually quite good with, you know, paperwork and things. And you said you went wrong a second ago, the original one running out, and then it was the extended one, so which is it? I'm not being funny, I'm just, uh, a bit confused. How would I even check that this is, like, on my records? Is there a policy number or something I could look up?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, so, uh, it's the extended one, I just, I misspoke, it's, hang on -- sorry, the screen's, it's showing the original warranty as the one that's expiring, so, um, it's whichever one's, I mean they sort of, they link together on the system. Look, I can't really give out the policy number on an unsecured line like this, it's, that's just process, but if you can confirm a couple of details for me I can pull it all up and then we can see exactly where you stand. And I do need to get this finalised today, because once it rolls over to tomorrow I won't be able to hold that renewal rate.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, can I just, hang on, because I'm getting a bit lost here. First it was the extended one, now it's the original one, and you can't give me the policy number, but you want me to give you details? That seems, um, backwards, doesn't it? Wouldn't you already have my details if I'm on your file? I mean, I'm not trying to be difficult, I'm just, I'd feel better looking at my own paperwork first. Is there a number I could ring you back on, or a proper website I could look you up on?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, a, a proper website? Uh, no, I wouldn't, I mean we don't really do the, the online side for renewals, that's not how it, hang on. Oh, and the number, right, so that's, the line I'm on is an internal one, it doesn't take incoming, so I can't give you that, but I can have someone call you back, probably later on, I'd have to check when. Honestly though, if we leave it till then I can't promise the renewal rate will still be there, so it really would be easiest if we just got it confirmed now, while you've got me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, but, hang on, I said I'd like to look at my own paperwork first, and I'd like a number to ring you back on, that's all I'm asking. A number. Because you've said it's the extended one and then the original one, and no website, and no number, and it all has to be done right now, and honestly that's making me, um, a bit uneasy. I'm sure you're perfectly nice, I just don't give out my details to someone who rings me out of the blue, I'd feel daft doing it. So I'm going to go and dig out my papers, and if there really is something that lapses today, well, I'll sort it myself with whoever I actually bought the car from. Alright? Thanks for ringing, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, wait, please, don't hang up, I, uh, I really don't want you to lose this. If you go off and dig out your papers, that's, that could take a while, and then it lapses today and there's nothing I can do. I'd have to, hang on, I'd have to check if someone can even reopen it. And the dealer you bought it from, they won't have this, this is a separate cover, so it won't be in whatever they gave you. Can we just, if you can confirm those couple of details, it's honestly two minutes, and then, and then you've got your papers and everything can be, um, cross-checked afterwards.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, but no. You've just told me it's separate cover that I wouldn't have any papers for, and a minute ago you wanted me to go and check my papers. And you keep saying it'll lapse today, but you can't give me a number or a website or anything. That's not right, is it? If it was a proper thing I'd be able to check it properly. So I'm not giving you any details, I'm going back to my tomatoes, and if it lapses, it lapses. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, one second, before you go, you said two turns back that I told you to check your papers, and I didn't, I mean I didn't say that, I said you could cross-check them afterwards, that's, that's a different thing. And the dealer bit, I only meant it's not on their, hang on, let me just, can you hold on one moment while I check something? Please? Because I really don't want this to lapse on you, and if you just give me the details, I can still get that renewal rate locked in today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm going to stop you there, because you've changed it again, and no, I'm not holding on, I'm not giving you any details, and I'd really like you to stop now. I've said goodbye twice and I'm a bit cross that I'm still here. Don't ring this number again, please. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you're cross because it's, uh, crossed over? No, the renewal hasn't crossed over yet, it's still showing open on my side, so you've got a little bit of time, I just need you to stay on the line while I, hang on, while I pull the, the file back up. It's only a couple of details and then I can lock that rate in for you, I really don't want to, um --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, no, I said cross, as in annoyed, not crossed over, and honestly that's the last thing I'm going to say about it. Well, uh, hang on, I'm not staying on while you pull anything up, there's nothing for you to pull up, I haven't given you a thing. Right. I'm putting the phone down now, and please don't ring again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, yeah, no, I hear you. I'll, uh, I'll note it on the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, there's a blackbird right in the middle of my lettuces, shoo, go on, get out of it. Sorry, where was I. Right, yes, thank you for noting it, and no more calls please, I'll sort out my own car things. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Oh good, hi [PERSON_1], this is [PERSON_2] calling from the billing office at [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the support technicians over on the accounts side. So, uh, I won't keep you long, it's honestly just a quick thing, but I'm looking at an unpaid medical bill here, an outstanding balance of [AMOUNT_1], and it's showing you as the person responsible for it on behalf of a relative. I know, I know, that probably came out of nowhere, but it's really a two-minute fix if we just get a couple of details squared away on your end, and then we can close it out today and nobody has to deal with it any further.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who -- hang on, I just woke up, I was having a bit of a nap. A medical bill? For who, I mean, I've got a few relatives, my sister's in [CITY_1] and, uh, there's my cousin who's had a bad -- no wait, what company did you say you were with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No worries at all, [PERSON_1], sorry to catch you mid-nap, that's on me. So it's [COMPANY_A], the hospital billing office, I'm [PERSON_2], and I'm over on the accounts side, uh, well, it's more the collections side really, but same office, same thing. As for which relative, I can't actually say that just yet, it's only shared once I've confirmed it's really you I'm speaking with, so if I could just grab your date of birth and the address you've got on file, we'll have that sorted in a minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, okay, but see, that's the part that's bothering me a bit, because you're ringing me, right? I didn't ring you. And now you want me to tell you my birthday and my address before you'll even tell me which relative it's about, and that feels sort of backwards to me. I mean, I don't know, my daughter always says never give anything out if someone phones you, but then she also says I'm too suspicious about the post, so I'm not sure what to think. And you went from accounts to collections in about ten seconds there, which, uh, is it accounts or is it collections? Because those are different things, aren't they? Look, why don't you just give me a number for the hospital, a proper one I can find myself, and I'll call back and ask them about it. That seems the simplest thing, doesn't it? I've got a pen somewhere, it's, uh, probably in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, yeah, everybody asks that, [PERSON_1], it's totally normal. Accounts, collections, same desk, honestly. Look, it's just your date of birth and the address, takes ten seconds, and then I can tell you everything.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, see, you didn't actually answer me, you just said it's the same desk and asked for my birthday again. And I asked for a number, a proper one I can look up myself, and you stepped right over that. Now, I'm tired, I only just woke up, but I'm not that tired. If it's a real bill, the hospital will still be there tomorrow, and I'll ring them on the number off a letter or their website, not one you read me. So no, I'm not giving you my birthday or my address on a call I didn't ask for. Thanks anyway, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, [PERSON_1], hang on, hang on, there's really no need to make a whole thing of it, it's two minutes, and honestly if this sits it just gets passed along to the next stage, and that's the part nobody wants. I'm only trying to save you the hassle here. Could I at least, uh, -- no, okay, you know what, it's your call. But I'd really think about it, because it won't just go away on its own.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, you're not -- look, "the next stage," that's just you leaning on me again, isn't it? Real people don't, I mean, if it's real, I'll deal with it the proper way, in writing, with a letter. I'm done. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], listen, I'm not leaning on you, I'm really not, it's only a couple of details, your date of birth and the address, that's all it is. It's quick, it's two minutes, and then it's done and dusted. You don't need a letter for that, [PERSON_1], honestly, it's just, uh, the birthday and the address and we can wrap this up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not doing it, and you've just done it again. A minute ago you said you couldn't tell me the relative until I'd said who I was, and now it's just a quick birthday and address, like it's nothing. Earlier it was a two-minute fix, now it's two minutes again but you've gone from accounts to collections to, I don't know what. Anyway, I said goodbye and you're still talking. I'll sort it out through the post, like I said. Goodbye, [PERSON_2].

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], I hear you, I do, but it's just the birthday and the address, that's really all I need. It's quick, honestly, it's two minutes, and then it's all done and you don't have to think about it again. I just don't want this to, uh, to land on you in a way you don't expect, so if we could just do the birthday and the address, [PERSON_1], that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: That's the fourth time you've asked me for the same two things, and you still haven't given me a number I can ring back, which is all I wanted. A person who actually works at a hospital would've just said, here's the number, off you go. So that's me finished. I'm not giving you anything, I'll deal with it by post if it's real, and I'd rather you stopped ringing me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, this is [PERSON_1], calling from [COMPANY_A], the public library. Is this [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, hang on, I've got people around me. The public library, did you say? And, um, who was it you wanted again? Because I didn't quite catch the name, [PERSON_1], was it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, [PERSON_1], and I'm with [COMPANY_A], the public library, so, uh, nothing alarming, I promise. I'm calling for [PERSON_2], if I've got the right number, and it's really just a courtesy call, the sort we make when a reserved item comes in. Take your time, though, I'm in no hurry, and if now isn't convenient, we could always, well, try again later, though it's probably worth getting to sooner rather than, uh, leaving it too long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A reserved item, right. Uh, yeah, I might be [PERSON_2], I just, I don't remember reserving anything. What is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's a fair thing to ask, and honestly I'd rather you ask than just take my word for it. Sorry, one moment, someone's just come to the desk -- right, I'm back. So, the item is a book, placed on hold under your name about a week ago, and I don't have the title in front of me at the moment, but it'll be on the reservation slip when you come in. It's been set aside at the front desk, and it'll stay there for ten days, though, uh, it's always nicer not to leave these things to the last minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you don't have the title in front of you? That's, uh, kind of odd, isn't it, if you're calling about the book? Sorry, I'm just, I'm trying to think if I even put one on hold. A week ago, you said, set aside at the front desk?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, it's a good point, and I'm glad you raised it, because it does sound a bit odd, and I'd sooner you felt comfortable than just went along with me. Uh, you asked me to say again about the front desk, and yes, a week ago is when the hold was placed, and the book is being kept at the front desk here at the library, under your name. The reason I haven't got the title in front of me is simply that I'm ringing from the back office, not the desk itself, but I can have a colleague check the slip, or, well, you could just call the library's main line, [PHONE_1], and ask for the holds shelf, whichever you'd find easier.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, I'll just call the main line myself, then. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, please do, that's, uh, that's exactly what I'd -- sorry, go on. No, that's the right thing to do, [PERSON_2], ring [PHONE_1], ask for the holds shelf, and they'll confirm it for you. There's no charge and nothing you need to prepare, you can just pick it up whenever suits. Thanks for being so careful, and have a good day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, thanks. Uh, just before I go, you said something earlier about it being worth getting to sooner rather than leaving it too long. Then you said ten days. So is there a deadline, or what? Because that sounded a bit like a push, no offence.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No offence taken at all, it's a fair thing to pick up on, and I should have been clearer. The deadline is the ten days, that's all, ten days from when it arrived, and after that the book goes back on the shelf for the next person. There's nothing beyond that, no fee, no form, nothing you have to do today.
