Like I said, it's only a hold, so, uh, if you'd rather not bother, that's perfectly fine too, it just goes back on the shelf. So, ten days, that's the whole of it, and ringing [PHONE_1] will confirm everything. Thanks for checking, [PERSON_2], and goodbye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, okay, so ten days, then back on the shelf, no fee, nothing to do today. Right. Well, um... I'll ring the main line and check, like I said. If there's nothing under my name, then, well, I'll just leave it. Okay, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is this -- yes, good, [PERSON_1], right? This is [PERSON_2], I'm the regional supervisor with the internal investigations unit at [COMPANY_A]. Sorry, let me -- I'll get to the reason quickly, because I'm calling about activity on your account, [ACCOUNT_REF], and it's not something I can go into with the branch staff aware of it, so I need you to keep this call between us for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh -- sorry, who? I just woke up, I was having a bit of a lie-down. Investigations... is that, what, is that the bank? Because I've got my account with, well, I'm not sure which one you said. And why can't the branch know? That's -- I don't know, that sounds a bit odd to me. Can you say who you are again, slowly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, [PERSON_2], regional supervisor, internal investigations unit, [COMPANY_A]. That's the bank your account sits with, [PERSON_1], I wouldn't be calling you otherwise. And the reason the branch can't know is the part I need you to follow, because it's why I'm ringing you directly. We believe someone on the inside is involved, so the fewer people who hear about this, the better, and that includes your family for now. Look, I understand you've just woken up, but this isn't a call I make lightly, and I'd rather not have to repeat myself on a line like this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I -- no, hang on. I mean, if it really is the bank, then why would you ring me and tell me not to tell anyone? That's -- I'd have thought, I don't know, you'd want me to go in and, no, that's not what I mean either. My daughter always says the bank never rings you out of the blue, and now you're saying not even her. How would I even know you are who you say you are? I haven't got anything in front of me, I've only just got up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], I'm not asking you to prove anything to me, I'm asking you to hear me out, and honestly it's a bit much to question my good faith when I'm trying to protect your money. Your daughter's right in general, the bank doesn't ring out of the blue, but this isn't a routine call, this is internal investigations, which is a different procedure entirely. And I didn't say don't tell anyone, I said keep it quiet from branch staff, that's the point, uh, family can be told once it's resolved. Now, the activity on [ACCOUNT_REF] is time sensitive, so can we just get through the verification step so I can show you I'm genuine?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Verification step? No, but, you're the one ringing me, so surely you're the one who should be showing me. I just don't see why I'd have to prove anything to you. And you did say my family too, you said that, I heard you say it. I mean, I'm not trying to be rude, I've only just woken up. But my daughter says the bank never rings out of the blue, so I think I'll just ring the branch myself, on the number I've got, and ask them. That's what I'd do. Yes, I think that's best, I'll ring them myself. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wait, [PERSON_1], hold on, please. If you ring the branch, you're ringing the very people I told you can't know about this. Whoever's involved could be sitting at that desk, and the moment you call, the whole investigation is compromised. I'd really ask you not to do that. And I'm a bit surprised, frankly. I've been straight with you from the start, and now I'm being treated like I'm the one with something to hide. Can you give me ten minutes before you do anything, so I can explain this properly?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry, I'm not giving anyone ten minutes who tells me not to ring my own bank. I'll ring them. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine, [PERSON_1], that's your decision. But I'll say this plainly, if anything happens on that account in the meantime, it won't be because I didn't try to warn you. I've got other people to get to today. You have the branch number, use it, and, uh, I'd just ask that you think about who you're telling when you do.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh... right. Hmm. Yes. Well, I'll be telling the bank, won't I, that's rather the point of ringing them. And I'm telling my daughter as well, thank you. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], wait, before you -- no, listen, telling your daughter is exactly what I asked you not to do, and if you -- look, I'm trying to help you here, and you're making this very difficult. Just give me two minutes, that's all I'm asking, two minutes before you ring anyone. Please.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, um... no. No, I don't think so. Every time I say I'll ring the bank you want me to wait a bit longer, and that's the bit that doesn't sit right with me. So I'll ring them, and I'll tell my daughter, and that's that. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], I'm asking you, please, don't hang up. Just two minutes, that's all, two minutes, and I'll explain the whole thing, and then you can ring whoever you like. I mean, I'm trying to protect you here, and I'd hate to see something go wrong on [ACCOUNT_REF] because we didn't, uh, get a chance to finish this. Two minutes, [PERSON_1]. Can you give me that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, there's the kettle going off, I'd put it on before I -- sorry. Where was I. No. No, I've said, haven't I? You keep asking for two minutes and then another two minutes, and that's just what makes me not want to give you any. I'm going to ring the branch, and I'll tell my daughter, and if there's a real problem they'll sort it out with me. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, hello. Sorry, is this, um, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? I'm calling on behalf of someone at [COMPANY_A], the records department, and I'm just, uh, I'm only trying to get a few things up to date on their end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who's asking? And which company, sorry, I didn't catch what it's actually about. I've got about two minutes, so what do you need?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, sorry. It's, uh, [COMPANY_A]. The records department. I'm just, I'm calling on behalf of someone there, I'm not, I'm only passing it along, really. It's about updating the records, that's all it is. Just, um, keeping them current. I only need to check one thing, and then I'll let you go. You're still at the same address, aren't you? It would mean a lot to them to have it right, I think they've been worried about it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, someone's waving at me through the glass, one sec. Right. No, I'm not confirming an address to someone who hasn't told me who they are. You've said records department twice and you still haven't given me a name or what this is about. Who's the someone, and what do they actually want?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I, look, I understand, I do, and I'm sorry, I'm not trying to, I mean, it's not like that at all. I'm not, I wasn't meaning to be, um, secretive or anything. It's just that I'm only the, the go-between here. The person I'm calling for, they asked me to, uh, to just make the call, because they said it would be easier coming from someone, well, from me, I suppose. And I didn't think to write down the whole, the whole explanation, which is, that's on me, that's my mistake. They did say, and I want to get this right, that it's about keeping the records straight, that nobody wants anything from you, it's only that there's been some, some mix-up, maybe, or there could be, and they'd feel awful if the address was wrong and, and things went to the wrong place. I mean, I'd feel awful too, honestly. So it's really just a yes or no, if you could, whether you're still at the same address. I'm not asking for anything else. That's, that's genuinely all of it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, no. You've said a lot there and I still haven't got a name. Go back a bit, you said you're calling on behalf of someone at the company, records department. Who? Give me a name, or a number I can ring them back on, because I'm not confirming anything to a go-between who can't tell me who he's going between.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I, uh, I don't have a, I mean, I'm not sure I'm able to give out a name, they didn't say I could, and a number, I just, I don't have one in front of me. I'm sorry. I really thought this would be, I didn't think it would be such a... You know, I'm only trying to help someone out here, and it's a bit hurtful, honestly, being treated like I'm up to something. I'm not. I just, I just wanted to check the one thing, that's all, and I feel awful that it's gone like this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, look, I'm not trying to hurt your feelings, but think about it from where I'm standing. A stranger rings me, says he's from a records department, can't name the person he's calling for, can't give a number, and the one thing he wants is for me to confirm where I live. That's about as textbook as it gets, and I'm not saying you're up to something, I'm saying I can't tell, and that's exactly why the answer's no. If it really is [COMPANY_A], they've got my details already, so they don't need me to confirm anything over the phone. They can write to me, or I can look up their main number myself and ring them, and I'll do that if I'm worried. But I'm not doing it through a call I didn't ask for, with someone who won't tell me who he is. So I'm going to stop here. Thanks, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please, I didn't, I wasn't -- okay. Okay, that's fair, I suppose. I'm sorry for, uh, for taking up your time. I'll just tell them I couldn't, that you'd rather, um, go through the main number. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you'll tell them I'd rather what, go through the main number? Yeah, no, that's fine, that's, uh, hang on, did you say you'd send something? Because I'm not having anything sent out either, just so we're clear. Anyway. If they've got a problem, they can write to me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't say I'd send anything, I never, I only meant I'd pass it along, that's, that's all, I'm not sending anything, I -- okay. Yes. Right. Sorry again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you'll what, you'll pass along my address? No. Absolutely not, don't pass anything along, you don't have it and you're not getting it. Look, I've got to go, I'm late. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Uh, sorry, it's been a long day, just checking I've got the right number.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, that depends. Who's -- sorry, who's asking? I mean, you've got the number, you tell me who you were trying to reach and, uh, who you are.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, fair enough, that's, no, that's fair, I should've said. It's, uh -- I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the tax office, customer care side of things. And I've got [PERSON_1] down on my screen, so I'm hoping I've got the right household. How's your day going, by the way? Mine's been, well, you know how Thursdays are.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the, what was that, the text office? Like, a text message thing? I haven't, uh, I haven't sent anything to anyone. And my day's fine, it's just a day. But you still haven't said what this is actually about.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no no, the tax office, [COMPANY_A], not text, I mumble when I've been on the phones all day, sorry about that. And nothing to worry about, honestly, this is a nice one for a change. It's just a, uh, a small matter with your file, and I'll get to it in a second, I just like to make sure I'm speaking to the right person first. Is this [PERSON_1], and is it all right if I confirm your date of birth while we're at it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, the tax office, got it, thanks. Look, I'm not trying to be difficult, it's just you've now asked me twice to confirm who I am and you still haven't told me one thing about why you rang. And I'm not going to read out a date of birth to someone who rang me out of the blue, that's, I mean, that's backwards, isn't it? You called me. If you've got me on a screen, you've got whatever's on file. So how about you tell me what the matter is, and, uh, what your name is, and which office you're actually calling from, and then we'll see. Because "nice one for a change" from the tax office, that's a, that's a new one on me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair point, you're quite right, and honestly I wouldn't want you handing over anything either, so forget the date of birth, that can wait. It's good news, [PERSON_1], that's all I meant. Our records show a refund owing to you, [AMOUNT_1] for the, uh, the twenty-twenty-one tax year, I think, hang on, let me just scroll back to that. And I'm [PERSON_2], customer care, so that's name and office sorted. Now, you said earlier you'd not sent anything to anyone, which, I'm sorry, I didn't quite follow, was that about the text thing, or did you mean something else?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that, that was just me mishearing you. I thought you said text office, so I said I hadn't sent anything. Nothing more to it. But, uh, going back a bit, you said your name and office were sorted, and I've got a name, sure, but you still haven't said which office. And the refund, you said twenty-twenty-one, then "I think, hang on, let me scroll back." Which is it? Because if it's my file on your screen, I'd have thought the year's the first thing you'd see.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, you've caught me out, I'm half on two screens here, it's a mess. Right, so, it's twenty-twenty, sorry, not twenty-twenty-one, and the amount's [AMOUNT_2], I had the wrong line before. And the office is, uh, it's just national, [PERSON_1], we're one big team, so there's no, you know, no local branch to name. Anyway, all I need to get this released is a couple of details to confirm it's you, and then it's done, nice and quick.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so that's the second year and the second amount now. Twenty-twenty-one, then twenty-twenty, [AMOUNT_1], then [AMOUNT_2]. And "one big team, no office to name", that's, I mean, that's not an answer. I'm going to say it again, plainly. I'm not giving you details to release a refund. If the tax office owes me money, it can write to me, or I'll go and log in myself, on my own, the way I always would. So what's the actual reference for this refund? Because if it's on your screen, you can read me that. You can read it out to me, and I'll check it against my own account.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, the reference, yes, of course, no problem at all, it's, uh -- [ACCOUNT_REF], and that's the one on this screen, though, hang on, there might be a second one on the older file, they sometimes issue a new one when it gets reassigned between teams, so if yours looks different on your side, that'd be why, it's very common, honestly. And look, I really don't want you thinking I'm trying to catch you out, I do about forty of these a day and most people are just pleased, you'd be amazed, I had a lady yesterday who nearly cried, because she'd forgotten she was even owed it. The only thing is, and I'm not rushing you, but these refunds do sit in a release queue, so if we don't confirm it today, it can go back to the pool and you'd be waiting months, which would be a shame when we're so close. So if you just want to pop your date of birth across, and then, uh, whichever account you'd like it paid into, I can have it sorted before I log off.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so now there might be two references, and one of them's the wrong one if mine looks different. That's convenient. And "today or it goes back to the pool", yeah, I've heard that one. Real refunds don't expire in an afternoon. I'm not giving you a date of birth or an account, not on a call I didn't ask for, with a man who won't say which office he's in. If it's real, it'll still be there when I log in myself. So that's me done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, [PERSON_1], come on, don't be like that, I'm only trying to do you a favour here! Nobody's asking for anything strange, it's a date of birth, honestly, and half the people I ring say exactly what you're saying and then ring back next week when it's too late. Look, forget the account for a second, just give me the date of birth and I'll hold the refund for you till tomorrow, how's that, that's me sticking my neck out. And you did say you were having a perfectly nice day, so why spoil it, eh?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Now it's a hold till tomorrow, so the deadline moved while we were talking. I'm not giving you a date of birth, not today, not tomorrow. If there's a refund, I'll find it myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no no, wait, [PERSON_1], hang on, you're not listening, I'm trying to help you here and you're just, honestly it's one little detail, the date of birth, that's all, and then I'll -- no, listen, don't hang up on a refund, you'll regret --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I did listen. That's why I'm hanging up. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? [PERSON_1]? Hello -- no, don't, it's just a date of birth, it's only a --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Still no. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Uh, my name is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the events venue, in the capacity of a verification and reservations specialist, and I'm reaching out regarding a provisional private-dining booking that's been lodged under your colleague [PERSON_3]'s retirement celebration.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who's [PERSON_3]? I mean, I might know the name, but, uh, hang on. Say that again, you're calling from where exactly? And what's it got to do with me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, apologies, I've gone at that rather fast. So, [COMPANY_A], that's the events venue, and yes, I did say provisional, uh, not provincial, and the booking is a private surprise dinner, so the vetting on the guest manifest is what I'm ringing about, specifically the, the attendee reconciliation. Your name came up as a colleague of [PERSON_3], who's retiring, and the organiser would like you on the guest list, but, I mean, the one stipulation is that [PERSON_3] themselves isn't to hear about it, it being a surprise.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, I don't -- hang on, sorry, the kids are being loud. Right. So somebody put my name down, but I haven't, I mean, nobody's actually said anything to me about a dinner. Who's the organiser? And why are you the one ringing me instead of them?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: So, uh, so, yes, quite, that's a fair question and, um, it's entirely understandable that nobody's mentioned it, because, I mean, the organiser deliberately hasn't circulated anything yet. The organiser is [PERSON_1]'s, sorry, no, that's you, forgive me, the organiser is a colleague of yours named [PERSON_2], and the reason it falls to us is that the venue does its own confirmation of attendee details before the provisional hold converts to a firm reservation, it's a, a sort of reconciliation protocol on our end. But look, I'm not asking you for anything today, no payment, no personal details, I'd simply like you to know it's coming and to keep it from [PERSON_3].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, wait, you said the organiser's named [PERSON_2]? That's, that's your name. You just said that was you. So which is it? And you said a second ago you're not asking for anything, but then why ring me at all if it's a surprise and nobody's told me? I mean --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, that was my slip. I've used the same placeholder for the two of us, which is careless. I'm [PERSON_2], the venue's verification specialist. The organiser is a different colleague of yours, and I'd rather not name them down the phone to someone I've only just reached, because I can't prove who I am yet. That's the honest answer to your question. And I'm ringing because the venue likes the guests to hear it from us at least once, so nobody's caught off guard by a guest list they didn't know about. But, I mean, none of that should be taken on trust. You've never heard of me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on -- no, put that down, we don't eat that. Sorry. Uh, right. So you can't tell me who the organiser is, and you can't prove who you are. That's, I mean, that's not a lot to go on, is it? If it's a real dinner, why wouldn't the organiser just ask me themselves?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, it isn't. Look it up yourself, [COMPANY_A], find the number on your own, and ask for the events desk about the booking.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, uh, hang on, can I go back a bit? Earlier you said the venue confirms attendee details before the hold turns into a firm booking. What details, exactly? Because you also said you weren't asking me for anything, and those two things sort of don't sit together. And, I mean, if I ring the events desk myself, what do I even tell them? That someone rang me about a dinner I wasn't told about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that, uh, that doesn't sit together, you're right, and I put it badly. The, the reconciliation is really just us checking the guest list against what the organiser submitted, I mean, it's our side of the paperwork, not something you'd have to give me anything for. So, no details from you, not today, not on this call. And what you'd tell the events desk is, um, exactly what you said, that someone rang saying they were from [COMPANY_A] about a private dinner booking, and could they confirm whether a provisional hold exists. They'd, sorry, they may not tell you the organiser's name, which is a, a privacy matter on their end, but they can tell you whether the booking is real, and that's what matters here, isn't it? The only thing I'd ask is that if it does turn out to be real, you keep it from [PERSON_3]. That's the whole of it. Ring them on a number you find yourself, [PHONE_1] is the one I'd have given you, but ignore that, use your own.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but you just said -- no, sorry, I'm going to stop you there. So you rang me, you can't tell me who the organiser is, you can't prove who you are, and you're telling me to go and check you out myself? Fine. I'll do that, if I do anything. But I'm not confirming a thing on this call, and I'm not promising to keep anything from anybody. Okay? Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, I mean, that's completely fair, and you shouldn't confirm anything to a caller you can't verify. Please do ring them yourself, on a number you've looked up, [COMPANY_A], the events desk, and, well, if they say there's no such booking then I'd, uh, I'd rather you hear that from them than from me. And there's no promise needed, not from you, not today. Right then. Sorry for the, the muddle, and, um, thank you for your time. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. No, hang on, I said bye already. Sorry, [PERSON_1], put the -- no, give it here. Right. I'm done with this, okay? If there's a dinner, someone I actually know can tell me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood. If it's real, someone you know will tell you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one thing before you go. A couple of turns back you said the venue likes guests to hear it from them at least once. Why? I mean, why would a venue ring a guest at all, before the organiser's even said anything? That bit still doesn't make sense to me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair, and honestly it doesn't hold up well. You have a good afternoon, and, uh, good luck with the tomatoes and the blackbird. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thanks, yeah, and you have a lovely afternoon too. Sorry, what was that last bit, the process going... inactive and then it's recorded as unconfirmed? Oh no, did you say it's going to be recorded as unemployed? Because I'm not, I've got a job, I'm only gardening because it's my afternoon off, ha. Oh, unconfirmed. Right. Well, that's fine then, I'll ring the main line like I said. Cheers, bye now, mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], security operations at [COMPANY_A] -- yes, the charity, you've given to us before, I'm calling about your monthly gift, it's -- no, hang on, let me finish, it lapsed a few months back and I need to confirm a couple of things on the record.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, what? Hang on, I've got a pan on, just -- hold on a sec. Um, the charity? Which, uh, which charity was that again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, take your time, I'll wait. It's [COMPANY_A] -- the charity, [COMPANY_A], you've supported us with a monthly gift for, I want to say a couple of years, and I know "security operations" sounds a bit alarming for what is really a thank-you call, that's just the department I work in, we look after donor records and making sure they're accurate. The long and short of it is your monthly donation of [AMOUNT_1] stopped coming through a few months ago, and before anything gets archived I'd rather hear from you directly than have your record just sit there marked as lapsed, because that's, well, that's not how we like to treat people who've been as loyal as you have. Anyway, go and see to your pan, I'm not going anywhere, and when you're back I'd like to ask whether you'd consider renewing it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, sorry, I'm back, I turned it down. Um, but I didn't think I'd stopped it? I mean, I thought I'd cancelled it ages ago, like a year, maybe longer. And you said a couple of years, so, uh, which is it? Sorry, I'm a bit lost.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's -- you're right, I did say a couple of years, and that was loose of me. Let me be exact: the gift ran for about two years, and then it stopped, and I'm not sure when you cancelled it, because the note on my screen only says lapsed, not cancelled. So if you cancelled it yourself a year ago, then that's what happened, and I'll take your word over my screen. All I'm really asking is whether you'd think about starting it up again, even at a smaller amount than [AMOUNT_1], but there's no obligation, and I'd much prefer you tell me no than feel pushed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Uh, no, I don't think so. Not right now, sorry. I've got dinner on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood. That's a no, and I'll record it as a no. I won't ask you again on this call, and I'm not going to try to talk you round. I do apologise for catching you in the middle of cooking, that's the trouble with calling in the evening, people are always halfway through something, and I'd rather you got back to your dinner than stood there listening to me. Now, if you'd like, I can take you off our calling list altogether, so you wouldn't hear from us again by phone. Or, if it's only the timing that's wrong, I can note that you'd prefer a call at a different time of day, and someone could ring you then instead. Whichever you'd rather, it's entirely up to you, and it makes no difference to how your past gifts are recorded. Those are thanked and filed either way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's -- okay, that's kind of you. Um, I think, I mean, could you just -- no, sorry. Take me off the list, I think. Yes. Take me off, please. And, uh, thanks for not -- well, thanks. Right, I'd better get back to the pan. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, yes, of course, that's done, I'll flag your number as do-not-call on the system as we speak, so you shouldn't hear from us by phone again. Sorry again for the interruption, and thank you for what you gave over the years, it genuinely did get used. Go on, go and rescue your dinner. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, thanks, uh, bye now. Sorry, the pan's, yeah. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, this is [PERSON_1], I'm the regional supervisor over at [COMPANY_A]. Uh, I'm calling about a repeat prescription that's been made up for collection. Now, I did try this number earlier, so, sorry, I should say, was that you who picked up around lunchtime, or someone else in the household?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, no, I didn't pick up at lunchtime. And I haven't got a repeat prescription with anyone, as far as I know. Who'd you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so I'm with [COMPANY_A], the pharmacy, I'm the regional -- well, I supervise the branches across [CITY_1]. And the, uh, the order is sitting here under your name, it's, no, let me, it's flagged as a repeat, so it's been auto-generated off the back of your last one. Look, I mean, if you haven't got a repeat set up, that's fine, but it's a bit odd to be questioning me on it when it's right here on the system.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Not questioning, just asking. Which branch is it at, and what's the medication?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, it's the, uh -- sorry, one second, [PERSON_2], can you leave that on the counter, thanks -- sorry, hello, yeah. It's our [CITY_1] branch. And for the medication, honestly, I'm not going to read that out over the phone, that's just standard procedure, we only go through the item list in person when you come in with some ID. I mean, that's how it's done at every one of our branches.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but, uh, you rang me. You've got my name, you've got a prescription, and you won't say what it is. So I'll ask again, which branch? Like the actual street, or the shop name, something I can look up. Because I haven't got a repeat set up with anyone.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, look, I'm not trying to be difficult here, but I've now explained twice that I can't go through the item list over the phone, and that's not me being evasive, that's just procedure. The branch is the main [COMPANY_A] on the high street in [CITY_1], it's listed under that name, and the number for it is [PHONE_1], so you can ring them directly and ask for the prescriptions desk. I mean, honestly, if you want to check it, check it, that's absolutely fine. I'd just rather not have this turn into me being treated like I'm up to something, because I'm only the one passing the message on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'm not going to ring a number you've just read me, that rather defeats the point. If there's genuinely something waiting, I'll look up the pharmacy myself and ask them. And if there isn't, well, no harm done. Anyway, I'll leave it there. Cheers.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, well, that's up to you, I suppose. I'd have thought ringing the branch would be the sensible thing, but, uh, no, fair enough, look it up yourself, that's perfectly reasonable. If there's nothing under your name when you ask, it'll just be a mix-up on our end and I'll sort it, so no harm done, like you say. Right, thanks for your time, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Uh, yes, hi, this is [PERSON_2] calling from the scheduling office at [COMPANY_A], and I'm just, I'm calling because your account's been flagged for a disconnection and the crew's actually set to cut the power at your address within the hour, so I wanted to reach you before that happens, okay?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, this is -- yes, speaking. Sorry, did you say the power's going to be, uh, cut off? Within the hour? I mean, I thought I was, well, I don't think I've -- sorry, I'm not very good with this sort of thing, could you just explain again what's happened with my account?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, so it's an outstanding balance on the account, [AMOUNT_1], it's past the final notice date, and once the crew's dispatched I can't pull them back, so we really need to get this settled in the next, uh, forty minutes or so. I'm showing the account under [ACCOUNT_REF], and what I can do right now is take care of it over the phone so the disconnection gets cancelled, so if you could just -- sorry, can I get you to confirm the name on the account for me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, um, the name. Sorry, hang on -- you've got the name there already, haven't you? I just, I don't remember getting a final notice, is all.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, so the notices went out by mail, the last one about, uh, two weeks ago, and it's on the account that it was, well, actually the final one was a phone message, not mail, so that's probably why you haven't got anything in the post. But the thing is, the crew's already scheduled, and I've only got about, what, thirty-five minutes now to get this settled, so if you could just confirm the name on the account and we'll get this cancelled.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, a phone message, well, I did have a few come through the other week, but I'm afraid I didn't always listen to them all the way, I'm so sorry, I'm not very good with the answering machine thing, my nephew set it up and I never quite got the hang of it. And you said the notices went out by mail first, and then it was a phone message, and now it's a phone message only, and I'm sorry, I'm a bit muddled about which it was. I mean, I'd hate for the power to go off, I really would, I've got the heating and the fridge and everything. But, um, I'm just wondering, and please don't take this the wrong way, how would I know it's really [COMPANY_A] I'm speaking to? Because you haven't actually said the name on the account yet, you keep asking me for it, and I thought, well, if you're from the office you'd have it in front of you. Is there a number I could ring back on, maybe? Or, I don't know, would it be better if I looked at the bill first?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, a bill, no, no need for the bill, the bill won't show this, it's a, uh, it's a scheduling matter, it's separate from the billing side. And I mean, ringing back isn't really an option, the line you'd get would be the main switchboard and they can't see the dispatch queue, so by the time you're through the crew's already out the door, and that's the thing, we've got about thirty minutes now, so if we could just get this cancelled, I only need you to confirm the name on the account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, I'm just trying to keep it straight in my head. You said thirty-five minutes a moment ago, and now it's thirty, which, well, that's fair, time goes on, I suppose. But earlier you said you could take care of it over the phone, and now you're only wanting the name, so I'm a bit lost on what happens after I say it. And I'm sorry, I really don't mean to be difficult, but it seems odd that I can't just look at my own bill, or ring the number on it. Wouldn't the electric people want me to do that? I'd feel a lot better about it, honestly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so what happens after is, uh, I just, no, sorry, the way it works is, well, once you've confirmed the name we move straight on to, to settling it, and that's, that's the part I'd walk you through, but look, the crew's -- we really are down to about twenty-five minutes now, so if you could just confirm the name on the account and then we'll...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, there's someone at the gate, I think it's the post, yes, the postman, hold on just a second. No, he's gone past, never mind, sorry about that. Now, where were we? You said once I say the name you walk me through settling it, but you haven't said how, and, well, it's gone from thirty-five to twenty-five minutes and I'm still not sure what it is I'm meant to be doing. I think I'd feel better if I just got the bill out and rang the number on it, honestly. Is that all right? I'm sorry to be a nuisance.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, look, the bill number won't, that goes to a different, uh, it won't connect you to dispatch, so there's no point in -- sorry, I've got another account coming up here that I need to, I'm going to have to leave it with you. Okay, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, well, um, goodbye then. I'm sorry I wasn't more help. I'll just find the bill and ring the number on it, and if there's anything owing they can tell me. Thank you for calling.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, okay, but I'd, uh, I'd hold off on that, because the crew's actually not due out until the end of the day anyway, so, so there's no real rush on your end. Right, I've really got to go, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, before you go, just one thing. Two turns back you said the number on my bill wouldn't connect me to dispatch, and now you're saying the crew isn't due until the end of the day. I'm a bit muddled. Was it the forty minutes, or the end of the day? And why would you tell me to hold off ringing the number on the bill? I'm sorry, I just don't follow. Hello? Oh, he's gone. Well, I'll ring the number on the bill anyway, I think. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, um, good afternoon, I'm so sorry to trouble you. Is this -- no, sorry, let me start again. I'm calling from the records department at [COMPANY_A], and I'm just updating a few files today. Are you still there? Good, thank you, I only need a moment of your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I'm -- sorry, hang on a sec, [clearing throat] I'm still here. Records department, did you say? Records for, I mean, which -- who exactly is this you're trying to reach?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, yes, that was unclear of me. It's the records department at [COMPANY_A], and I'm just working through the files that are due for an update, so it's really only a routine check. I don't want to take up your time, I only need to confirm one small thing, that you're still living at the address we have on file. Is that all right? You're still there, yes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Which address, though? You haven't said whose file this is, or what [COMPANY_A] even, um, what I'd have to do with you. And you want me to confirm it, so you're not reading it out to me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm sorry, I know that's frustrating, and I should have explained better. It's just, I can't really read an address out over the phone, that's for your own protection, in case it's not actually you I've reached. So I only need you to confirm that you're still living at the address we have on file. That's all it is, a quick confirmation. You are still there, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but I still don't know whose file this is. You haven't said a name, you haven't said what [COMPANY_A] has to do with me. And if you can't tell me the address because it might not be me, then, I mean, how do I know it's not the other way round? How do I know it's you who's who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I -- no, you're right, that's, um, a fair thing to ask, and I'm sorry. Uh, it's just, I'm only a case handler, you see, I don't actually have the wider details in front of me, only the update list. And I'm only trying to make sure your details are kept safe, that's really the whole reason. So if you could just confirm you're still at the address, I can mark it done and let you get on. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so you're -- no, wait. You're keeping my details safe, but you don't have my details in front of you? That doesn't, I mean, how does that -- sorry, [muffled, away from phone] no, put that down, please. Sorry. Right. So, what's my name, then? On your list. Can you tell me that much?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I -- um, I can't read the name out either, I'm afraid. It's the same reason, it's only to protect you. Look, I can hear this is a bad moment, and I don't want to worry you. Are you still there? Maybe it's better if I leave it, and I'll note down that I wasn't able to complete the check today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Maybe leave it. If [COMPANY_A] actually needs something from me, they can write to me. Okay, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, I'm so sorry for the bother, truly. I'll, um, I'll just note it as not completed. Thank you for your patience, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, yes, goodbye, and thank you again, I really am sorry to have taken up your afternoon. I do hope I haven't worried you, because there's honestly nothing to be worried about, it's only the sort of thing that comes round every so often when files are due, and, well, I did wonder if I'd caught you at a bad moment, what with, um, the noise in the background. So I'll just mark it as not completed, like I said, and, uh, if anything does come through in the post, you needn't think twice about it. Are you still there? Sorry, silly of me, of course you've gone. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, I haven't gone. Two turns ago you said it's only to protect me, that you can't read the name out, and now you're saying it's nothing to worry about, so which is it? And what do you mean, if something comes in the post I needn't think twice? Why would anything come?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, I didn't mean -- sorry, I shouldn't have said that about the post, that was silly of me, forget I said it. It's only that -- no, really, there's nothing coming, I only meant -- I'm sorry, I've confused things, haven't I? It's nothing at all, honestly, and I won't keep you any longer. Thank you for your time, and I'm sorry again. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, wait, you can't just, I mean, you said it, so why did you say it? Why would anything come in the post? And you still haven't told me who you actually are or what this has to do with me. If there's something real, then they can write to me, properly, with a name on it. I'm not confirming anything over the phone. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, one second, someone's just -- no, that's fine. Yes, this is [PERSON_2] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the recruitment agency, and I'm following up on your application for the remote position. Good news is you've been shortlisted, but I do need to get you through onboarding before the end of today's window, so is now an okay moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Account services? I haven't applied for anything lately, and certainly not a remote job. I'm standing in a queue, so, uh, what exactly is this about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, I understand, and I won't take long. Your details came through on our system under the remote placement list, so you're already shortlisted, which is the part that matters. The only thing is the onboarding slot closes at five today, so I'd just need to confirm a couple of things and get you through that before it lapses. Is that [PERSON_1] I'm speaking with?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you still haven't answered me. I didn't apply for anything, so how am I on a list? And you've asked me twice now if I'm who I am, but you rang me. You tell me who you've got on that screen. What's the company again, and what's this slot closing at five, why's that my problem?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, I do hear you, but the name on my screen is [PERSON_1], and the company is [COMPANY_A], we're a recruitment agency, account services. And the list, it's, uh, it's populated from applications and referrals, so it's standard that someone might not recall -- look, the point is, you're shortlisted, and the onboarding slot does close at five today, that's just procedure. There's a small onboarding cost of [AMOUNT_1] to clear, and then you'd start straight away, so shall I take you through it before the window shuts?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, there it is. A cost. I'm shortlisted for a job I never applied for, and I've got to pay you before I start? No. Real employers don't charge you to work for them, I've been stung by that sort of thing before. I'm not paying anything, I'm not confirming anything, and I'm not going through any slot. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, no, please, before you go, I do understand the concern, and I'd just say that the onboarding cost isn't a fee to us, it's, uh, it's an administrative clearance, it's refunded within the first pay cycle, so it's really a deposit more than a charge. And it's standard across our remote placements, it's in the procedure, I can't change how the procedure is set up, I only administer it. The thing is, the slot does close at five today, and once it lapses the shortlist position goes to the next candidate, and I'd hate for that to happen, because the role is, I mean, it's well paid for what it is, it's fully remote, you set your own hours, and there's no interview stage, we've already done that part. So if I could just confirm you're [PERSON_1], and then I can take you through the clearance quickly, it's only a few minutes, and then you're set up and starting straight away, and, sorry, as I said, it does close at five, so I'd really prefer to get you done before then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Deposit, clearance, administrative whatever, you can call it what you like, it's still me paying money upfront for a job I never asked for. And no interview, well paid, set your own hours? That's the exact pitch I got last time. The next candidate can have it. I'm done, and I'm not confirming my name either. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Okay. Well, the slot does still close at five, so if you change your mind, the, uh, the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I won't be changing my mind. Keep your reference, I don't want it. And take me off whatever list you've got, because I never put myself on it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, yes, I'll, uh, I'll flag that, though I should say removal isn't something I can do from here, that goes through the, um, the applications team, so it might take a few days to drop off. And I'd only say -- look, you did apply, it's on the record under your referral, so it's not like we just, uh, picked you off a list. Anyway, the window does close at five, so, if you're sure.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I did not -- no, look, first you said it was a list, now it's a referral, now I've applied? Which is it? Because I -- no. I'm not doing this. Whatever's on your record, it's not from me, and I'm not going to stand here arguing it while you keep telling me about five o'clock. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Lovely, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A] -- I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, I know how these afternoons get, one thing after another, right? Now, I'm just, uh, wanting to make sure I've got the right person, because I think I spoke to someone at this number a few days ago and they said something about you being away, and I wasn't quite sure what they meant by that -- were you traveling, or was that, sort of, a different [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, who did you say you were calling from? And, um, you said someone told you I was, what, a stray? No, sorry, that can't be right -- I'm not sure I caught that word. Anyway, I haven't spoken to anyone about being away, so I'd like to know first who you are and what this is regarding.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no no, I said away, not stray, though I can see how that came out muddled, that's on me, I ramble when I'm on the phone. Okay, so the straight answer, it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], the shop that ran the prize draw at the [CITY_1] community fair, the weekend before last, and you filled in one of our little entry slips at our stall. I'm calling because your name came up in the draw, nothing big, it's a small prize, nothing to pay, and honestly the only thing I need from you is a time to pop by the shop and pick it up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. I don't remember filling in an entry slip. Which shop, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, fair enough, those slips go by fast, you drop one in the bowl while you're chatting and then forget all about it. It's [COMPANY_A], the shop on the high street in [CITY_1], and we had the little table by the entrance at the [CITY_1] community fair, that was Saturday the [DATE_1], with the big glass bowl and the tickets. If it helps, you can check us out yourself, look up our number, ring the shop directly, and ask for me, [PERSON_2], no hurry on that at all. And look, if you honestly don't remember entering, that's okay too, I'd rather you say so than feel pushed into anything, there's nothing to pay and nothing I need from you over the phone. Does the fair ring any bells at all, or were you maybe there with someone else who might've put your name down?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh... hm. Right. Let me think a moment. I mean, I may have been at the fair, I can't honestly say, but I don't recall a bowl or a slip. And a couple of things, if you don't mind. How did you get this number? Because if I filled in a slip, I'd want to know what I wrote on it. And what's the prize, specifically? You've said small, but not what it is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, good questions, and that's exactly what you should be asking. The slips had a name and a phone number on them, that's all, so the number came straight off the one you wrote, no lists, nothing bought in. As for the prize, it's a [AMOUNT_1] gift basket, a few bits from the shop, nothing fancy. Honestly I probably should've led with that instead of waffling about the weather, ha. And look, if the whole thing feels off, don't take my word for it. Ring the shop on the number you find yourself, ask for [PERSON_2], and they'll confirm the draw and the date. Or just ignore my call, there's no deadline that matters, the basket'll sit on a shelf either way. I'd hate for you to feel pushed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay. I'll say this plainly, because I'd rather be precise than polite. You haven't asked me for anything yet, and the offer to check independently is the correct thing to say, so I'll give you that. But I still can't place the slip, and I notice the story has shifted a little. You opened by asking whether I'd been away, as if you were confirming I was the right person, and now it's a draw where my name came out of a bowl. Those are two quite different reasons to ring. And if the number came off a slip I wrote, then you'd also have the name and, presumably, how I filled it in. So what name did you actually have on the slip? I'm not going to confirm anything to you, but I'd like to hear what you think you're holding. Otherwise, I'll do exactly what you suggest. I'll find the shop's number myself, ring them, and ask for you. And if that doesn't check out, well, that tells me what I need to know.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're right to poke at that, and honestly the first bit was me being clumsy. I wasn't really confirming you were the right person, I was, uh, just trying to ease in and made a hash of it. The only reason I ring is the draw. And I'll tell you what I'm holding, it's just the name [PERSON_1] and this number, no address, nothing else, that's all the slip asks for. Oh, and while I'm tidying up, I said the basket's a few bits from the shop, but now I think about it the voucher's [AMOUNT_1] and the basket's the extra, so it's one or the other, sorry, I'm mixing up my own notes. Either way, ring the shop, ask for me, and if it doesn't check out, bin the call and no harm done. And if you do feel like popping by, the basket or voucher or whatever it ends up being, it's only ever collected in person at the shop, nothing to pay, nothing to hand over.
